[4153] In December 2023, Australia, the U. K. and the U. S. held an AUKUS defense ministers’ meeting and confirmed the progress of support for Australia’s acquisition of nuclear-powered submarines and advanced technology cooperation

[4154] During the meeting, it was announced that: Australian Navy crew would begin operations in Guam in 2024 to acquire nuclear-powered submarine maintenance skills in support of the Submarine Rotational Force — West (SRF-West) that will be established off the west coast of Australia

[4155] The three countries will conduct joint experiments and exercises with uncrewed maritime systems and share and process maritime data in real time to improve their maritime domain awareness and all three countries will promote the technological development of quantum sensing to improve undersea positioning capabilities and to accelerate technological development of submarine-based undersea vehicle as part of efforts to further develop the SSN-AUKUS

[4156] In April 2024, an AUKUS defense ministers’ joint statement was issued, confirming cooperation in the acquisition of nuclear-powered submarines under AUKUS’s Pillar I, while announcing its consideration of cooperating with Japan under Pillar II, the area of advanced capabilities

[4157] Relations with Foreign Countries (1) Relationship with the United States

[4158] Australia and the United States have an alliance based on the ANZUS (Security Treaty among Australia, New Zealand and the United States of America) Treaty[3], a mutual defense treaty that underpins Australia’s security policy

[4159] In response to the spread of communism in East Asia and the descending British influence in the Asia-Pacific after World War II, Australia strengthened its alliance with the United States, mainly possessing U.S.-made high-performance land, sea and air equipment

[4160] Australia has dispatched its troops to U. S.-led wars and conflicts, such as the Vietnam War, the Gulf War and military operations in Afghanistan and Iraq

[4161] A trilateral security treaty among Australia, New Zealand and the United States, which went into effect in

[4162] Since 1986, the United States has suspended its obligation to defend New Zealand due to its adoption of a non-nuclear policy

[4163] The treaty is thus effective only between Australia and the United States and between Australia and New Zealand

[4164] Since 1985, the two countries have been regularly convening the foreign affairs and defense ministerial consultations or AUSMIN (Australia-United States Ministerial Consultations), to discuss major diplomatic and security issues

[4165] In July 2023, AUSMIN was held in Australia and in their joint statement, both countries noted that the U. S.-Australia alliance has never been stronger and committed to expanding collaboration between the two countries, as well as with regional partners and institutions, to ensure an Indo-Pacific that is open, stable, peaceful, prosperous and respectful of sovereignty

[4166] In November 2011, the United States and Australia announced the “Force Posture Initiative,” a framework for the rotational deployment of the U. S. forces to Australia as part of the U. S. rebalance policy during the Obama administration

[4167] Since 2012, the U. S. Marine Corps has been deployed on a rotational basis to northern Australia, including Darwin

[4168] Additionally, the U. S. Air Force has been deploying B-52 strategic bombers and F-22 fighter jets to Australia as needed to conduct joint exercises and training with the RAAF

[4169] In July 2023, the rotational deployment of the U. S. Army landing craft took place for the first time during the U. S.-Australia joint exercise “Talisman Sabre.”

[4170] The United States and Australia have also indicated their intention to deploy the U. S. Navy patrol and reconnaissance aircraft on a rotational basis in Australia in the future

[4171] Since 2005, the U. S. Forces and ADF have biennially conducted “Talisman Sabre” to improve interoperability and strengthen ties among participating countries

[4172] In 2023, it was the largest exercise ever, with 13 countries participating, with Indonesia, Fiji, Papua New Guinea and Tonga participating for the first time

[4173] The exercise was conducted in the land, maritime and air domains, including amphibious operations and land combat training

[4174] Relationship with China

[4175] China is Australia’s largest trading partner and two countries have conducted various exchanges in the defense area such as dialogues between the defense authorities, bilateral exercises, and mutual visiting of vessels, in addition to exchanges and cooperation in the political areas

[4176] Meanwhile, Australia has been clearly showing its wariness towards China by explicitly conveying its stance on China given the military use of South China Sea and its expansion to Pacific island countries

[4177] The Australian government has been expressing strong concerns over China’s reclamation and construction activities in South China Sea and opposing any unilateral attempt to change or influence the status quo through militarization or coercive actions on disputed features

[4178] It has also expressed its intent to continue exercising its rights to freedom of navigation and overflight

[4179] In April 2020, Australia had suggested the necessity for an independent investigation into the origin of novel coronavirus outbreak in China

[4180] China successively imposed trade blockages on Australian beef and other products, leading to a rapid deterioration of the Australia-China relations

[4181] Subsequently with the change of government in Australia, the two countries resumed diplomatic and security dialogue and the first Australia-China defense ministers’ meeting in about three years was held in June

[4182] In November 2023, Prime Minister Albanese visited China and met with President Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Li Qiang

[4183] This visit of Australian Prime Minister to China was the first time in seven years

[4184] On the other hand, according to the Australian government, in November 2023, there was an incident which had resulted in the injury of an Australian diver

[4185] When the diver on the Royal Australian Navy frigate, conducting monitoring and surveillance activities against North Korea’s illicit “ship-to-ship transfers”, was removing a fishing net entangled in the ship’s screw within Japan’s EEZ, sonar waves were emitted by a Chinese navy guided-missile destroyer sailing nearby and had injured the Australian diver

[4186] The Australian government expressed serious concerns to the Chinese government, describing the Chinese navy’s activity as dangerous and unprofessional, but the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs insisted the Chinese military had consistently conducted professional operations in accordance with international law and practice

[4187] Relations with Southeast Asia and Pacific Island Countries

[4188] In its 2020 Defence Strategic Update, Australia announced a policy of focusing on the Indo-Pacific region, particularly the adjacent areas from the north-eastern Indian Ocean, through maritime and mainland Southeast Asia to Papua New Guinea and the South West Pacific

[4189] Australia has been deepening its relations with Indonesia in the security and defense fields following the signing of the Lombok Treaty, a security cooperation framework, in November 2006 and the elevation of their relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in August

[4190] The bilateral relationship has been strengthened through initiatives such as the regular holding of Foreign and Defense Ministers Meetings (2+2) and the announcement in February 2024 that they are considering a treaty-level defense cooperation agreement

[4191] With Singapore and Malaysia, Australia carries out regular combined joint exercises in the South China Sea and other areas under the Five Power Defence Arrangements (FPDA; entered into force in 1971) framework, whereby the two countries, the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand would consult together in the event of any form of armed attack or threat of such attack against Singapore or Malaysia, for the purpose of deciding what measures should be taken

[4192] Australia considers that Singapore is its most advanced defense partner and that they share Australia’s interest in a secure maritime trading environment

[4193] Defense cooperation between the two countries is also deepening, including the signing of the Memorandum of Understanding on Military Training and Training Area Development in Australia under the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in October

[4194] Regarding Malaysia, Australia stations the ADF in Royal Malaysian Air Force Base Butterworth and contributes to maintaining regional security and stability through patrol activities in the South China Sea and the northern Indian Ocean

[4195] Australia has been strengthening its defense relationship with the Philippines, primarily through support for building counter-terrorism capabilities and at the Australia-Philippines defense ministers’ meeting in February 2023, it was concurred that this meeting would be held annually from the following year

[4196] Australia has been participating in the U.S.-Philippines joint exercise Balikatan since 2014 and in August 2023 it conducted its first Australian-Philippines amphibious exercise, Exercise Alon, which included scenario training for reclaiming enemy-captured island

[4197] Additionally, in November the same year, Australian and the Philippines forces conducted Maritime Cooperative Activity in the water and air around the Philippines for the first time

[4198] Regarding Pacific Island countries, the Albanese Government criticized the former Morrison Government for failing to intervene in the signing of a framework agreement between Solomon Islands and China on security cooperation in April 2022 and announced a basic policy to strengthen engagement with Pacific Island countries

[4199] Based on this policy, the government announced the establishment of Australia Pacific Defence School to provide training programs for members of Pacific Island countries and security forces and the establishment of a framework to support the development of climate-resilient infrastructure for these countries for which climate change is a critical issue

[4200] Australia plays a leading role in assisting these countries in fields such as security maintenance, natural disasters response and maritime patrol

[4201] In addition, in the field of maritime patrol, Australia still regularly deploys ADF assets to the South Pacific to assist with patrol activities

[4202] Australia has provided 18 Guardian-class patrol boats to Pacific island nations

[4203] Commentary: Security Issues Faced by Pacific Island Countries

[4204] Pacific Island Countries is a collective term for 14 island countries located in the South Pacific Ocean

[4205] They are important to Japan as they are a source of abundant marine resources due to their vast exclusive economic zones and serve as transport routes for energy resources

[4206] On the other hand, due to their distance from other regions and their narrow and dispersed national territories, they face various constraints and vulnerabilities, and none of them, excluding three countries, have their own military

[4207] Under these circumstances, they position climate change as the single greatest security threat and take the loss of land due to rising sea levels and the expansion of natural disasters seriously

[4208] These countries have traditionally had deep relationships with the United States, Australia, and New Zealand

[4209] However, in recent years geopolitical competition between the major powers has become apparent due to China’s increasingly active international approach

[4210] For example, while China secured a security cooperation agreement with the Solomon Islands that reportedly includes provisions that allow the dispatch of Chinese police and military to them as well as Chinese port calls and replenishment of ships, the United States has signed a defense cooperation agreement with Papua New Guinea, which is said to include U.S. military access to Papua New Guinea’s ports and airports

[4211] Furthermore, as China seeks to expand its influence through large scale infrastructure development and the dispatch of hospital ships, the United States is attempting to maintain and expand its existing military presence simultaneously

[4212] Thus, competition between the United States and China over involvement in the region is attracting attention

[4213] New Zealand

[4214] New Zealand is located in the Indo-Pacific and is an important strategic cooperative partner that shares fundamental values with Japan

[4215] In July 2022, the Department of Defence (DoD) announced that it would conduct a Defence Policy Review to formulate a long-term defense strategy in light of the growing impact of climate change and the intensification of strategic geopolitical competition, including Russia’s aggression against Ukraine

[4216] It was decided that this “review” would be implemented through the development of four documents

[4217] In August 2023, as the first phase of this “review,” the DoD, recognizing that the country is facing the most challenging strategic environment it has had for decades, released the Defence Policy and Strategy Statement, which sets out defense policy goals and strategies and announced the Future Force Design Principles, which guide the New Zealand Defence Force’s (NZDF) investment plans for the next 15 years

[4218] In its Statement, the Department of Defence (DoD) noted that the heightened competition and tensions in the disputed Indo-Pacific region could have significant impact on New Zealand’s interests and that the impact of climate change will exacerbate existing fragilities within Pacific Island countries and across the region which in turn can increase economic and governance risks

[4219] On China, the DoD observed that the country is using all instruments of national power in ways that can pose challenges to existing international rules and norms

[4220] Also, it is assessed that China continues to invest heavily in growing and modernizing its military, and is increasingly able to project its military and paramilitary force beyond its immediate region, including across the wider Indo-Pacific region

[4221] In light of this assessment, the DoD indicated that the Defence Forces would shift its focus to more actively shaping the country’s security environment, rather than responding to incidents as they happen

[4222] Regarding climate change, the DoD affirmed its commitment to continuing Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) activities for Pacific Island countries in cooperation with like-minded countries and others

[4223] The DoD intends to release a defence white paper with the final defense policy, strategy, capabilities and budget, as well as a defence capability plan outlining a defense development plan to complete the Defence Policy Review

[4224] As for diplomatic relations, New Zealand has maintained close relationships with the United States and Australia and sees Australia as its only formal defense ally

[4225] Section 7 Southeast Asia

[4226] General Situation

[4227] Southeast Asia is the center of the Indo-Pacific region, located at the intersection of the Pacific Ocean and the Indian Ocean and occupies a strategic position for traffic, linking the Pacific and the Indian Oceans, such as the Straits of Malacca and the South China Sea

[4228] Therefore, it is an important region for Japan, which relies on maritime transport for many of the supplies needed for economic activities and the lives of the Japanese people

[4229] Meanwhile, this region still has destabilizing factors, including the territorial disputes in the South China Sea, ethnic minority issues, and separatist and independence movements

[4230] Moreover, there has also been problems with Islamic extremist groups and piracy incidents obstructing the safe passage of ships

[4231] In order to cope with these issues, the countries in Southeast Asia are working to build military forces for national defense and maintenance of domestic public security, as well as for addressing new security issues such as counter-terrorism and counter-piracy

[4232] Each country is also pursuing cooperation respectively with such countries as the United States, China, Russia, and Australia to this end

[4233] Recently, given the backdrop of economic development, countries have been modernizing their military forces, mainly their naval and air forces, as well as strengthening their maritime law enforcement capabilities

[4234] Security and Defense Policies of Each Country 1. Indonesia

[4235] Indonesia is a major country in Southeast Asia, with the world’s largest Muslim population

[4236] At the same time, it is the largest archipelago country in the world as it has vast territorial waters and occupies a strategic position for maritime traffic

[4237] As part of its military force reform, Indonesia aims to meet the minimum requirements for defense capabilities—what it calls “Minimum Essential Force (MEF).”

[4238] In particular, Indonesia acknowledges that its maritime defense capabilities are still very much inadequate

[4239] Accordingly, Indonesia has announced a defense budget increase as well as a policy to bolster its deployment of assets to the Natuna Islands, in the South China Sea, and other locations

[4240] Indonesia has deployed an integrated unit and an air squadron, etc., and in December 2018, it was reported that the transfer of the headquarters of a naval combat group command to Natuna is almost completed, that an opening ceremony of a military base with piers that can accommodate submarines, and hangars for unmanned vehicles was conducted, and furthermore, that the ground-breaking ceremony for a submarines support facility was held in April

[4241] Concerned about the “nine-dash line” claimed by China, which overlaps with Indonesia’s EEZ in the vicinity of the Natuna Islands, Indonesia has enhanced its patrol activities in the area

[4242] In December 2019, Indonesia’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a note of protest on the grounds that a Chinese Coast Guard vessel had been found to have operated illegally in the EEZ around the Natuna Islands by escorting fishing fleet

[4243] Indonesia adopts a free and active foreign policy and emphasizes cooperation with Southeast Asian countries

[4244] With the United States, Indonesia is strengthening its cooperative relationship in such fields as military education and training and military equipment procurement

[4245] In addition, Indonesia has carried out bilateral training including army exercise Garuda Shield, naval exercise Cooperation Afloat Readiness and Training (CARAT)1 and counter terrorism exercise Southeast Asia Cooperation Against Terrorism (SEACAT)2 with the U.S. In 2023, Indonesia continued on from the previous year to conduct multilateral multi-service exercise Super Garuda Shield, participated by armed forces of Australia and Singapore, the Self-Defense Forces of Japan, and others

[4246] A general term that refers to a series of bilateral naval exercises that the United States conducts with Bangladesh and other Southeast Asian nations 2 Refers to counter-terrorism combined exercises that the United States conducts with Southeast Asian nations

[4247] Malaysia

[4248] Malaysia’s first defense white paper, which was published in December 2019, finds its potential to serve as a bridge between the vast Pacific and Indian Oceans as the country is divided in two territories—Peninsular Malaysia, and Sabah and Sarawak, on the island of Borneo—located between the two oceans

[4249] The white paper also recognizes the fact that, while Malaysia’s strategic location and natural resources are blessings ones, they also pose a security challenge to itself

[4250] Given these attributes, Malaysia has historically been affected by the political dynamics of major powers, and even today, Malaysia sees in its defense white paper that uncertain U. S.-China relationship is the most important strategic challenge for Malaysia

[4251] In connection with the recent continued anchoring of Chinese vessels around South Luconia Shoal, over which Malaysia claims sovereignty, Malaysia has announced that its Navy and maritime law enforcement agencies would conduct around the clock monitoring, and that Malaysia would protect its sovereignty

[4252] Along with this expression of protest and strengthening of its maritime defense capabilities, the Minister of Defense reportedly announced the decision to establish a new naval and air base near the airport in Bintulu, which is close to James Shoal and South Luconia Reef

[4253] Malaysia has also striven to bolster its defense posture in eastern Malaysia including carrying out live-fire missile exercises in Sabah state, on Borneo in eastern Malaysia in July

[4254] In particular, as well as conducting bilateral exercises with the U.S. such as CARAT and SEACAT, Malaysia has been promoting military cooperation including capacity building in the maritime security field

[4255] Malaysia also prioritizes defense relations based on the Five Power Defence Arrangements (FPDA)3 and has established the headquarters of the Integrated Area Defence System (IADS), which coordinates the activities of the FPDA, at the Royal Malaysian Air Force Butterworth Air Base

[4256] Entered into effect in

[4257] This agreement states that Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom will discuss what response should be adopted in the event of an aggression towards or a threat of an attack on Malaysia or Singapore

[4258] The five countries carry out various exercises based on these arrangements

[4259] Myanmar

[4260] Myanmar shares borders with China and India and is a gateway to the Indian Ocean for China and some ASEAN countries

[4261] In light of these factors, Myanmar is noted for its strategic significance

[4262] Its armed forces had control over the government following the collapse of the socialist regime in

[4263] However, with an economic slowdown caused by the economic sanctions imposed by the West, the transition to civilian rule was completed based on the road map to democracy

[4264] Myanmar’s parliamentary election was conducted in November 2020, and the National League for Democracy (NLD) secured an overwhelming single majority in both houses with the number of seats significantly higher than the previous election

[4265] However, in February 2021, then State Counsellor Aung San Suu Kyi and her party’s senior members were detained by Myanmar’s military, which was claiming election fraud, and the armed forces declared a state of emergency to carry out a coup d’état, and powers were handed over to the commander-in-chief

[4266] The State Administration Council (SAC) chaired by Commander-in-Chief of the Myanmar Armed Forces Min Aung Hlaing was formed by the Armed Force

[4267] Then, in April of the same year, although the Committee Representing Pyidaungsu Hluttaw (CRPH) instituted by Pro-Democracy Group declared the establishment of the National Unity Government (NUG), the Armed Forces designated them and others as Terrorist Organizations

[4268] After the ASEAN Leaders’ Meeting held the same month with the presence of a Myanmar military representative, a “Five-Point Consensus” was agreed to, recognizing ASEAN’s proactive and constructive role in promoting a peaceful resolution

[4269] In August of the same year, SAC announced the establishment of an “interim government” with the commander-in-chief of the Myanmar Armed Forces as the “provisional prime minister.”

[4270] Since late October 2023, fighting has intensified in the northeast, with three ethnic armed groups launching large-scale attacks on the Armed Force, and the Armed Force retreating from several towns

[4271] In early January 2024, the ethnic minority side revealed that more than 2,300 Armed Force soldiers, including generals, had surrendered in the eastern region

[4272] Meanwhile, in mid-January, the Armed Force and Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that the Armed Force and the three ethnic armed groups had reached a ceasefire agreement in northern Myanmar, mediated by China

[4273] The details of this ceasefire agreement have not been publicized, and its effectiveness remains to draw attention

[4274] At the ASEAN Summit meeting held in May 2023, the Chairman’s Statement expressing continued deep concern over the escalation of the conflict and violence was issued

[4275] In January 2024, Special Envoy of the ASEAN Chair on Myanmar Alounkeo visited Myanmar and held talks with current “regime” officials, including Senior General Min Aung Hlaing and ethnic armed groups

[4276] Myanmar has maintained a good relationship with China since the two countries established diplomatic relations in 1950 and the country is regarded as a major supplier of equipment

[4277] Myanmar has also received Chinese aid for pipeline construction and the development of Kyaukpyu Port

[4278] In January 2020, President Xi Jinping became the first Chinese leader to visit Myanmar for 19 years and affirmed China’s policy of promoting economic cooperation through the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI

[4279] Myanmar maintains a cooperative relationship with Russia in the military field since the period of the past military regime, and Russia was a destination for students from Myanmar and a supplier of major defense equipment

[4280] In July 2022, the Commander-in-Chief visited Russia, and discussed promotion of defense cooperation with the Deputy Defense Minister

[4281] Furthermore, in September 2022, the Commander-in-Chief met President Putin for the first time, in Vladivostok, to exchange views on cooperation in all sectors, emphasizing their good bilateral relations

[4282] Cooperative relations with North Korea, including weapons trades, were maintained under Myanmar’s military regime in the past

[4283] Following the transition to democracy, although Myanmar denied its military ties to North Korea, the report issued by the Panel of Experts of the UN Security Council Sanctions Committee on North Korea in March 2018 reported that the country received a ballistic missile system and other weapons from North Korea

[4284] A report published by the United Nations Human Rights Council in May 2023 indicated that from February 2021, when the military launched its coup, until December 2022, at least $1 billion worth of weapons and components for manufacturing them were exported from foreign countries to Myanmar

[4285] This included Myanmar’s imports such as Su-30 fighter jets from Russia and JF-17 fighter jets from China

[4286] The Philippines

[4287] The Philippines considers that its archipelagic attributes and geographic location are a source of both strength and vulnerability

[4288] Moreover, the country sees that its strategic location and rich natural resources have also provided a strong temptation to expansionist powers

[4289] Traditionally, the Philippines has positioned resolving internal armed conflicts as its greatest security concern, but it has begun to shift its focus to strengthening territorial defense against the backdrop of the recent dismantling and weakening of domestic anti-government armed groups and rising tensions in the South China Sea

[4290] The Philippines, with a historically close relationship with the United States, has maintained a cooperative relationship with the U.S. under Mutual Defense Treaty and Military Assistance Agreement, even after the withdrawal of the U. S. Forces in

[4291] In February 1998, the two countries signed a Visiting Forces Agreement (VFA), which prescribed the legal status of U. S. military personnel when the U. S. Forces conducts combined military exercises or other related activities in the Philippines

[4292] Furthermore, in April 2014, the two countries signed the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA), which allows enhanced cooperation in disaster relief, rotational deployment of the U. S. Forces, construction and improvement of agreed locations in the Philippines by the U. S., and U. S. Forces’ prepositioning of equipment and others

[4293] In March 2016, the two countries agreed on five bases of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) for carrying out defense cooperation under the EDCA

[4294] Although former President Duterte notified the United States its intention to terminate the VFA in February 2020, he decided to withdraw the notice in July

[4295] In recent years, the two countries have been conducting various military exercises, including large-scale exercise Balikatan, amphibious exercise KAMANDAG, and maritime exercise Sama Sama

[4296] President Marcos, who took office in June 2022, met with President Biden of the U. S. for the first time in person in September 2022 in New York

[4297] The two leaders discussed the situation in the South China Sea and underscored their support for freedom of navigation and overflight and the peaceful resolution of disputes

[4298] In February 2023, defense ministers of the U. S. and the Philippines announced the agreement to designate four new bases for the EDCA

[4299] These four bases consist of three in northern Luzon Island near Taiwan and one on Palawan Island facing the South China Sea

[4300] Furthermore, in May 2023, the U. S.-Philippines Bilateral Defense Guidelines were adopted and released for the first time, which serve as a roadmap of modernization of alliance cooperation and deepening interoperability between the U. S. and the Philippines

[4301] In September 2023, the U. S.-Philippines joint navigation, which had ended under the Duterte administration, was carried out, with a U. S. destroyer and a Philippines frigate conducting joint navigation in the South China Sea

[4302] In November, in the water and air surrounding the Philippines, including the South China Sea, they carried out Maritime Cooperative Activities

[4303] Thus, the defense cooperation between the two countries has begun to progress again since the inauguration of the new administration

[4304] The Philippines and China have competing claims over the sovereignty in the Spratly Islands and Scarborough Shoal of the South China Sea

[4305] In January 2013, seeking a settlement under international law, the Philippines started arbitral tribunal proceedings pursuant to UNCLOS against China

[4306] In July 2016, the final award was rendered, accepting nearly all of the Philippines’ submissions

[4307] The Government of the Philippines released a statement that it welcomed the award by the arbitral tribunal and strongly affirmed its respect for the decision

[4308] The conflicts between the Philippines and China over the South China Sea dispute were observed even after 2020 during which the COVID-19 infections became a global pandemic

[4309] The Philippines protested that a Chinese military vessel had directed fire-control radars at a Philippine Navy ship in February 2020, and that China had established administrative districts on islands in the South China Sea in April of the same year

[4310] In his policy speech in July 2022, President Marcos emphasized that he would not allow any attempt by foreign power to take even one square inch of the Philippines’ sovereign territory

[4311] Furthermore, in the same month, the Department of Foreign Affairs of the Philippines released a statement commemorating the sixth anniversary of the award

[4312] Chinese Coast Guard vessel firing water on a Philippine supply ship near Second Thomas Shoal (December

[4313] AFP-iji

[4314] In January 2023, President Marcos met with President Xi Jinping during his state visit to China

[4315] They agreed to appropriately manage the differences between the two countries regarding the South China Sea issue through peaceful means, and also agreed to establish a direct communication mechanism between the diplomatic authorities of the two countries

[4316] However, since then, there have been frequent reports of obstructive activities by Chinese Coast Guard vessels and other vessels against the Philippine vessels in areas such as the Spratly Islands

[4317] For example, the Philippines government announced that in December 2023, The Philippines supply ship and the Philippines Coast Guard Vessel were obstructed by the Chinese Coast Guard vessel and others through dangerous maneuvers such as intentional collisions and firing of water cannon near the Second Thomas Shoal in the Spratly Islands, where the Philippines warship Sierra Madre was stranded

[4318] The Philippines’ supply ship, escorted by a Philippines Coast Guard Vessel, was attempting to replenish the supplies of the stranded warship

[4319] In response, President Marcos condemned the action by the Chinese vessels towards the Philippines vessels and their personnel, pointing out that it was aggression and provocation, and a clear violation of international law

[4320] The same month, Defense Minister Teodoro held a telephone conversation with U.S. Defense Secretary Austin

[4321] During the conversation, it was reiterated that the U. S.-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty extends to both countries’ armed forces, public vessels, and aircraft -including those of its coast guard- anywhere in Pacific, to include the South China Sea

[4322] Singapore

[4323] Given its limited land area, population, and resources, Singapore’s existence and development depend on the peace and stability of the region in a globalized economy

[4324] Singapore highly prioritize its national defense, with defense spending accounting for about 10% of its national budget

[4325] In October 2022, the Digital and Intelligence Service was established as the fourth service of the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF), integrating existing command, control, communications, computers, intelligence, and cyber capabilities

[4326] Singapore emphasizes the importance of cooperative relations with ASEAN and the FPDA, and has concluded defense cooperation agreements with countries within and outside the region

[4327] With the aim of contributing to peace and stability in the region, Singapore supports United States’ presence in the Asia-Pacific

[4328] Since signing the 1990 Memorandum of Understanding (November 1990), Singapore has been allowing the United States to use military facilities in the country

[4329] In addition to the port calls to Changi Naval Base by U.S. aircraft carriers, the rotational deployment of Littoral combat ships (LCSs) began in

[4330] In 2015, the P-8 patrol aircraft of the U. S. Forces were deployed to Singapore for around one week for the first time

[4331] The two countries have committed to continue carrying out similar deployments routinely

[4332] In addition, Singapore conducts combined exercises with the U. S., such as CARAT and SEACAT

[4333] Singapore has strong economic ties with China, and the two countries also conduct bilateral naval exercises

[4334] In October 2019, the two countries signed the enhanced Agreement on Defence Exchanges and Security Cooperation (ADESC), which formalized existing defense cooperation, including regularization of dialogue and exercises

[4335] On the other hand, diplomatic relations with China have been strained partly due to Singapore’s advocacy of the ruling of the arbitral tribunal to Philippines v. China when it comes to the resolution of the South China Sea disputes and partly due to Singapore’s defense cooperation with Taiwan

[4336] In March 2020, Singapore and Australia signed the Treaty on Military Training and Training Area Development in Australia

[4337] This treaty enables the Singapore Armed Forces to access Australia’s training area which will be newly developed

[4338] Thailand

[4339] Thailand’s defense policy includes: strengthening defense cooperation through ASEAN, international organizations, and other entities; defense that makes comprehensive use of political, economic, and other national strengths; and effective defense aimed at increasing the readiness of the Royal Thai Armed Forces (RTAF) and developing the defense industry

[4340] Under its flexible omni-directional diplomatic policy, Thailand pursues cooperation with other Southeast Asian countries and coordination with major countries

[4341] In particular, Thailand has an alliance with the United States based on the Southeast Asia Collective Defense Treaty (Manila Treaty) (effective from February 1955), and the U.S. military has access to the Thai military’s U-Tapao Royal Thai Navy Airfield

[4342] Thailand has been conducting the U. S.-Thailand combined exercise “Cobra Gold” since 1982, which is currently one of the largest multilateral exercises in Southeast Asia

[4343] In addition to the marine corps of the two countries have continued their combined naval training CARAT and counter-piracy and trafficking exercise SEACAT

[4344] Thailand and China have conducted combined training such as Blue Strike between their marines and Falcon Strike between their air forces

[4345] Vietnam

[4346] Based on its viewpoint that the sea is closely associated with the national construction and defense, Vietnam has established the objective of becoming a strong marine country, particularly prioritizing the modernization of its military forces and law enforcement forces at sea as well as ensuring the capability for maritime domain awareness, maritime independence, sovereign rights, jurisdiction and national interests at sea

[4347] Vietnam deploys its omni-directional diplomatic policy and intends to actively participate in international and regional cooperation in order to build friendly relations with every nation

[4348] In March 2016, Vietnam opened an international port in the Cam Ranh Bay, which is located in a strategically important location, and Navy vessels from many countries including Japan have called at the international Cam Ranh Bay port

[4349] Vietnam and the United States have strengthened their military relations in recent years

[4350] This has taken such forms as combined training with the U.S. Navy and port calls by U.S. Navy vessels in Vietnam

[4351] In 2017, mutual visits were conducted by the leaders of both countries and an agreement was reached on the deepening of defense cooperation

[4352] In March 2018, the USS Carl Vinson became the first U. S. aircraft carrier to visit Vietnam since the Vietnam War

[4353] In September 2023, during U. S. President Biden’s first visit to Vietnam as president, he met with then President Thuong and agreed to upgrade the bilateral relationship to a comprehensive strategic partnership

[4354] In this context, the United States committed to continue to support Vietnam in building an independent defense capability

[4355] Vietnam and Russia continue to strengthen cooperation in the area of national defense, with Vietnam dependent on Russia for the majority of its defense equipment

[4356] In April 2018, the two countries signed a military and technical cooperation roadmap, while in July 2019, a Vietnamese naval vessel visited the port of Vladivostok for the first time

[4357] In December the same year, a submarine rescue vessel from Russia’s Pacific Fleet visited the port of Cam Ranh and participated in the first bilateral joint submarine rescue exercise

[4358] Section 5-5-5 (1) (Relations with Asian Countries

[4537] Europe and Canada. 1. General Situation

[4538] With the end of the Cold War, many European countries and Canada now recognize the need to address diverse security challenges

[4539] At the same time, these countries had recognized that the threat of large-scale invasion by other countries had disappeared

[4540] Nevertheless, since the heightening of tensions in Ukraine in February 2014 and particularly with the aggression against Ukraine that began in February 2022, there is a growing need to revisit existing strategies and plan new concepts in order to deal with Russia's unilateral changes to the status quo by force as well as hybrid warfare

[4541] With regard to international terrorism, the continuity of threats has been recognized and there is a continuous need to take counterterrorism measures

[4542] In addition, border security problems remain a challenge, including those regarding refugees and migrants that have rapidly increased due to Middle East turmoil such as the prolonged civil war in Syria

[4543] To respond to such challenges and situations, Europe and Canada have sought to further strengthen and expand multilateral frameworks, such as the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and the European Union (EU

[4544] At the same time, it is working to contribute to the security and stability of the international community by proactively participating in activities outside the region

[4545] Moreover, steps are taken at the national level by reviewing security and defense strategies, reforming national defense systems, and strengthening bilateral and multilateral defense and security cooperation

[4566] Enhancement of Multilateral Security Frameworks

[4567] Founded for the core task of collective defense among member states, NATO celebrates its 75th anniversary in

[4568] It has expanded the scope of its activities to conflict prevention and crisis management since the end of the Cold War

[4569] NATO’s three core tasks are deterrence and defense, crisis prevention and management, and cooperative security

[4570] Amid an increasing sense of crisis among member states in response to Russia’s aggression against Ukraine, a new NATO Strategic Concept was adopted at the NATO Summit in June 2022 for the first time in twelve years since

[4571] Although the previous Strategic Concept stated that the Euro-Atlantic area is at peace and the threat of a conventional attack against NATO territory is low, this new Strategic Concept states that the Euro-Atlantic area is not at peace and the possibility of an attack against member states’ sovereignty and territorial integrity cannot be discounted

[4572] In the previous Strategic Concept, NATO had stated that it was aiming for “a true strategic partnership” with Russia

[4573] In the new Strategic Concept, however, NATO placed Russia as the most significant and direct threat to member states’ security and to peace and stability in the Euro-Atlantic area

[4574] This new Strategic Concept mentioned China for the first time, stating that China’s ambition and coercive policies are the challenge against NATO’s interests, security and values

[4575] The new Strategic Concept also pointed out that the deepening relationship between China and Russia and their mutually reinforcing attempts to undercut the rules-based international order run counter to NATO’s values and interests

[4576] In addition to this, it mentioned the nuclear and missile development by North Korea for the first time and stated that the Indo-Pacific region is an important region and NATO will strengthen dialogue and cooperation with the partners, as it can directly affect Euro-Atlantic security

[4577] NATO invited Japan, Australia, New Zealand, and the ROK as the important partners to the NATO Summit held in June 2022, and decided to enhance cooperation with them on maritime security and disinformation countermeasures among other issues

[4578] Through these actions, NATO has emphasized one of its core missions of defending member states while strengthening deterrence and defense capabilities based on an understanding of how the situation has drastically changed

[4579] Since 2014, NATO has overhauled its plans and structures to ensure member states can respond to any threat from any direction, with an agreement to establish a forward presence, particularly in the east

[4580] The first multinational battalion-sized battlegroups were deployed in Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, and Poland in 2017, with further battlegroups having been created in Bulgaria, Hungary, Romania, and Slovakia since

[4581] At the NATO summit in June the same year, it was agreed that these battlegroups would be expanded from battalion to brigade size as needed

[4582] A new force model was also agreed, on a far larger scale with far greater readiness than traditional readiness

[4583] The NATO summit in July 2023 approved the most comprehensive and detailed regional defense plan since the Cold War

[4584] This is expected to significantly improve the consistency between NATO’s collective defense plans and NATO members’ own plans for force, readiness, capabilities, and command and control

[4585] Under this new defense plan, “Steadfast Defender 2024,” the largest-scale military exercise since the end of the Cold War, was conducted from January to May

[4586] Involving all NATO member states, the exercise saw NATO troops rapidly deployed from North America to the Atlantic Ocean to strengthen the defense of the Euro-Atlantic region

[4587] Additionally, alongside collective defense, NATO’s core tasks include operations to prevent and control crises from inside and/or outside of member states

[4588] In the Mediterranean, a permanent maritime force has been deployed due to increase in the influx of illegal immigrants transiting the Mediterranean

[4589] This force monitors the influx of illegal immigrants and shares information

[4590] Also, a wider array of missions including counterterrorism and capacity building assistance have been conducted

[4591] In the Middle East, with regard to the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant (ISIL), NATO has dispatched early warning and control aircraft forces and implemented NATO surveillance and reconnaissance missions since October

[4592] It is also supporting security units of Iraqi Armed Forces on training and capacity building

[4593] NATO is also carrying out missions in Kosovo and other countries

[4594] Regarding defense spending among NATO member states, the 2014 agreement set a target of 2% of GDP, and in November 2022, NATO Secretary General Stoltenberg stated that 2% of each member country’s GDP should be more as a kind of floor than a ceiling

[4595] At the July 2023 summit, NATO member states agreed to invest a minimum of 2% of their respective GDPs in defense spending

[4596] As a result, defense spending across European member states and Canada increased by 11% in 2023, and by 2024, defense spending in 18 countries is expected to reach 2% of each GDP

[4597] In response to Russia’s aggression against Ukraine, Finland and Sweden reversed their longstanding policy of military non-alignment and joined NATO in April 2023 and March 2024, respectively

[4598] This brought the total number of NATO members to 32. 2 EU

[4599] The EU is strengthening its security initiatives under the Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) and the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP

[4600] In December 2017, the Permanent Structured Cooperation (PESCO) was launched as a defense cooperation framework comprising 26 of the member states

[4601] NATO made it clear that it promotes developing new capabilities in aviation and maritime domains, training and support for armed forces and sharing expertise of specific domains such as the cyberspace domain through this framework

[4602] Therefore, the strengthening of Europe’s defense capabilities is expected

[4603] Furthermore, the EU is enhancing its engagement to the Indo-Pacific region, disclosing its first Indo-Pacific strategy in April 2021 followed by a joint communication detailing it in September

[4604] This joint communication states that the growing tensions resulting from China’s significant military buildup and show of force in the East China Sea, South China Sea, and Taiwan Strait have a direct effect on security and prosperity in Europe

[4605] To achieve the aim of a rules-based international order, partnership with countries sharing the same values, including Japan, is necessary, along with the reinforcement of economic relations with Taiwan, including through trading and investments

[4606] In March 2022, the European Council adopted the Strategic Compass laying out a common strategic vision for security and defense policies in the next five to ten years

[4607] The document stated that the EU will establish a fully operational EU Rapid Deployment Capacity of up to 5,000 troops by 2025 for use in rescue and evacuation operations

[4619] One of NATO's long-standing challenges has been to strengthen the defense of the Baltic Sea region, which lies on the front line with Russia

[4620] In particular, if Russia were to occupy the Suwatki Gap, which connects the Russian exclave Kaliningrad with Belarus, the Baltic states would be at risk of becoming geographically isolated from the other member states

[4621] To address these concerns, since Russia unilaterally annexed Crimea in 2014, NATO has been working to expand its forward presence and reinforcement posture on its eastern flank

[4622] The accession of Finland and Sweden to NATO realized in 2023 to 2024 further strengthens the defenses of the Baltic Sea region

[4623] Both countries have been increasing their interoperability with NATO member states since

[4624] Furthermore, Finland has a large number of ground forces, including reserves, and it is strengthening its air power with the procurement of F-35s while Sweden is enhancing its naval power with a focus on submarines

[4625] This strengthening of the national defenses of both countries combined with their improved interoperability with member states will contribute to a more robust NATO's defense posture in the Baltic Sea region, where both countries are located

[4626] Additionally, the accession of Finland and Sweden to NATO will also lead to the enhancement of NATO's defense plans

[4627] NATO reportedly approved defense plans for the Baltic states and Poland in 2019, but it was unclear whether NATO assumed cooperation with Finland and Sweden in the plans

[4628] With both countries becoming members, however, future NATO defense plans are expected to be developed with the assumption of some degree of access to both countries

[4629] This means that both countries could become options for reinforcement routes from member states or as starting points for counterattacks, which would also lead to the development of NATO's defense plans for the Baltic Sea region

[4630] More importantly, the accession of the two countries to NATO will link the Baltic Sea region and the Atlantic Ocean (including the Arctic region

[4631] High North]) as part of NATO territory

[4632] This will improve the connectivity of NATO’s territory across North America, the Atlantic Ocean, Europe, and the Baltic Sea region, and it will also contribute to the improvement of NATO's overall defense planning

[4633] NATO approved regional defense plans for its entire territory in

[4634] The membership of Finland and Sweden in NATO may lead to the further development of the regional defense plans

[4760] Viewpoint

[4761] Clashes between Israel and the Palestinian Militants

[4762] NISHINO Masami, Senior Fellow, Asia and Africa Division, National Institute for Defense Studies

[4763] On October 7, 2023, militants of the Islamic fundamentalist organization Hamas, which effectively controls the Gaza Strip, invaded southern Israel, killing approximately 1,200 people and abducting over 200 others

[4764] These human casualties shocked Israel

[4765] In the past, Hamas frequently used suicide bombings, so Israel began full-scale construction of a separating wall in 2002 to contain them

[4766] Later, when Hamas focused on launching rockets, Israel began operating the Iron Dome missile defense system in 2011, which intercepted most of them

[4767] As a result, Israel believed that the threat from Hamas was reduced, but this belief was shattered

[4768] It has been suggested that one of the factors behind Hamas's attack this time was that Saudi Arabia and Israel were close to establishing diplomatic relations

[4769] If the two countries established diplomatic relations, other Arab countries were expected to follow suit

[4770] Hamas appears to have tried to provoke the conflict to prevent the establishment of such diplomatic relations

[4771] This attack served as a reminder of the importance of lessons from the past

[4772] On October 6, 1973, during a Jewish holiday, Israel suffered a surprise attack by Arab forces, resulting in heavy damage

[4773] Therefore, the lesson was that Israel needed to be prepared because the enemy would launch a surprise attack on holidays when its defense systems were off guard

[4774] However, half a century later, Israel was again subjected to a similar surprise attack

[4775] The Israeli military immediately launched a counterattack, sending ground forces into the Gaza Strip in late October

[4776] In the fighting in the Gaza Strip, Israel has the advantage in military strength, so Hamas is focusing on: concealing the whereabouts of its leaders and hostages, using propaganda to win public opinion on its side, and negotiations by its leadership abroad

[4777] Israel’s goal is to destroy Hamas, i.e., to disable its leadership and military wing and rescue the hostages

[4778] Hamas's goal is to maintain its existence in the Gaza Strip

[4779] To achieve its goal, Hamas will likely need to leverage hostages and public opinion to negotiate a permanent ceasefire

[4780] The Gaza Strip is small and has been blockaded, so the longer the fighting drags on, the more likely it is that Israel will be able to thoroughly search and neutralize Hamas leaders, and Hamas is running short of supplies and finding it more difficult to continue fighting

[4781] In light of this, it can be said that prolonged fighting is advantageous for Israel

[4782] However, even if the Israeli military wins, it is likely that some Gaza residents will continue to support Hamas, and Hamas members are also present in the West Bank and neighboring countries, so although Hamas will be weakened, it is unlikely to be destroyed

[4783] The number of deaths in the Gaza Strip has risen, prompting more countries to criticize Israel, but countries other than the United States are unlikely to have a significant impact on Israel's military operations

[4784] The United States, which is seen as the only country that can exert enough influence to force Israel to stop the fighting, has continued to supply weapons to Israel but warned in May 2024 that it would stop supplying some weapons depending on the actions of the Israeli military

[4785] The United States has already halted the supply of some ammunition, and this change in the US stance could affect Israel's military operations in the medium to long term

[4786] As for the full-scale spillover of the conflict beyond the Gaza Strip, both the United States and Iran, the latter of which backs pro-Iranian groups such as Hezbollah conducting attacks in solidarity with Hamas, will try to avoid such spillovers

[4787] Some pro-Iranian forces, such as the Houthis in Yemen, are not hesitating to escalate the conflict, but since the U.S. military and others are primarily dealing with the Houthis, Israel does not have to use its resources against distant adversaries

[4788] However, in April 2024, Iran directly attacked Israeli territory from its own territory for the first time using ballistic missiles, and Israel appears to have attacked Iran in response

[4789] In such a case, the United States has a policy of not cooperating with an attack on Iran in order to avoid escalation, so Israel is likely to cope with it on its own

[4790] Attacks against Hamas in neighboring countries, like the killing of a leading member of Hamas in Lebanon in January 2024, are expected to occur in the future

[4956] Trends and Challenges Facing the International Community Concerning the Space, Cyber, and Electromagnetic Domains and Information Warfare

[4957] Risks that hinder free access and usage of cyberspace, the oceans, outer space and the electromagnetic spectrum are becoming increasingly serious

[4958] In particular, the threat of cyber attacks has grown rapidly and the theft of sensitive information, etc., has also been taking place on a routine basis, even in the form of state-backed attacks

[4959] It is likely that hybrid warfare consisting of both military and non-military measures for the accomplishment of military objectives will be employed in more sophisticated ways through means such as information warfare, including through the dissemination of disinformation prior to armed attacks

[4960] These trends pose serious challenges to the international community, including Japan

[4961] section 1 Trends Concerning Military Science and Technology That Have Expanded to Information Warfare, etc

[4962] Science, Technology and Security

[4963] The creation of science, technology and innovation is the source of Japan’s own economic and social development and the appropriate use of technological capabilities is indispensable not only in national security but also in addressing global issues such as climate change

[4964] The nations of the world are focusing their efforts on research, development and military applications of cutting-edge technologies that might be game-changers in that they could change the whole situation of future battles, such as artificial intelligence (AI), quantum technology and next generation information and communication technology

[4965] Our attention needs to be focused on these applications as something that will greatly improve the accuracy and speed of decision making, as information processing, which has so far been limited by the capabilities of human beings and conventional computers, could become faster and automatic

[4966] In addition, we need to focus on the fact that high-speed, large-capacity and safe communication based on these new technologies will greatly contribute to the need for automation and manpower savings in the use of future defense technologies

[4967] Risks in the cyberspace domain and other areas are also becoming more serious

[4968] Above all, these new technologies blur the boundary between military and non-military matters, enhancing the so-called gray-zone situation

[4969] There are many examples in which diverse means that are not limited to purely military ones have been used to create chaos in other countries, such as cyber attacks targeting communication or important infrastructure, or the use of drones

[4970] Technological influence in the field of security is becoming greater; for example, the technology known as deepfake with which fake videos are created through the application of AI technology is spreading, while information warfare through the dissemination of disinformation is constantly taking place

[4971] In addition, technology competition among nations becomes apparent, notably in the fields of next generation information communication system (Beyond 5G) and semiconductors

[4972] This competition is based on the perception that it is profitable to lead international standardization with superiority in the emerging technologies that are to become important for national economy and security

[4973] Moreover, it is commonly getting understood that securing supply chains for critical key products such as semiconductors and rare metals is important from a security standpoint

[4974] In this situation, the concern is that some nations are stealing information related to advanced technologies developed by private companies, universities and other organizations in other countries using cyberspace, corporate acquisitions, corporate activities including investments, academic exchanges and covert operatives and using the information for their own military purposes

[4975] For this, each nation takes measures for their “economic security,” such as strict export control, reinforcement of screening for investments from foreign countries and higher independence for technological development and production

[4977] Trends of Military Cutting-edge Technology (1) Hypersonic Weapons

[4978] The United States, China, Russia and others are developing hypersonic weapons, including Hypersonic Glide Vehicles (HGVs) that would be launched from ballistic missiles, maneuvered to glide at hypersonic speed (Mach 5 or above) in the atmosphere and hit targets, as well as Hypersonic Cruise Missiles (HCMs) using scramjet engines and other technologies that enable hypersonic flights

[4993] High-power Energy Technology

[4994] High-power energy weapons, such as railguns, high-energy laser weapons and high-power microwave weapons, are being developed as a means to counter various airborne threats

[4995] A railgun is a kind of weapon that shoot bullets using a magnetic field generated from electrical energy

[4996] Unlike missiles, the bullets used for railguns have no propulsion device

[4997] For this reason, the bullets are smaller, cost less and require less space for storing

[4998] Therefore, railguns are said to be capable of coping effectively with attacks involving a large number of missiles

[4999] Laser weapons, which use high-power laser energy to destroy targets, are being developed by the United States, China, Russia and other countries as low-cost, effective means of intercepting a large number of small, unmanned aircraft and small vessels

[5001] In 2023, the U.S. Army received prototypes of the 50kW-class vehicle-mounted laser weapon “DE M-SHORAD (Directed Energy Maneuver-Short Range Air Defense)” and concluded a contract to develop 300kW-class laser weapons

[5055] Perspective

[5056] Information Warfare and Intelligence Services: Adaptation to Challenges of the State-sponsored Influence Operations and Disinformation SETO Takashi, Research Fellow, Cyber Security Division, National Institute for Defense Studies

[5057] Liberal democracies have faced serious concerns about state-sponsored “Influence operations,” such as covertly spreading disinformation on social networking services (SNSs

[5058] They are recognized as “hybrid threats” short of armed conflict as they undermine the trust of democratic institutions like elections

[5059] In addition, they have been grave national security threats as they support “hybrid warfare,” a combination of the military and non-military means for revising the status quo while managing the escalation

[5060] Digital enabled influence operations, in nature, exploit privately owned ICT platforms and exacerbate existing political, economic, and social vulnerabilities within the targeted community

[5061] In response, Western democracies have pursued a “whole-of-society approach” that convenes inter-agency and cross-sectoral cooperation, such as industry and civil society stakeholders, to tackle the challenges of influence operations

[5062] While the whole-of-society approach comprises a variety of multi-stakeholder efforts, the whole of the government's preparedness for “integrated information warfare with special regards to cognitive dimension,” comprising both intelligence and strategic communication functions, is vital as it shapes shared situational awareness and helps public-private partnerships and international cooperation to identify and disrupt imminent threats

[5063] Recent examples highlight two distinctive approaches to the government's institutional adaptation toward “information warfare” among Western democracies

[5064] One is organizing a specialized government body that is responsible for tracking and exposing digitally-enabled operations leveraging open-source intelligence (OSINT), such as VIGINUM under the French General Secretariat for Defense and National Security

[5065] The other is harnessing national intelligence services to deal with the challenges of information warfare

[5066] The latter approach was exemplified by the relentless declassification of intelligence analysis by the U.S. and UK intelligence community to expose and preempt Russia's false flag operations and disinformation campaign, thereby disrupting Russia's blitzkrieg military victory like the annexation of Crimea in

[5067] Similar initiatives include the U. S. and U. K-led international campaigns, in collaboration with like-minded European allies such as the Netherlands, in order to publicly expose tradecrafts of covert cyber operations and traditional sabotage by adversaries’ foreign intelligence apparatus

[5068] Recent academic literature has pointed out two distinctive advantages of harnessing intelligence services to respond to the challenges of information warfare

[5069] One is access to sensitive sources and methods and unique analytical insights, which are not always available to the OSINT by non-state actors

[5070] Leveraging privileged access to such capabilities enables them to identify and attribute covert nation-state sponsorship faster than other stakeholders

[5071] This aspect is something like placing the intelligence agencies as “early-warning sensors” against state-sponsored influence operations

[5072] The second aspect is leveraging such unique insights and international media attention generated by strategic declassification efforts as a “catalyst” for reciprocal knowledge co-production and narrative amplification dynamics vis-à-vis industry and civil society partners

[5073] For example, the US/UK-led intelligence disclosure before the Russian invasion of Ukraine, with exceptional international media attention, stimulated the independent OSINT-enabled verification by Bellingcat and other international research institutes, leading to shared but verified situational awareness of threats and international solidarity in support of Ukraine

[5074] Another example is the series of the Joint Cyber Security Advisory issued by the U.S. allies and partners, which aims to scale up the reciprocal sharing of cyber threat intelligence vis-a-vis persistent state-sponsored cyber campaigns beyond the specific jurisdiction

[5075] These developments imply that intelligence services in liberal democracies have struggled to adapt to complex information environments in the 21st century, where they must build collaborative feedback loops between industry and civil society partners, as the state’s monopoly of knowledge and narrative has been eroding due to the proliferation of the ICT

[5076] Such dynamics also raise a question about the organizational identity of the national intelligence apparatus between the traditional roles of the secretive supporter serving the government decision-makers and the public-facing roles for reaching out to various stakeholders as a “whole-of-society approach”

[5077] In conclusion, the relationship between information warfare and intelligence agencies symbolizes the challenges of adaptation of secret intelligence in the liberal democracy vis-a-vis the information environment of the 21st century

[5078] For initiatives by the Ministry of Defense and the Self-Defense Forces, see Part II, Chapter 1, Section 5 of the White Paper

[5079] Note

[5080] This column is an independent analysis from the researcher's academic perspective, and its contents do not represent an official government position I. Diffusion of Information-related Technology and Information Warfare

[5081] As has been pointed out in the cases of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, the 2023 clashes between Israel and the Palestinian militants as well as the presidential election in Taiwan, concerns over information warfare, such as the dissemination of disinformation and the proliferation of information aimed at eroding trust in the target government or dividing society using social networking services (SNS) and influencers have been growing

[5082] It is believed that Russia and China are waging information warfare both domestically and abroad, aiming to build an information environment favorable to them

[5083] For example, it has been pointed out that China is spending billions of dollars to promote propaganda, spread disinformation and conduct censorship by investing in the media of other countries

[5084] It has also been noted that China and Russia are collaborating to spread propaganda and disinformation, disseminating their convenient narratives to target recipients in countries like Japan, the United States, Taiwan and Europe, as well as third countries in the Global South

[5085] It has been pointed out that autonomous programs called bots are becoming more commonly used in tactics on social media

[5086] Major social media companies are working to remove bot accounts, but there are also moves to use fake photos generated by AI to avoid being targeted for removal

[5087] Furthermore, advances in AI technology could make deepfakes and generative AI-created videos, images and documents even more of a serious threat, as they are highly realistic and can be created in a short time with easily accessible tools

[5088] In response, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security issued an advisory on the threat of deepfakes in September

[5089] In November the same year, the Department of Defense developed the “Strategy for Operations in the Information Environment (SOIE),” which stated the need for the Office of the Secretary of Defense, the Joint Chiefs of Staff and regional military forces to collaborate toward the same goal

[5090] In Europe, the EU has proposed the concept of “Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference” (FIMI) and is working on countermeasures

[5091] As for technological responses, the U. S. Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is developing detection functions to verify the authenticity of various information in the media and private companies are also developing software that utilize AI and algorithms to automatically collect and analyze online information

[5092] This software is being introduced to public institutions in various countries as a new means of gathering information

[5093] “Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference” (FIMI

[5094] This is a concept that refers to "a series of actions by foreign governments or others that have (or may have) the intention of wielding malign influence over the sense of values, procedures, or political processes" of one’s country

[5095] EU, NATO and each European country show serious concerns about the spread of FIMI in the world

[5096] FIMI is often carried out legally, deliberately and systematically by foreign countries, non-state actors, or affiliated organizations, to wield influence on public opinion of one’s country or disrupt democratic processes such as presidential elections

[5097] This kind of information manipulation operation disables not only each individual but society as a whole from making its own decisions

[5098] This is one of the major threats to a democratic society based on free and open information

[5099] Trends Concerning Defense Production and Technology Bases

[5100] Advanced technologies based on significant technological advances in the civilian field have so much power that they can completely change the way battles happen

[5101] Relative merits in industry and technology greatly influence national security

[5102] Under these circumstances, many countries are taking on a variety of initiatives in order to maintain and enhance their national defense production and technological bases

[5103] First of all, each country enhances investments to defense research and development to ensure technological superiority

[5104] For example, about half of the nearly 16 trillion yen invested in the government research expenditure of the United States is paid out by the DoD

[5105] This is in contrast to the situation in Japan in which the research and development budget for the Ministry of Defense (the MOD) is only around 5% of government research expenditure

[5106] The United States also offers large-scale funds to research conducted by companies and universities

[5107] For example, DARPA, an internal organization of the DoD, has requested a budget of US$4,370 million for FY2025 to continue active investments in innovative research at companies and universities, with the aim of maintaining the U.S. Forces’ technological superiority

[5108] In addition, the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) mediates between companies owning innovative technology and the DoD to make the most of cutting-edge technologies from the civilian field in the resolution of challenges in the security sector

[5109] The DIU has produced contracts with over 450 companies mainly in six fields, including AI, autonomous technology and the cyber field

[5147] Trends in Space Domain I. Space Domain and Security

[5148] There is no concept of national borders in space, meaning that the utilization of satellites enables the observation of, communication with and positioning over any area on Earth

[5149] Thus, major countries make efforts to enhance the capabilities of a variety of satellites and launch them for the purpose of enhancing C4ISR (command, control, communication, computer, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance) functions

[5150] Such satellites include information collecting satellites that collect various activities as images and radio waves, early warning satellites for detecting the launch of ballistic missiles, positioning satellites for enhancing the precision of weapons systems, communication satellites relays communication and the like

[5151] On the other hand, anti-satellite weapons (ASAT) to hinder the utilization of space by other countries are also under development

[5152] Regarding destructive Direct-Ascent Anti-SATellite (DA-ASAT) missiles, China and Russia conducted tests targeting their own satellites in 2007 and 2021, respectively

[5153] As a result, a large amount of space debris has been generated, raising concerns about the risk of such debris colliding with satellites and other space assets of various countries

[5154] Regarding China, it has been pointed out that the robot arm technologies being developed by China to inspect and repair on-orbit satellites can be diverted to ASAT weapons such as satellite-attack satellites (so-called “killer satellites”

[5155] As for Russia, it has been pointed out that the ejection of an object from its satellite against a nearby satellite was an ASAT experiment

[5156] Furthermore, it has been pointed out that China and Russia are developing jammers for interfering with communications between target satellites and ground stations, as well as high-energy technology such as laser weapons designed to degrade or damage satellites

[5157] In addition, a Russian cyber-attack on a satellite communication provider in 2022 disrupted satellite communications services, raising concerns about cyber-attacks on space systems

[5158] As threats in space continue to rise, many countries are increasingly positioning space as a “warfighting domain” or “operational domain.”

[5159] These countries are working on space domain awareness (SDA) to monitor threats to their space assets

[5160] Against this backdrop, the existing international agreements do not have direct provisions on prohibiting the destruction of space assets or avoiding actions triggering space debris

[5161] Accordingly, with peaceful usage and the need to prevent an arms race in mind, the United Nations is debating this issue in the Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space (COPUOS) and the First Committee of the United Nations General Assembly

[5162] In recent years, topics related to disarmament, such as “Prevention of an Arms Race in Outer Space” and “Reducing Space Threats through Norms, Rules and Principles of Responsible Behaviors,” have also been discussed

[5163] In 2023, the UN General Assembly also adopted a resolution to continue these discussions

[5164] In addition, as part of the efforts of like-minded nations, the Combined Space Operations Initiative (CSpO) meetings are being held to discuss space security, with three new countries, including Japan, joining to discuss operational cooperation and information sharing

[5184] Chapter 3, Section 2-2-5 (Military Posture) 2. China

[5185] China has been promoting space development since the 1950s and has been further intensifying its space activities, including landing an unmanned probe on the far side of the moon, completing the space station “Tiangong,” and advancing plans for a lunar base

[5186] In 2023, China launched a number of satellites, including the positioning satellite "BeiDou" and the earth observation satellite "Yaogan," and is also working to build a satellite constellation for rapid information gathering and communication

[5187] While traditionally emphasizing international cooperation and the peaceful use of space, it is pointed out that China proactively used space for military purposes, including information collection, communications and positioning through satellites

[5188] For example, the possibility of military use has been pointed out for “BeiDou” for aircraft and vessel navigation and guidance of missiles, and for “Yaogan” for electronic and image reconnaissance

[5189] Regarding carrier rockets such as the “Long March” series, the Chinese state-owned enterprises that developed and produced them are said to be also developing and producing ballistic missiles, and it is believed that the development of carrier rockets could also be applied to the development of ballistic missiles

[5190] It is pointed out that China recognizes counter space operations as a means to deter and confront the United States’s intervention to regional conflicts and carries out ASAT weapons development and the like

[5191] In addition to the satellite destruction test in 2007 mentioned above and the “non-destructive” test of an ASAT missile in July 2014, it is also pointed out that China continues to acquire and develop various ASAT capabilities and related technologies such as ground-based lasers and space robots

[5192] China is thus expected to focus on space development through close cooperation between government, military and private sectors

[5193] The United States estimates that China pursues space capabilities the same as or higher than those of the United States.4 It is also pointed out that the number of Chinese military satellites under operation is larger than that of the United States

[5194] In terms of policy, China insists that space is key to international strategic competition and that the safety of space is a strategic safeguard for nation building and social development

[5195] It also reveals the principle that it accelerates development of the aerospace domain

[5196] In the white paper titled “China’s Space Program: A 2021 Perspective” issued in January 2022, it was emphasized to “build China into a space power” and it stated that China promotes the space industry
