[6511] Section 2 Defense-Related Expenditures

[6512] In order to protect Japan’s territory, which extends approximately 3,000 kilometers along both the north-south and east-west axes, Japan needs capabilities to deal with vessels and landing forces invading Japan, including its remote islands, from locations outside of threat zones

[6513] Such threats include anti-aircraft missile capabilities

[6514] Also, it is essential for Japan to possess capabilities that are necessary and sufficient to block and eliminate the opponent’s vessels, landing forces, and the like from various locations in our country in a multilayered manner no matter which region an invasion may initiate

[6515] Against this backdrop, Japan can force the opponent to complicate its measures if it diversifies its launch platforms and respond with a combination of various stand-off missiles with various features

[6516] To this end, the MOD/SDF will secure a necessary and sufficient amount of stand-off missiles by procuring foreign-made missiles early on while supporting the expansion of the domestic capacity to manufacture missiles

[6517] The MOD/SDF will also expedite R&D and mass production efforts for early acquisition of capabilities to operate more advanced stand-off missiles

[6518] For early acquisition of stand-off missiles, the MOD/SDF will start deploying domestically made, Upgraded Type-12 SSM (surface-launched variant) in FY2025, one year earlier than planned, in light of an increasingly severe security environment

[6519] It will also begin acquiring U.S.-made Tomahawks in FY2025, one year earlier than planned

[6520] Through these measures, the MOD/SDF will promptly secure sufficient capabilities prior to the establishment of increased production of domestic missiles

[6521] At the same time, the MOD/SDF will advance efforts to establish a series of functions necessary for the operation of stand-off missiles, including target information gathering functions and command and control functions

[6522] Part III, Chapter 1, Section 4-1 (Responses to Invasion of Japan, Including Its Remote Islands

[6523] Procuring Aegis System Equipped Vessels

[6524] Recent years have seen rapid changes and developments in missile-related technologies, most notably hypersonic glide vehicles (HGVs) and missiles flying with irregular trajectories

[6525] This points to the urgent need to reinforce integrated air and missile defense capabilities, including ballistic missile defense capabilities

[6526] For the primary purpose of defending Japan from threats of ballistic missiles and other weapons systems that are thus increasingly sophisticated, the MOD/SDF will begin constructing Aegis System Equipped Vessels (ASEVs) during FY

[6527] It aims to commission them early (the first ASEV in FY2027 and the second in FY

[6528] These ASEVs will be equipped with Standard Missile (SM)-6 capable of responding to HGVs and others at the terminal phase, as well as with various warfare and mobile capabilities equivalent to or above those of existing Aegis-equipped destroyers

[6529] They will also be designed to be resistant to rolling, more habitable with personal spaces, and expandable so as to enable them to operate future equipment

[6530] In addition, the ASEVs will save the necessary number of crew by some 20% compared with existing Aegis-equipped destroyers

[6531] Part III, Chapter 1, Section 4-2 (Response to Missile Attacks

[6532] Aegis System-Equipped Vessels Improving the resiliency of existing SDF facilities such as SDF camps and bases across Japan SDF facilities are the foundation for the sustainability and resiliency of Japan’s defense capabilities; therefore, it is important to ensure their sufficient functioning

[6533] Because about 40% of SDF facilities were built during periods when the old earthquake resistance standards were in effect, it is urgently required to improve the resiliency of existing facilities so as to ensure the safety of SDF personnel on a daily basis and prevent the easy loss of operational capabilities even in a contingency

[6534] For this reason, the MOD/SDF already began in FY2023 to work on developing a master plan for improving the resiliency of more than 20,000 SDF buildings across Japan

[6535] Under this master plan, the MOD/SDF plans to start making such improvements in FY

[6536] In the process, improvements will also be made to the living and work environments for uniformed SDF personnel

[6537] Part III, Chapter 1, Section 6-4 (Improving the Resiliency of Facilities

[6541] Material expenses are also referred to as "program expenses," and since general material expenses include repair costs for equipment, education and training expenses for personnel, and the purchase of fuel, they are referred to also as "activity expenses

[6555] Classification by purpose of use

[6556] By purpose of use, defense-related expenditures are broadly classified into “personnel and food provision expenses,” which cover items such as wages and meals for SDF personnel; “equipment procurement expenses,” which cover the procurement of new equipment (e.g., tanks, destroyers, fighter aircraft, etc.); “maintenance expenses,” which cover items such as training and education of SDF personnel, fuel for vessels and aircraft, and equipment repairs; “facility improvement expenses,” which cover the construction of buildings such as aircraft hangars and barracks; and “research and development expenses,” which cover investments in cutting-edge technologies

[6557] In the defense-related expenditures for FY2024, as in those for FY2023, the combined total of expenses for equipment procurement and research and development exceeds 20% of the total defense-related expenditure, while the percentage of equipment maintenance and other expenses has also increased

[6663] Defense Buildup and Defense Budget

[6664] Security-related Expenses

[6665] In the National Security Strategy of Japan, which was formulated in December 2022, Japan has decided to take the necessary measures to make the level of its budget, for both the fundamental reinforcement of defense capabilities and complementary initiatives, reach 2% (about ¥11 trillion) of the current GDP (estimated at some ¥560 trillion for fiscal 2022), through building on the contents of necessary defense capabilities, and by taking into account indexes of international comparison, with a view to coordination with its ally, likeminded countries and others

[6666] NATO member countries and other countries have committed to spending under their defense budget that is commensurate with their respective economic capabilities in order to maintain the security environment

[6667] In the case of Japan, looking at its defense budget as a percentage of GDP has a certain significance as an indicator for the reinforcement of its defense capabilities in light of changes in the security environment within the international community

[6668] With this understanding, the government has decided to set a 2-percent target for FY2027 for the combined budget level for the fundamental reinforcement of defense capabilities and other supplementary measures (security-related expenses

[6669] Of the combined budget, DBP-related expenditures as part of expenditures for the fundamental reinforcement of defense capabilities are expected to amount to some ¥8.9 trillion yen for FY

[6670] Expenditures for complementary initiatives are calculated based on the items the past administrations have adopted to provisionally estimate security-related expenditures while using the NATO definition for reference

[6671] Of such expenditures, SACO-related expenses and the portion of U. S. Forces realignment-related expenses that is aimed at mitigating the impact on local communities are estimated at about ¥0.2 trillion

[6672] The portion borne by relevant ministries and agencies is estimated at around ¥0.9 trillion given the JCG budget and PKO-related expenses

[6673] Expenditures for measures to reinforce the comprehensive defense architecture—R&D, public infrastructure development, cybersecurity, and international cooperation not least for enhancing the deterrence of Japan and like-minded countries—are approximately estimated at ¥1 trillion

[6674] Estimating the portion of security-related expenditures borne by relevant ministries and agencies involves the moot issue of which specific expenditures contribute to Japan's defense

[6675] Yet the government has calculated this portion based on the items the past administrations have adopted to provisionally estimate security-related expenditures while using the NATO definition for reference

[6676] The calculation assumes that this portion includes (i) expenditures related to military and civilian veterans and the weapons of the former Japanese military, such as pension expenditures and expenditures related to ammunition disposal; (ii) PKO-related expenditures, such as contributions to the U.N.'s PKO; (iii) expenditures for security-related organizations, such as the JCG and the Cabinet Satellite Intelligence Center; (iv) SDF-related expenditures, such as personnel expenses for defense attachés; and (v) expenditures related to the stationing of the U. S. Forces in Japan, such as base subsidies

[6677] Of the measures to reinforce the comprehensive defense architecture, the government will promote R&D of science and technology that contributes to the enhancement of the comprehensive defense architecture by matching R&D needs based on the views of the Ministry of Defense (MOD) with the appropriate technological seeds possessed by relevant ministries and agencies

[6678] With regard to public infrastructure development, the government will develop airports and seaports as necessary based on the needs of the SDF and the JCG to ensure their smooth utilization and deployment on a steady-state basis for effective response in light of the security environment

[6679] As for cybersecurity, the government plans to improve its overall response capabilities to or above the levels of leading Western countries

[6680] This involves the introduction of active cyber defense

[6681] The government is now considering what specific measures to take, with the Cabinet Secretariat playing the central role

[6682] Measures for international cooperation are best represented by Official Security Assistance (OSA), a new grant aid framework that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has created to help like-minded countries reinforce their security capabilities and deterrence

[6683] The MOD/SDF will work closely with OSA in such areas as the transfer of defense equipment and technology

[6686] Japan’s Security and Defense

[6687] Section 1 National Security Council

[6688] Japan’s security environment is the most severe and complex since the end of World War II, and the security challenges that it needs to address are becoming more serious

[6689] Under such circumstances, it is necessary to carry forward the policies pertaining to national security from a strategic perspective under strong political leadership with the Prime Minister at its core

[6690] For this reason, the National Security Council, which was established in the Cabinet to provide a platform to discuss important matters with regard to Japan’s security, has been serving as a control tower for foreign, defense, and economic policies pertaining to national security

[6691] Since its establishment in December 2013, the Council has met 338 times (as of the end of March

[6692] The NSS, NDS, and DBP formulated in December 2022 have also been deliberated and approved in this National Security Council

[6693] The National Security Secretariat established within the Cabinet Secretariat provides constant support to the National Security Council as its secretariat

[6694] The Secretariat is also tasked with the planning, design, and overall coordination of basic guidelines and important matters with regard to foreign, defense, and economic policies pertaining to national security

[6695] The Secretariat is provided with human resources and information by the ministries and agencies closely related in terms of policy

[6696] There are many civilians and uniformed personnel seconded from the Ministry of Defense (MOD) engaging in the planning and design of policies, with their expertise

[6697] In addition, information on global military trends and other matters is provided from the MOD/SDF in a timely manner

[6698] The enhanced ability to formulate national security policies has led to the systematic alignment of Japan’s national security, and to the provision of a direction for policies with regard to new security challenges

[6699] Furthermore, individual defense policies are formulated and efforts to accelerate decision-making are made based on the basic guidelines discussed at the National Security Council, and this is contributing significantly to improved development and implementation of policies within the MOD/SDF

[6836] Section 2 Organization of the MOD/Self-Defense Forces (SDF

[6837] Systems to Support the Minister of Defense

[6838] The Minister of Defense takes charge of and manages the matters related to the defense of Japan as the competent minister, and is in overall charge of the SDF duties in accordance with the provisions of the SDF Law

[6839] The Minister is supported by the State Minister of Defense, the Parliamentary Vice-Ministers of Defense (two), and the Senior Adviser to the Minister of Defense

[6840] There are also the Special Advisers to the Minister of Defense, who advise the Minister of Defense, and the Defense Council, which deliberates on basic principles concerning affairs under the Ministry’s jurisdiction

[6841] Furthermore, the Administrative Vice-Minister of Defense, who organizes and supervises the administrative affairs of each bureau and organization to support the Minister of Defense, and the Vice-Minister of Defense for International Affairs, who is responsible for the overall coordination of duties such as those related to international affairs

[6842] Moreover, the Internal Bureaus of the MOD, Joint Staff, Ground Staff Office, Maritime Staff Office, Air Staff Office, and the Acquisition, Technology and Logistics Agency (ATLA), as an external bureau, have been established in the MOD

[6843] The Internal Bureaus of the MOD are responsible for basic policy relating to the duties of the MOD/SDF

[6844] The Minister’s Secretariat and the Directors-General of each Bureau within the Internal Bureaus, along with the Commissioner of ATLA who is in charge of defense equipment administration, support the Minister of Defense by providing assistance from a policy perspective

[6845] The Joint Staff is a staff organization for the Minister of Defense concerning the operation of the SDF

[6846] The Chief of Joint Staff provides centralized support for the operations of the SDF for the Minister of Defense from a military expert’s perspective

[6847] The Ground Staff, Maritime Staff and Air Staff are the staff organizations for the Minister of Defense concerning their respective services except operations of the SDF, with the Chiefs of Staff for the Ground Self-Defense Force (GSDF), the Maritime Self-Defense Force (MSDF) and the Air Self-Defense Force (ASDF) acting as the top ranking expert advisers to the Minister of Defense regarding these services

[6848] In this manner, the MOD has ensured that the support for the Minister from a policy perspective and the support for the Minister from a military expert’s perspective are provided in a well-balanced manner like the two wheels of a cart, so to speak, in order for the Minister of Defense to appropriately make decisions

[6849] REFER Chapter 1, Section 2-3-4 (Securing Civilian Control

[6850] Base of Defense Administration in Regional Areas

[6851] The MOD has Regional Defense Bureaus in eight locations across the country (Sapporo City, Sendai City, Saitama City, Yokohama City, Osaka City, Hiroshima City, Fukuoka City, and Kadena Town) as its local branches in charge of comprehensive defense administration

[6852] In addition to implementing measures to promote harmony between defense facilities and regional societies and inspecting equipment, the Regional Defense Bureaus adopt various measures to obtain the understanding and cooperation of both local governments and local residents towards the activities of the MOD/SDF

[6853] Part IV, Chapter 4, Section 1 (Measures to Harmonize with Local Communities and the Environment

[6854] In order to rapidly and effectively fulfill the duties of the SDF, the MOD/SDF has adopted the joint operations system in which the GSDF, the MSDF, and the ASDF are operated integrally

[6855] Furthermore, it works towards building an architecture that is capable of realizing cross-domain operations in domains such as space, cyberspace and the electromagnetic spectrum

[6856] The Joint Staff is responsible for joint operations of the SDF

[6857] It is headed by the Chief of Joint Staff, who develops a joint operations concept for SDF operations, and centrally supports the Minister of Defense on SDF operations from a military expert’s perspective

[6858] The Minister of Defense’s commands concerning the operations of the SDF are delivered through the Chief of Joint Staff, and the Minister of Defense’s orders concerning operations of the SDF are executed by the Chief of Joint Staff

[6859] In doing this, the Defense Minister’s commands and orders are delivered through the Chief of Joint Staff not only in cases where a joint task force

[6860] is organized, but also in cases where a single SDF unit is employed to respond

[6861] The Joint Staff undertakes functions relating to the operations of the SDF, while the Ground, Maritime and Air Staff Offices undertake functions for unit maintenance, such as personnel affairs, building-up defense capability, and education and training

[6862] The NDS and DBP call for the establishment of a permanent Joint Headquarters that facilitates the centralized command of each SDF service

[6863] The aim is to build a system that is capable of seamless cross-domain operations at all phases from peacetime to contingencies, with the aim of strengthening the effectiveness of joint operations of the Ground, Maritime, and Air SDF services

[6864] To this end, the MOD/SDF will establish the SDF Joint Operations Command (JJOC) in Ichigaya as a permanent Joint Headquarters, which will be headed by the Commander, SDF Joint Operations Command (C-JJOC

[6884] Two or more units from GSDF, MSDF, and/or ASDF are temporarily organized as an ad hoc joint task force, as needed, under the current absence of a permanent Joint Headquarters to conduct joint operations

[6885] Under such an arrangement, however, the SDF cannot quickly develop a flexible defense posture in response to the state of the situation and its developments

[6886] It is also difficult to put in place a posture needed for cross-domain operations from peacetime

[6887] The JJOC will centrally command joint operations by the GSDF, MSDF, and ASDF from peacetime

[6888] Its ability to train cross-domain operations from peacetime will improve the effectiveness of joint operations and enable prompt response to contingencies and decision-making constantly

[6889] Currently, the Chief of Joint Staff coordinates with the U.S. counterparts, namely the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, who is in charge of longer-term military strategies, as well as the Commander of the U.S. Indo-Pacific Command, who is in charge of joint operations between the SDF and U.S. Forces

[6890] The JJOC will enable closer coordination with U. S. Forces and stronger Japan-U. S. joint response capabilities

[6891] Relations between the JJOC and the Joint Staff

[6892] The Joint Staff is a staff organization that supports the Minister of Defense with regard to the operation of the SDF from a military expert’s perspective

[6893] The JJOC, on the other hand, is a unit designed to centrally command GSDF, MSDF, and ASDF units across Japan from peacetime, which was not a permanent function of the SDF until now

[6894] Thus, the JJOC and the Joint Staff are organizations with different purpose and position, and the role of the Joint Staff will not change with the establishment of the JJOC

[6895] As to the current operation of the SDF, the commands of the Minister of Defense are conducted via the Chief of Joint Staff whereas the orders of the Minister of Defense are executed by the Chief of Joint Staff

[6896] Even after the JJOC is established, the Chief of Joint Staff will continue to convey the commands and orders of the Minister of Defense regarding the operation of the SDF to the JJOC and other units and give detailed guidance within such purview

[6897] In this way, clear lines of responsibility will be drawn between the JJOC and its commander on one hand and the Joint Staff and its chief on the other

[6898] The establishment of the JJOC and its new function of centrally operating GSDF, MSDF, and ASDF units across the country from peacetime will improve the effectiveness of joint operations and enable prompt response to contingencies and decision-making constantly

[6899] Commentary/Deepening the SDF’s Joint Operations System

[6900] Aiming for a comprehensive and effective administration of the SDF for joint SDF operations, the Joint Staff Council comprising a Chairman and the Chiefs of Staff of the GSDF, MSDF and ASDF was established in July 1954 at the time of the foundation of the Defense Agency and the SDF

[6901] Based on this, the Internal Bureau of the Defense Agency assisted the Minister of State for Defense in his command responsibilities mainly from policy perspective, while each Chief of Staff and the Joint Staff Council did so mainly from military perspective

[6902] However, the Chiefs of Staff of the GSDF, MSDF, and ASDF all provided their own expert military advice to the Minister of State for Defense independently, with the Joint Staff Council providing coordination as a council organization when necessary

[6903] In other words, it was a posture in which operations by each SDF service were the norm

[6904] After that, there were changes in the environment surrounding the SDF

[6905] For example, the SDF was required to deal with new threats and diverse contingencies

[6906] Recognizing that, in order to swiftly and effectively respond to these changes, the SDF must adopt a posture in which the GSDF, MSDF, and ASDF can conduct operations in a systematic and coordinated fashion during normal conditions, the government established the posture required for Joint operations, including the creation of the Joint Staff, the transfer of operational functions from the Staff Offices of the GSDF, MSDF and ASDF to the Joint Staff, and the integration of intelligence functions into the Defense Intelligence Headquarters

[6907] In March 2006, the SDF posture was shifted to the joint operations system, a posture in which joint operations are the norm

[6908] This shift integrated the functions of supporting the Minister of Defense from a military expert's perspective

[6909] At the SDF unit level, however, the Joint operations system translated into a joint task force organized to carry out a specific duty under Article 22, paragraph 1 or 2 of the Self-Defense Forces Law

[6910] The SDF had yet to be able to adopt a posture in which the GSDF, MSDF, and ASDF can conduct operations in a systematic and coordinated fashion during normal conditions

[6911] The Joint Staff Council held the first meeting in

[6912] This applies to cases in which a special unit is organized to carry out a specific duty or when the required troops are placed partly under the authority of a commander outside of their usual command structure based on the stipulations of Article 22, paragraphs 1 or 2 of the Self-Defense Forces Law, and refers to units made up of two or more units from the GSDF, MSDF, or ASDF

[6913] In order to swiftly and effectively execute various missions such as responding to ballistic missiles and large-scale disasters, it is necessary to operate the GSDF, MSDF, and ASDF in an integrated manner

[6914] To achieve this, a joint task force spanning the GSDF, MSDF, and ASDF is organized under a single commander

[6915] In order to deal simultaneously with a contingency and a disaster, it is possible to organize a joint task force separately even after the JOC is established

[6916] This was where the Medium Term Defense Program (FY 2019 - FY 2023) came in

[6917] This program stated: “For the future framework for joint operations, SDF will take necessary measures after considering how to conduct the operation of organizations in which the functions in the new domains are operated unitarily, and come to conclusions after considering how the integrated structure should be during steady-state to appropriately execute instructions from the Minister based on the posture of the strengthened Joint Staff.”

[6918] Based on such consideration, the Defense Buildup Program endorsed by the Cabinet in December 2022 stated: "a permanent Joint Headquarters will be established in order to build a system capable of seamlessly conducting cross-domain operations at all stages from peacetime to contingency, with the aim of strengthening the effectiveness of joint operations among each SDF services

[6919] This was how the Joint Operations Command came to be established

[6921] Chapter

[6922] Framework for the SDF Activities

[6923] Article 3 in the Self-Defense Forces Law divides the duties of the Self-Defense Forces into main duties (item 1 of the same article) and secondary duties (items 1 and 2 of the same article

[6924] Defense Operations to defend Japan correspond to main duties, which only the Self-Defense Forces can carry out

[6925] Secondary duties consist of “duties for maintaining public order as necessary” (secondary duties under item 1) and duties defined by other laws “to an extent that does not interfere with performance of the main duties” (secondary duties under item

[6926] The former includes public security operations that police entities cannot handle alone, maritime security operations, destruction measures against ballistic missiles and other weapons, disaster relief dispatches, and measures against intrusion of territorial airspace

[6927] The latter covers responses to Important Influence Situations and international peace cooperation activities

[6928] These main and secondary duties are jointly known as “primary missions

[6929] Armed Attack Situations/Anticipated Attack Situations and Survival-Threatening Situations

[6930] The Armed Attack Situation Response Act is aimed at establishing a system to respond to Armed Attack Situations or Anticipated Armed Attack Situations and Survival-Threatening Situations, thereby contributing to the peace and independence of Japan as well as the safety of the country and the people

[6931] The Act specifies items that should be stipulated as basic principles and basic policies (the Basic Response Plan), as well as the responsibilities of national and local governments, for responding to Armed Attack Situations/Anticipated Armed Attack Situations, and Survival-Threatening Situations

[6932] The Government will take action in accordance with the Act in the event of an armed attack, such as a missile attack on Japan or an invasion of its remote islands as described below in Part III, Chapter 1, Section 4, or an armed attack against a foreign country that is in a close relationship with Japan, which as a result, threatens Japan’s survival and poses a clear danger of fundamentally overturning Japanese people’s right to life, liberty, and pursuit of happiness

[6933] When an Armed Attack Situation/Anticipated Armed Attack Situation or a Survival-Threatening Situation occurs, the Government will make a Cabinet decision on a Basic Response Plan based on the Armed Attack Situation

[6946] Act on the Peace and Independence of Japan and Maintenance of the Nation and the People's Security in Armed Attack Situations/Anticipated Armed Attack Situations, and Survival-Threatening Situations

[6947] “Armed Attack Situations” refers to situations in which an armed attack against Japan from outside occurs or in which it is recognized that clear danger of an armed attack against Japan from outside is imminent

[6948] “Anticipated Armed Attack Situations” refers to situations that are not yet an armed attack situations but in which circumstances are critical and an armed attack against Japan is anticipated

[6949] Survival-Threatening Situations “Survival-Threatening Situations” means situations where an armed attack against a foreign country that is in a close relationship with Japan occurs, which as a result, threatens Japan's survival and poses a clear danger of fundamentally overturning Japanese people's right to life, liberty and pursuit of happiness

[6954] The reason why there are no other appropriate means available to ensure Japan’s survival and protect its people, and the use of force is necessary to respond to the situation when the situation is confirmed as an Armed Attack Situation/Anticipated Armed Attack Situation or a Survival-Threatening Situation

[6955] Important matters related to the response measures include the issuance of Defense Operation orders or requests for Diet approval to issue such orders, as described below, in the event of an Armed Attack Situation, or a Survival-Threatening Situation

[6969] Responses of the SDF

[6970] The Prime Minister can issue a Defense Operation order to the whole or part of the SDF when it is deemed necessary for the defense of Japan in Armed Attack Situations and Survival-Threatening Situations

[6971] Prior Diet approval is required for a Defense Operation order in principle

[6972] The SDF under Defense Operation duty is allowed to exercise the use of force only when the Three Conditions for “the Use of Force” are satisfied

[6973] Civil Protection

[6974] The Civil Protection Law specifies the responsibilities of the national and local governments as well as measures for evacuating residents, providing relief to evacuated residents, and responding to armed attack disasters in order to protect the lives, bodies, and property of the people and to minimize the impact on the livelihood of the people in an Armed Attack Situation/Anticipated Armed Attack Situation and during an emergency response

[6975] If the Minister of Defense deems it unavoidable after receiving a request from prefectural governors or a request from the Task Force Chief5, the Minister of Defense may order SDF units and organizations6 upon approval from the Prime Minister, to implement civil protection measures or emergency response protection measures (including assisting with the evacuation of and immediate restoration

[6983] The Prime Minister assumes the position of the Director of the Crisis Management Headquarters, but these positions are regulated as separate entities

[6984] Units and organizations of the GSDF, MSDF, or ASDF

[6985] Maintenance of Public Order and to an Armed Attack 1 Public Security Operations (1) Public Security Operations by Order

[6986] In the event of an indirect aggression or other emergency situations, the Prime Minister can order the whole or part of the SDF to deploy if it is deemed impossible to maintain public security with the general police force

[6987] In this instance, in principle, the Prime Minister must bring the order to the Diet for deliberation, and request for its approval within twenty days from the day the order has been given

[6988] Public Security Operations by Request

[6989] The governor of a prefecture, upon consulting with the Public Safety Commission of the prefecture, can request the Prime Minister to dispatch units and organizations of the SDF if is deemed unavoidable as the situation will have a serious influence on public security

[6990] Following such a request, the Prime Minister can order the SDF to mobilize when the situation calls for such action

[6991] Maritime Security Operations

[6992] When there is a special need to protect lives or property or maintain public security at sea,8 the Minister of Defense can order the SDF units to take necessary actions at sea upon approval by the Prime Minister

[6993] Part I, Chapter 1, Section 3-2 (Measures against Violations of Japan’s Sovereignty) 3 Counter-Piracy Operations

[6994] When there is a special need to respond to acts of piracy, the Minister of Defense may order SDF units to conduct operations under the Counter-Piracy Measures Act to deal with piracy acts at sea upon approval by the Prime Minister

[6995] Part II, Chapter 3, Section 2-2 (Counter-Piracy Operations) Destruction Measures against Ballistic Missiles or Other Objects

[6996] In cases where ballistic missiles or other objects are flying to Japan as an armed attack or flying to Japan in a Survival-Threatening Situation, and where the “Three Conditions” are met, the SDF can respond with the defense operation

[6997] In cases where ballistic missiles or other objects are flying to Japan but which are not found as an armed attack, the Minister of Defense can take the following measures: (1) If the Minister of Defense judges that ballistic missiles or other objects are likely to fly to Japan and that it is necessary to prevent damage to human lives and property due to its fall in the territory of Japan, the Minister, upon the approval of the Prime Minister, can order the SDF units to take measures to destroy the ballistic missiles or other objects actually flying to the country in the airspace over the territory of Japan or the high seas

[6998] In addition to the cases of (1), there may be cases where the situation suddenly changes with little information available on the launch, for example, and the Minister of Defense cannot have time to obtain approval from the Prime Minister

[6999] In preparation for such cases, the Minister of Defense may create an emergency response manual beforehand and obtain approval from the Prime Minister

[7000] Following the emergency response manual, the Minister of Defense can order, for a specified period of time, the SDF units to take measures to destroy ballistic missiles or other objects in the airspace over the territory of Japan or the high seas when such objects are actually flying to the country

[7015] Disaster Relief Dispatches and Others (1) Disaster Relief Dispatches

[7016] Prefectural governors or other officials may request the Minister of Defense, or an officer designated by the Minister, to dispatch SDF units, etc., in the event of a disaster if they deem such a dispatch necessary in order to protect lives or property

[7017] Upon such a request, the Minister or the designated officer will, in principle, make a judgment based on a comprehensive evaluation of three conditions—urgency, non-substitutability, and public nature—and dispatch the units if it is deemed necessary for the SDF to respond to the disaster

[7018] This procedure is based on the idea that prefectural governors and other officials should grasp the overall conditions of the disaster and their own disaster relief capabilities first, and then decide whether to make a request for the SDF disaster relief dispatch

[7019] However, under circumstances of particular urgency when there is no time to wait for a request, the Minister of Defense or the designated officer may discretionarily dispatch units, etc. without waiting for such a request

[7020] In cases where emergency patients need to be transported from the sea, remote islands or elsewhere but both the Japan Coast Guard (JCG) and the local governments concerned have difficulty in dealing with the situation, the SDF conducts an emergency airlift of such patients under the framework of disaster relief dispatches

[7021] Earthquake Disaster Prevention Dispatch and Nuclear Disaster Relief Dispatch

[7022] When a warning declaration is issued based on the Act on Special Measures Concerning Countermeasures for Large-Scale Earthquakes, or when a declaration of a nuclear emergency situation is issued based on the Act on Special Measures Concerning Nuclear Emergency Preparedness, the Minister of Defense is authorized to order the dispatch of units upon the request of the Director of the Seismic Disaster Warning Headquarters or the Director of the Nuclear Disaster Countermeasures Headquarters (the Prime Minister in either case

[7023] Fig

[7024] Flow of a Disaster Relief Dispatch); (Response to Large-Scale Disasters, etc

[7025] The Commandant of the Japan Coast Guard, the Director General of the Regional Coast Guard Headquarters, and the Director of the Airport Administrative Office may request a disaster relief dispatch

[7026] With regard to disaster relief dispatch, earthquake disaster prevention dispatch, and nuclear disaster relief dispatch, (1) SDF personnel ordered for the dispatch may take measures such as evacuation (Article 4 of the Police Duties Execution Law) based on Article 94 of the SDF Law (Authority in Disaster Relief Dispatch, etc.); (2) SDF Reserve Personnel and SDF Ready Reserve Personnel may be called up for service in the event of disaster relief dispatch, and SDF Ready Personnel in the event of earthquake disaster prevention dispatch or nuclear disaster relief dispatch; and (3) special units may be temporarily formed as necessary

[7027] Most notably, the commanding officers of SDF units, etc. across Japan are designed as such in consideration of convenience for prefectural governors, etc. when they make such a request

[7028] Disasters include not only natural disasters such as storms, torrential rains, tremendous snowfalls, floods, storm surges, earthquakes, and tsunamis, but also human-caused disasters such as fires, maritime accidents, aircraft crashes, and train accidents

[7029] The Prime Minister issues an earthquake alert with the endorsement of the Cabinet in the event that an earthquake prediction is reported by the Director-General of the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and when it is deemed necessary to urgently implement emergency earthquake disaster prevention measures

[7040] Measures against Intrusion of Territorial Airspace

[7041] The Minister of Defense may order SDF units to take the necessary measures to make the intruding aircraft land or withdraw from the territorial airspace of Japan (by guiding intruders away, issuing radio transmission warnings, using weapons, etc

[7042] when a foreign aircraft intrudes Japan’s territorial airspace in violation of international law, the provisions of the Aviation Law, or other relevant laws and regulations

[7043] It is a violation of Japanese airspace when objects of foreign countries, even if they are unmanned aircraft (including balloons), intrude into our airspace without permission

[7044] The

[7045] Japanese Government has traditionally considered that the use of weapons during scrambles responding to intrusions into Japanese airspace is permissible only when such measures fall under the requirements of legitimate self-defense or necessity, assuming that such intrusions are made by manned and military aircraft

[7046] Given that the use of weapons against unmanned aircraft, including balloons that intrude into Japanese airspace, would not directly harm people, the Japanese Government in

[7047] February 2023 clarified its interpretation of Article 84 of the Self-Defense Forces Law, which concerns the use of weapons against unmanned aircraft, as follows: In such a case where the safety of aircraft cannot be ensured if the situation left as it is, and when deemed necessary to use weapons to protect legal interests, such as the lives and property of people within Japanese territory as well as the safety of aircraft flying along air routes, such use of weapons can be permitted even if such use does not fall under the requirements of legitimate self-defense or necessity

[7048] Rescue and Transportation of Japanese

[7049] Nationals and Others Overseas

[7050] The Minister of Defense can transport Japanese nationals and others in need of life or physical protection to a safe area if requested by the Minister for Foreign Affairs in the event of emergency situation in a foreign country

[7051] To date, the Japanese Government has amended the

[7052] SDF Law three times

[7053] The latest amendment—which was made in 2022 considering the experiences including the transportation of Japanese nationals and others from Afghanistan—involved removing restrictions on the means of transportation, reviewing the safety requirements for implementation, and expanding the scope of primary transportation recipients

[7054] The Minister of Defense can also rescue Japanese nationals and others by protecting or recovering them upon request from and consultation with the Minister for

[7055] Foreign Affairs if there is a threat of harm to life or body and all of the following are satisfied: - Competent authorities of the country concerned are currently working on maintaining public safety and order, and no acts of combat are confirmed to take place in the areas where rescue measures are taken; - The country concerned provides consent for the

[7056] SDF to take the rescue measures (including the use of weapons); and - Coordination and cooperation with the competent authorities of the country concerned is expected to be ensured to carry out the rescue measures as smoothly and safely as possible in response to anticipated dangers

[7113] Situations and Survival-Threatening

[7114] Situations

[7115] While both Important Influence Situations and Survival-Threatening Situations are different legal concepts that are determined separately based on the requirements set forth in the respective laws, they share common standards such as the likelihood of Japan being embroiled in a war or the extent of damage to Japanese nationals

[7116] Therefore, Survival-Threatening Situations may be conceptually subsumed under Important Influence

[7117] Situations

[7230] Chapter 1 Japan’s Own Architecture for

[7231] National Defense

[7232] Fundamental Reinforcement of Japan’s Defense

[7233] Capabilities and Reinforcing the Defense Architecture of the Whole Country

[7234] Fundamental Reinforcement of Japan’s Defense Capabilities

[7235] The most consequential responsibility of the Government of Japan and the basis of Japan’s national security, is to resolutely defend to the end the lives of Japanese nationals and their peaceful livelihoods as well as Japan’s territorial land, airspace and waters

[7236] When threats materialize through a combination of capability and intention, difficulties arise in accurately ascertaining another party’s intention from an outside perspective

[7237] In addition, if a nation’s decision-making process is opaque, there will always exist conditions under which threats may materialize

[7238] In order to defend one’s own country from a nation with powerful military capabilities and the intention to launch aggression, it is necessary to have deterrence capabilities that make the other nation realize the difficulties of achieving unilateral changes to the status quo by force

[7239] It is also necessary to build one’s own capabilities, namely, defense capabilities, by focusing on the other nation’s capabilities and ensuring it does not harbor the intention to commit aggression

[7240] In addition to traditional forms of invasion through air, sea and land conducted now, new ways of warfare have emerged that combine large-scale missile attacks by ballistic and cruise missiles with enhanced precision strike capabilities; hybrid warfare, including information warfare such as false flag operations; the domains of space, cyber and electromagnetic spectrum as well as asymmetric means of attack that leverage unmanned assets; and rhetoric that could be interpreted as open threats involving the use of nuclear weapons by nuclear weapon states

[7241] Amid the most challenging and complex security environment since the start of the postwar period

[7242] Japan needs to directly face up to the grim reality and fundamentally reinforce its defense capabilities, with a focus on the capabilities of its opponents and new ways of warfare, to protect the lives and peaceful livelihoods of Japanese nationals

[7243] Defense capabilities of Japan and the ultimate guarantor of Japan’s national security

[7244] They serve to deter threats to Japan and should a threat to Japan arise, to block and eliminate the threat, thereby demonstrating Japan’s will and ability to defend itself to the end

[7245] Based on this recognition, the National Defense Strategy of Japan (NDS) presents three defense objectives and three approaches to achieve them, as shown in Fig

[7246] III

[7247] Fig

[7255] Fundamental Reinforcement of Japan's Defense Capabilities and Reinforcing the Defense Architecture of the Whole Country

[7256] Strengthening of Japan's Own Architecture for National Defense 3 Reinforcing collaboration with Like-minded Countries and Others to ensure the peace, stability and prosperity of the international community as a whole, including those to strategically promote multilateral and multilayered security cooperation and those to ensure maritime security and for international peace cooperation activities, arms control, disarmament and non-proliferation

[7257] Reinforcing the Defense Architecture of the Whole Country

[7258] The SDF must be strong in order to protect Japan, but national defense cannot be achieved without a whole-of-country approach

[7259] For this reason, besides the fundamental reinforcement of its defense capabilities, Japan will develop a defense architecture for the whole country by integrating its national power, which includes its diplomatic, intelligence, economic and technological capabilities and systematically combining various policy means

[7260] To strengthen such whole-of-government efforts, it is essential to break down the stove-piping approach within the Government

[7261] As part of this initiative, the government of Japan is reinforcing its comprehensive defense architecture as a complement to and an inseparable part of the fundamental enhancement of its defense capabilities and is promoting initiatives in four areas: (1) research and development (R&D), (2) public infrastructure development, (3) cybersecurity and (4) international cooperation to enhance the deterrence capabilities of

[7262] Japan and its like-minded countries and others, under the framework of relevant government agencies

[7348] Section 2 Shaping a Security Environment that does not Tolerate Unilateral Changes to the Status Quo by Force

[7349] The primary object of the National Defense Strategy (NDS) is to shape a security environment that does not tolerate unilateral changes to the status quo by force

[7350] An important part of measures to prevent unilateral changes to the status quo by force is diplomatic efforts backed by the strengthening of Japan’s own defense architecture

[7351] Coupled with diplomatic efforts, the Ministry of Defense (MOD)/Self Defense Forces (SDF) will promote cooperation with the ally and multilayered coordination with like-minded countries to create a desirable security environment

[7352] As a maritime nation, it is extremely important for Japan to reinforce the maritime order and ensure the freedom and safety of navigation and overflight

[7353] For this reason, Japan implements necessary measures for the safety of Japan-related vessels in order to ensure the stable use of its vital sea lanes

[7354] Chapter 2 (Japan-U. S. Alliance); Chapter 3 (Collaboration with Like-Minded Countries and Others); Part IV, Chapter 1, Section 3 (Promoting Defense Equipment and Technology Cooperation and Transfer of Defense Equipment

[7355] Response to Illicit Ship-to-Ship Transfers 1. Basic Concept

[7356] Under the UN Security Council resolution No. 2375 adopted in September 2017, UN member states are prohibited from facilitating or engaging in the transfer of goods at sea to or from North Korean-flagged vessels (so-called "illicit ship-to-ship transfers

[7357] This is intended to prevent North Korea from smuggling to evade sanctions imposed based on the UN Security Council resolution

[7358] Toward the common goal of the complete, verifiable and irreversible denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula, Japan needs to work closely with the international community, including China and Russia, as well as the United States and South Korea, to ensure the effectiveness of the UN Security Council resolutions, including responses to “illicit ship-to-ship transfers”

[7359] Response by the MOD/SDF

[7360] The Ministry of Defense/Self-Defense Forces (SDF) has the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (MSDF) gather information on vessels suspected of violating the UN Security Council resolution as part of its regular monitoring and surveillance activities in the waters surrounding Japan and cooperates closely with relevant ministries and agencies, relevant countries and relevant international organizations

[7361] During the period from 2018 onward to the end of March 2024, MSDF vessels and other assets have so far observed 24 cases of seaborne rendezvous between North Korean-flagged tankers and foreign-flagged tankers, etc. on the high seas of the East China Sea

[7362] The information was shared with relevant agencies and ministries each time

[7363] As a result of comprehensive judgment across the Government, the vessels concerned are strongly suspected of having engaged in "illicit ship-to-ship transfers" with North Korean-flagged vessels, which is prohibited by UN Security Council resolutions

[7364] Japan reported this to the UN Security Council Sanctions Committee on North Korea, shared the information with relevant countries, gave information to the relevant countries regarding the tankers concerned and made public announcements on the subject

[7365] In recent years, there has been growing international concern about these illicit maritime activities, including “illicit ship-to-ship transfers” with North Korean-flagged vessels

[7366] Since April 2018 as of the end of March 2024, not only the United States, but also Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, New Zealand, France and Germany have dispatched naval vessels and aircraft in the waters surrounding Japan, including the East China Sea, to conduct monitoring and surveillance activities

[7367] The MOD/SDF will continue their close cooperation with concerned countries to ensure compliance with the UN Security Council resolution

[7368] REFERENCE: Japan's Initiatives to Ensure the Effectiveness of the UN Security Council Resolution

[7374] Information Gathering Activities for Ensuring the Safety of Japan-related Vessels in the Middle East

[7375] Background of the Deployment of the SDF to the Middle East

[7376] Peace and stability in the Middle East are crucial to the peace and prosperity of the international community, including Japan

[7377] In addition, for Japan as well, it is very important to ensure the safety of Japan-related vessels in the Middle East, one of the world’s major energy sources, on which Japan depends for about 90% of its crude oil imports

[7378] In the Middle East, amidst rising tensions, there were incidents of attacks on ships

[7379] In June 2019, Japan-related vessels suffered damage

[7380] Under these circumstances, the United States, European countries and other countries are taking steps to ensure the safety of navigation in the region by utilizing ships and aircraft

[7381] To ease tensions and stabilize the situation in the Middle East, the Japanese Government has actively promoted diplomatic initiatives

[7382] In addition, following deliberations within the Government, in December 2019, the Cabinet approved governmental efforts to ensure the safety of Japan-related vessels

[7383] In this context, Japan’s own initiatives to ensure peace and stability in the Middle East and the safety of Japan-related vessels are as follows: (1) further diplomatic efforts to ease tensions in the Middle East and stabilize the situation; (2) thorough implementation of navigation safety measures, including close information sharing with relevant industries; and (3) conduct information gathering activities via the use of SDF assets

[7384] The areas of operation of these information gathering activities consist of the high seas of three areas of water: the Gulf of Oman, the northern Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Aden to the east of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait (including the Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ) of the coastal states) is to utilize P-3C patrol aircraft of the Deployment Air Force for Counter Piracy Enforcement (DAPE), as well as destroyers of the Deployment Surface Force for Counter Piracy Enforcement (DSPE

[7385] Information gathered by the MOD/SDF is shared with the Cabinet Secretariat, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT), Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) and other relevant ministries and agencies, as well as with relevant industries through public-private liaison meetings, to be used for the government’s navigation safety measures

[7386] Information gathering activities by the MOD/SDF

[7387] The MOD/SDF’s information gathering activities are part of the government’s navigation safety measures and are aimed at collecting information necessary to ensure the safety of Japan-related vessels

[7388] The activities are to be conducted in accordance with the provisions of Article 4, paragraph (1), item (xviii) of the Act for Establishment of the Ministry of Defense, as they would need smooth decision making and order issuance in relation to maritime security operations as measures for unforeseen circumstances or other changes in the situation, which are provided in Article 82 of the Self-Defense Forces Law

[7389] Results of the SDF’s Activities

[7390] In January 2020, P-3C patrol aircraft of the counter-piracy unit began information-gathering activities, followed by a destroyer of the Deployment Surface Force for information-gathering activities in February

[7391] Based on the November 2023 Cabinet decision, one destroyer and one patrol aircraft are conducting both counter-piracy operations and information-gathering activities

[7399] In light of the need to ensure the safety of navigation for Japan-related vessels, if it is deemed before the expiration of the period that activities by the SDF are no longer necessary, then, in addition to concluding these activities at that point and without waiting for the end of the activity period, the National Security Council will consider how to respond if there is a significant change in the situation

[7453] Section

[7454] Responding to Unilateral Changes to the Status Quo by Force and Such Attempts

[7455] The second objective of the National Defense Strategy of Japan (NDS) is for Japan to deter, through cooperation with our ally, like-minded countries and others, unilateral changes to the status quo by force and such attempts that concern Japan’s peace and security

[7456] In addition, in the event of such a situation, Japan will swiftly take action in response, using all possible methods to prevent an invasion of our country and bring the situation under control from an early stage

[7457] To continue demonstrating Japan’s will and capability to deter unilateral changes to the status quo by force and such attempts and to influence the actions of opponents, it is necessary for the nation to improve and reinforce training and exercises conducted as flexible deterrent options (FDO) and strategic communication (SC) with a whole-of-government approach, as well as with its allies, like-minded countries and others

[7458] Moreover, from peacetime, it is important to detect indications at an early stage of situations by implementing persistent intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) as well as analysis while cooperating with relevant ministries and agencies and for the Government as a whole to conduct rapid decision-making depending on the situation with related organizations

[7459] Due to this, Japan is reinforcing its responses by the Government as a whole

[7460] Key Persistent ISR surrounding Japan

[7461] Basic Concept

[7462] Japan comprises just over 14,000 islands, surrounded by wide sea space, which includes the sixth-largest territorial waters (including inland waters) and Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) worldwide

[7463] The SDF is engaged in intelligence collection and monitoring and surveillance during peacetime over Japan’s territorial waters and airspace, as well as the surrounding sea and airspace so that it can respond to various contingencies immediately and seamlessly

[7464] Response by the MOD/SDF

[7465] The Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (MSDF) monitors ships navigating in the waters surrounding Hokkaido, the Sea of Japan and the East China Sea in peacetime, using patrol aircraft and others

[7466] The Japan Air Self-Defense Force (ASDF) uses radar sites at each location nationwide and early warning and control aircraft amongst others, to conduct monitoring and surveillance activities over Japan and its surrounding airspace

[7467] These activities of the MSDF and ASDF happen 24 hours a day

[7468] Monitoring and surveillance activities in major channels are also conducted around the clock by MSDF guard posts, the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force. REFERENCE

[7484] The Senkaku Islands (Ishigaki City, Okinawa Prefecture) are clearly an inherent part of the territory of Japan, both historically and under international law

[7485] Japan actually has effective control of the islands

[7486] Therefore, there is no territorial issue to be resolved in the first place

[7487] After carefully confirming that there were no signs of any other country's control in 1895, the Japanese government decided to put the Senkaku Islands under the jurisdiction of Okinawa Prefecture by legitimate means under international law at a Cabinet meeting and officially incorporated the islands into the territory of Japan

[7488] China began to make its own claims regarding the Senkaku Islands in the 1970s, after a UN agency pointed out possible oil reserves in the East China Sea in

[7489] It had not raised any objections until this point

[7490] Nor had it given any explanation for not having raised any objections

[7491] However, since Chinese government vessels intruded into Japanese territorial waters surrounding the Senkaku Islands for the first time in 2008, such vessels and others have repeatedly intruded into our territorial waters despite our strong protests, which is utterly unacceptable

[7492] The activities of Chinese maritime patrol vessels, which are asserting their own claims in our territorial waters around the Senkaku Islands, are a violation of international law in the first place

[7520] Whole-of-Government Responses (1) General Situation

[7521] To never tolerate unilateral changes to the status quo by force, it is important for the related organizations to cooperate to take action based on decision-making by the Government as a whole during peacetime

[7522] For this reason, the Government as a whole will conduct simulations and integrated training and exercises to improve the effectiveness of responses, while establishing coordination procedures on a regular basis

[7523] In addition, with regard to the protection of critical facilities such as nuclear power plants and response to infringements that do not lead to external armed attacks or armed attack situations in areas surrounding remote islands, Japan will conduct training and exercises between the police, JCG and the MOD/SDF on a regular basis with contingencies in mind

[7524] Reinforcing Coordination with the Japan Coast Guard

[7525] Maintaining maritime security is primarily the mission of the JCG, but in cases that cannot be handled by the JCG, the SDF will also respond through maritime security operations and public security operations in coordination with the JCG

[7551] Measures against Violations of Japan’s Sovereignty

[7552] Warnings and Scrambles in Preparation against Intrusion of Territorial Airspace

[7553] Under international law, countries have complete and exclusive sovereignty over their territorial airspace

[7554] Measures against aircraft intruding into territorial airspace are conducted as an act to exercise the right of policing intended to maintain public order

[7555] Unlike measures taken on land or at sea, these measures can be taken only by the SDF

[7556] Therefore, the ASDF is primarily responsible for conducting the actions based on the provisions of Article 84 of the Self-Defense Forces Law

[7557] Responses by the MOD/SDF

[7558] The ASDF detects and identifies aircraft flying in airspace surrounding Japan using warning and control radars as well as early warning and control aircraft

[7559] If any suspicious aircraft heading to Japan’s territorial airspace are detected, fighters and other aircraft scramble to approach them to confirm the situation and monitor the aircraft as necessary

[7560] Furthermore, in the event that this suspicious aircraft has actually intruded into territorial airspace, a warning to leave the airspace would be issued, among other responses

[7584] Response to Submarines Navigating Underwater in Japan’s Territorial Waters (1) Basic Concept

[7607] Section 4 Responses to Invasions of Japan, Including Missile Attacks

[7608] The third defense objective of the National Defense Strategy (NDS) is, should deterrence fail and invasion of Japan occur, to rapidly respond to the invasion in a tailored and seamless manner; to take primary responsibility to deal with the aggression; and, while receiving support from our ally and others, to disrupt and defeat the invasion

[7609] In response to an invasion of Japan, including our remote islands, Japan would block and eliminate the invading forces from a long distance

[7610] Japan will also acquire superiority across domains and conduct cross-domain operations that organically integrate capabilities in the domains of space, cyber and electromagnetic spectrum as well as in the ground, maritime and air domains to secure asymmetrical superiority and block and eliminate the invading forces

[7611] Japan would also continue persistent actions to crush the opponent’s will to invade

[7612] Moreover, in response to an invasion of Japan, including missile attacks, Japan will intercept missiles on the high seas and over our territory through missile defense

[7613] In addition, as a measure for self-defense to the minimum required level to prevent attacks in cases where no other means are clearly available, Japan will utilize capabilities including stand-off defense capabilities to enable conducting effective counterstrikes in the opponent's territory and together with missile defense, deter missile attacks

[7614] Furthermore, in the event of a large-scale terrorist attack or an attack on critical infrastructure that poses a serious threat to the lives, health and property of Japanese citizens, Japan will cooperate with related organizations to take effective countermeasures

[7615] Moreover, if there were to be a predicted invasion of Japan, Japan will make sure that it is possible to smoothly implement measures for civil protection, including the issuance of evacuation guidance for residents

[7616] Responses to Invasion of Japan, Including Its Remote Islands 1. Basic Concept

[7617] Japan possesses numerous remote islands spanning a broad national territory which extends approximately 3,000 kilometers along both the north-south and east-west axes, across which the Government must protect the lives, health and property of its citizens, as well as its territory, territorial waters, airspace and various resources that are widely dispersed

[7618] To precisely respond to invasions of Japan, which has such geographic characteristics, it is necessary to station units and so forth in accordance with the security environment and also to maintain a readiness to detect signs at an early stage through persistent intelligence gathering and surveillance, etc. by the Self-Defense Forces (SDF

[7619] Moreover, it is important to ensure maritime superiority1 and air superiority2 as well as swiftly maneuver and deploy them according to situations

[7620] If our deterrence were to fail and an invasion of Japan occurred, to eliminate any violation of our territory, Japan would organically integrate our capabilities in the domains of space, cyber and electromagnetic spectrum as well as the ground, maritime and air domains and overcome any inferiority in individual domains through cross-domain operations that amplify our overall capabilities through synergy effects

[7621] Japan would also conduct flexible and sustained activities through joint operations, continue swift and persistent actions, secure our territory and crush the opponent's will to invade

[7624] Initiatives of the MOD/SDF (1) Strengthening of Stand-off Defense Capabilities

[7625] Some foreign countries have significantly improved their radar detection coverage as well as the range and performance of various missiles

[7626] This means that the range of these threats would be over several hundred kilometers around an invading force

[7627] To protect and defend the territory of Japan, it is necessary to improve the level of deterrence against armed attacks on our country by fundamentally strengthening our stand-off defense capabilities, such as anti-aircraft missiles and deal with naval vessels and landing forces invading our country, including islands, from outside the threat zone

[7628] Therefore, no matter which region of Japan an invasion might begin in, firstly the Ministry of Defense (MOD)/Self-Defense Forces (SDF) will equip itself with the necessary and sufficient capabilities to block and eliminate the opponent’s vessels, landing forces and the like from various locations in our country in a multilayered manner

[7629] Also, the MOD/SDF will, while diversifying launch platforms including enabling them to launch missiles from ground-based launchers, aircraft and naval vessels, respond to the situation by combining stand-off missiles, forcing the opponent to make a complex response

[7630] In addition, the MOD/SDF will, while acquiring necessary and sufficient quantities of foreign-made stand-off missiles at an early stage, encourage the expansion of the domestic manufacturing system of made-in-Japan stand-off missiles to acquire necessary and sufficient quantities as soon as possible

[7631] Further, the MOD/SDF will promote initiatives to secure a series of functions necessary to operate stand-off missiles, including the collection of targeting information and command and control

[7632] After building a practical operational capability for stand-off missiles, the MOD/SDF will accelerate research, development and mass production initiatives and swiftly acquire the capability to operate more advanced stand-off missiles

[7633] Specifically, in FY2023, the MOD/SDF began the mass production of Upgraded Type-12 SSM (surface-launched variant) for early deployment to troops

[7634] The initial plan was to deploy them in FY2026, but this has been accelerated by one year and the deployment is to begin in FY

[7635] Further, to ensure survivability, the development of Upgraded Type-12 SSM (surface, ship and air-launched variants) is continuing so that they can be launched from various platforms (ground, naval ship and aircraft

[7639] In addition, the development of Upgraded hyper-velocity gliding projectiles for the defense of remote islands, which began in FY2023, continues

[7640] Further, research into hypersonic missiles has been conducted since FY

[7641] From FY2024, their manufacturing system has been expanded to acquire mass production and others from an early stage and in an effort to extend the range of various guided missiles

[7642] Besides, while utilizing the ground equipment of Upgraded Type-12 SSM, the MOD/SDF will begin to develop new stand-off missiles with improved anti-ship and anti-surface capabilities, such as long-range flying performance, precision guidance performance, etc

[7643] Stand-off Defense Capabilities: The capabilities to deal with naval vessels and landing forces that invade our country, including islands, from outside the threat zone

[7644] To conduct anti-ship and anti-ground attacks from outside the threat zone, these capabilities include guided missiles with a longer range and high survivability, capable of avoiding interception and effectively disrupting an attack on Japan while ensuring the safety of SDF personnel

[7645] Future Operation of Stand-off Defense Capabilities

[7646] As well as acquiring mass-produced ammunition for these domestically produced stand-off missiles, the introduction of foreign-made stand-off missiles will be implemented and continued

[7647] In this case, given a certain amount of time required to maintain the necessary quantity of domestically produced stand-off missiles, the U.S.-made Tomahawk, which is already in mass production, are to be acquired as soon as possible

[7648] The initial plan was to acquire up to 400 Tomahawks from Block V in FY2026 and FY 2027, but given the more severe security environment, negotiations were held with the U. S. side to accelerate the acquisition

[7649] As a result, some Block V will be changed to Block IV which will be acquired from FY2025, one year earlier than originally planned and by adding Tomahawk launch capabilities to naval vessels and promoting personnel training, sufficient capabilities will be swiftly secured before establishing a system to boost the production of domestically produced stand-off missiles

[7654] Future Operation of Stand-off Defense Capabilities. (2) Strengthening of Unmanned Defense Capabilities

[7655] Compared to manned equipment, unmanned assets have major advantages, such as minimizing casualties and allowing for long-term continuous operation

[7656] Furthermore, combining these unmanned assets with artificial intelligence (AI) and manned equipment can be a game-changer that fundamentally transforms force structure and ways of warfare, enabling Japan to gain asymmetrical superiority in the air, sea and underwater domains

[7657] For this reason, these unmanned assets will be effectively utilized not only for information gathering and monitoring and surveillance, but also for a wide range of missions including combat support

[7658] The acquisition of RQ-4B (Global Hawk) began in FY2015 to enhance the constant surveillance capability over a wide area and the third RQ-4B arrived at ASDF Misawa Air Base (Aomori Prefecture) in June 2023, completing the initially planned system

[7659] In addition, since May 2023, a MQ-9B (Sea Guardian) has been on trial operation at the Hachinohe Air Base (Aomori Prefecture) of the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (MSDF) and from April 2024, its takeoffs and landings are to be verified at the Kanoya Air Base (Kagoshima Prefecture) of the MSDF

[7660] Other demonstrations are underway for transport Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) and reconnaissance UAV (for mid-range) (upgraded) with upgraded capabilities

[7661] In February 2024, transport UAV were used to demonstrate the transportation of supplies to the ship

[7662] In the FY2024 budget, the MOD/SDF will acquire upgraded UAV (for mid-range) to enhance intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance and targeting (ISRT) capabilities as well as obtaining USV with proven operational records in various countries as test equipment to quickly acquire knowledge of unmanned surface vehicles (USV) operations and promote the development of domestically produced USV

[7663] The MOD/SDF will also conduct research into multi-purpose combat-support USV with low observability that selectively carry functions such as monitoring and surveillance and anti-ship missile launch to support manned naval vessels

[7664] In addition, the MOD/SDF will begin to develop unmanned amphibious vehicles, as unmanned assets capable of landing on any shore of islands, transporting supplies and performing other missions from the sea to ground units

[7665] Japan is also co-developing the next-generation fighter aircraft with the United Kingdom and Italy, aiming to complete its development by 2035 and also planning to begin developing UAV that will collaborate with this next-generation fighter aircraft and support it autonomously

[7666] In December 2023, Japan and the United States agreed to conduct joint research into AI technology, which is expected to be applied to this UAV

[7667] Japan will cooperate with the United States and other countries concerned to enhance its unmanned asset defense capabilities

[7668] Strengthening of Mobile Deployment Capabilities

[7669] Given the geographical characteristics of Japan, which stretches 3,000 km from east to west, north to south and includes numerous islands, for responding to an invasion of Japan, Japan needs to build the capacity to ensure that its routinely deployed units remain operational at all times and that the necessary units (personnel, equipment, supplies, etc.) are swiftly maneuvered and deployed according to the situation and needs to establish the infrastructure to make this possible, to secure maritime and air superiority and disrupt the access and landing of units invading Japan

[7670] To this end, Japan will reinforce the SDF’s maritime and air transportation capabilities by acquiring various transportation assets such as transport vessels, transport aircraft, transport helicopters, etc. and also maximize its use of civilian transportation capabilities, including Private Finance Initiatives (PFI

[7671] Specifically, the SDF Maritime Transport Group (tentative name) will be newly formed as a joint unit to improve the capability of mobile deployment to the southwest region

[7672] Moreover, the acquisition of transport assets like transport ships and helicopters to be used for rapid transport of troops and supplies to the islands in the southwestern region and elsewhere will be promoted

[7673] Furthermore, PFI vessels will continue to be secured to avoid creating a vacuum in the transportation system utilizing civilian vessels and the integrated transportation system will be strengthened by using civilian vessels

[7674] In addition, to ensure smoother and more effective transport and supplies for units by the aforementioned capabilities, Japan will strengthen its integrated logistics posture, take necessary measures to use existing airports, seaport facilities and the like as operational infrastructure and improve supply capabilities

[7675] Japan will also actively promote the improvement of supply bases located throughout the country

[7705] Section 4 Responses to Invasions of Japan, Including Missile Attacks

[7706] Japan’s Integrated Air and Capabilities (1) Basic Concept

[7707] As Japan is surrounded on all sides by water, responding to airborne threats is extremely important

[7708] In recent years, airborne threats to Japan have been becoming increasingly diverse, complex and enhanced, including capability enhancements of ballistic missiles equipped with multiple/maneuverable warheads, higher-speed and longer-range cruise missiles and stealth and multi-role manned and unmanned aircraft, as well as the emergence of anti-ship ballistic missiles and hypersonic glide vehicles (HGVs

[7709] Therefore, Japan will fundamentally enhance its detection, tracking and interception capabilities, as well as strengthen integrated air and missile defense capabilities by establishing a system capable of centrally and optimally operating various sensors and shooters through a network

[7710] In response to a missile attack on Japan by an opponent, Japan would first intercept the missile flying towards Japan over the high seas and in its territorial airspace by means of its missile defense system

[7711] Also, as a minimum necessary self-defense measure that cannot be avoided to prevent an attack by ballistic missiles and the like in cases where it is recognized that no other means are available, Japan would utilize its stand-off defense capabilities and other capabilities to mount effective counterstrikes against the opponent’s territory

[7712] By equipping itself with such effective counterstrike capabilities, Japan will constrain missile launches by opponents and facilitate interceptions by its missile defense, thereby deterring the launch of missile attacks themselves when coupled with its missile defense

[7886] Japan depends upon other countries for the supply of much of its resources and food, making maritime transportation routes the lifeblood for securing the foundation of our existence and prosperity
