[11235] Cooperation Activities

[11236] To be a proactive contributor to world peace, it is important for the SDF to be fully prepared for any future operations

[11237] For this reason, all the three branches of the SDF, namely the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force (GSDF), the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force (MSDF) and the Japan Air Self-Defense Force (ASDF), designate dispatch stand-by units and always maintain a state of readiness

[11238] In addition, engineering units, staff officers and others as well as C-2 transport aircraft and C-130H transport aircraft are registered with the UN Peacekeeping Capability Readiness System (PCRS) to enable the UN Headquarters to grasp the PKO dispatch preparation status of each country more specifically

[11239] The SDF is also enhancing information-gathering capabilities and protection capabilities, which are required for the SDF units to carry out their missions while ensuring the safety of personnel and units in international peace cooperation activities and other similar ones

[11240] Furthermore, in order to respond to various mission environments and prolonged missions, the SDF is improving its capabilities for transport, deployment and information communication, as well as developing a structure of logistics and medical support for conducting smooth and continuous operations

[11241] With regard to the education necessary for engaging in international peace cooperation activities, the GSDF International Peace Cooperation Activities Training Unit, which belongs to the Ground Component Command, provides training for GSDF personnel to be deployed to international peace cooperation activities, as well as supports their training

[11242] In addition to the Japan Peacekeeping Training and Research Center JPC of the Joint Staff College offers not only basic education courses on international peace cooperation activities, but also specialized education to train personnel who can be appointed as contingent commanders of UN PKO missions and staff officers of mission headquarters

[11243] These specialized courses are conducted by using UN standard training materials and foreign instructors

[11244] Based on the current situation of more multi-dimensional and complicated international peace cooperation activities, JPC has also provided education for personnel from foreign militaries and other Japanese ministries and agencies

[11245] The initiative aims to promote the coordination and cooperation and contribute to more effective international peace cooperation activities

[11246] Missions as the combination of “main duties” and “the secondary duties" defined in the Article 3 of the SDF Law

[11247] The primary mission” is defense of Japan while “the secondary missions” are the maintenance of public order and activities in response to Important Influence Situations as well as international peace cooperation activities

[11248] Welfare and Mental Health Measures for

[11249] Dispatched SDF Units

[11250] The MOD/SDF is implementing various family support and mental health support measures for dispatched SDF personnel and their families to alleviate any anxieties they may go through during the dispatch

[11251] For example, depending on the characteristics of the duties of the unit to be dispatched, the MOD/SDF provide SDF personnel with necessary measures such as the following: (1) education before the dispatch on necessary knowledge on how to reduce stress; (2) mental health checks before and during the dispatch as well as after returning to Japan; (3) counseling on anxieties and concerns during the dispatch, conducted by staff specially trained for carrying out mental health care; (4) dispatch of a mental health care team mainly including a medical officer with expertise on mental health care; (5) stress reduction education upon returning to Japan; and (6) special medical checkup after returning to Japan

[11301] In July 2011 following South Sudan’s independence, with the objective of consolidating peace and security as well as helping South Sudan to establish necessary conditions for the development, the UNMISS was established

[11302] In response to requests from UN for cooperation with UNMISS, particularly for dispatching GSDF engineering units, Japan has dispatched units and personnel including staff officers to the Headquarters and SDF engineering units

[11303] South Sudan shares borders with six countries and is positioned in a highly important location, connecting the African continent on all four points of the compass

[11304] The peace and stability of South Sudan is essential not only for the country itself; but also for the peace and stability in its neighboring countries, which leads to those of the whole Africa, as well as a crucial issue that should be dealt with by the international community

[11305] Based on the experiences gained through past PKO, the MoD/SDF has contributed to the peace and stability of South Sudan by providing personnel cooperation in infrastructure development, which is highly expected by the UN

[11306] UNMISS is the only UN PKO to which Japan currently dispatches its personnel and the dispatch of staff officers supports the progress of the peace process in South Sudan together with the international community

[11307] It is significant for Japan to continue dispatching its staff officers from the perspectives of maintaining close involvement in the UN, cooperation with neighboring African countries, and securing opportunities for human resource development

[11308] Part I, Chapter 3, Section 10-2 (Africa) (2) Additional Dispatch of Staff Officers

[11314] Of the two additional uniformed GSDF personnel dispatched in 2024, the DCOS (PET) operates and supervises the personnel, evaluation and training divisions at the UNMISS force headquarters, while the PA provides support to the DCOS (PET) to ensure smooth implementation of the duties

[11346] International Disaster Relief Activities

[11347] In recent years, the role of military has become more diverse and opportunities to leverage military capabilities for Humanitarian Assistance/Disaster Relief (HA/DR) are growing

[11348] The SDF has also been proactively engaged in international disaster relief activities from the viewpoint of humanitarian contributions and improving the global security environment

[11349] To this end, the SDF maintains its readiness to take any necessary actions based on prepared disaster relief operation plans

[11350] The SDF has proactively conducted international disaster relief activities in consultation with the Minister for Foreign Affairs, leveraging its features and capabilities, while considering specific requests by the governments of affected countries and disaster situations

[11351] Outline of the Japan Disaster Relief Team Law

[11352] Since the enforcement of the Japan Disaster Relief Team Law in 1987, Japan has been engaged in international disaster relief activities upon requests from the governments of affected countries or the international organizations

[11353] In 1992, the Japan Disaster Relief Team Law was partially amended to allow the SDF to participate in international disaster relief activities and to transport its personnel and equipment for this purpose

[11354] International Disaster Relief Activities by the SDF and SDF’s Posture

[11355] Considering specific requests by the governments of affected countries and the scale of disaster situations, the SDF’s international disaster relief activities encompass (1) medical services, such as first-aid medical treatment and epidemic prevention; (2) transportation of supplies, patients and personnel by helicopter and other means; (3) waterpurifying activities using water-purifying devices; (4) cooperation in search and other activities by MSDF fixed-wing patrol aircraft

[11356] In addition to such cooperation, (5) the SDF may use transport aircraft and ships to carry disaster relief personnel and equipment to the affected area

[11357] GSDF units including those of the Ground Component Command and regional armies are always in readiness for such operations autonomously

[11358] The Self Defense Fleet of the MSDF and Air Support Command of the ASDF are always in readiness as well to transport personnel and supplies to affected areas

[11359] International Disaster Relief Activities for the Earthquake Disaster in the Republic of Türkiye

[11360] The earthquake with epicenter in southeastern Türkiye on February 6, 2023 caused significant damage in the country, with more than 50,000 people killed

[11361] At the request of the Government of Tiirkiye, Japan dispatched the Japan Disaster Relief and Rescue Team, a medical team and others

[11362] The MOD transported equipment and other items necessary for the Japan Disaster Relief and the medical team operating in the affected area from Japan to Tiirkiye from February 13 to 17 by a B-777 special transport aircraft

[11363] Furthermore, upon a request from the Government of Türkiye and NATO, one KC-767 aerial refueling/transport aircraft transported emergency relief supplies from Pakistan to Türkiye

[11364] The Minister of Defense issued an order on March 24, 2023 to terminate the international disaster relief activities, in which about 60 personnel were engaged

[11365] This was the first international disaster relief activity undertaken by the SDF in cooperation with NATO

[11366] The Government of Tiirkiye and NATO expressed high appreciation and gratitude for this activity, which resulted in further deepening relations not only with Tiirkiye but also with NATO

[11367] Reference: International Disaster Relief Activities

[11368] Section A Initiatives for Arms Control, Disarmament and Non-Proliferation

[11369] The proliferation of weapons of mass destruction (WMDs) and missiles that can deliver them, as well as the proliferation of not only conventional arms but also goods and sensitive technologies of potential military use, pose a pressing challenge to the peace and stability of the international community

[11370] Moreover, many countries are working on the regulation of certain conventional weapons, considering the need to maintain a balance between humanitarian perspectives and defensive needs

[11371] In order to deal with these issues, the international frameworks for arms control, disarmament and non-proliferation have been developed under which Japan has played an active role

[11372] The National Security Strategy of Japan (NSS) describes arms control, disarmament and non-proliferation, including for weapons of mass destruction, etc., as one of the key measures among efforts to strengthen a free and open international order

[11373] In addition, the NSS also states that Japan will cooperate to improve the effectiveness of international organizations and multilateral export control regimes

[11403] Initiatives Focused on Treaties Relating to Arms Control, Disarmament and Non-Proliferation

[11404] Japan actively participates in international initiatives for arms control, disarmament and non-proliferation in regard to WMDs, in the form of nuclear, chemical and biological weapons, as well as missiles that can deliver them and associated technologies and materials

[11405] Japan has contributed to the Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC) by offering its knowledge in the field of chemical protection since the negotiating stage

[11406] Following the entry of the CWC into force, Japan has dispatched eight Japan Ground Self-Defense Force (GSDF) experts on protection against chemical weapons to the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), which was established to continuously implement verification measures

[11407] In addition, small quantities of the chemical substances under the regulation of the CWC are synthesized for protection research at the GSDF Chemical School (Saitama City

[11408] Thus, in accordance with the CWC regulations, the school has submitted annual reports and undergone inspections times in total since the establishment of the OPCW and it has been confirmed that there are no problems

[11409] Moreover, Japan is also working on projects to destroy abandoned chemical weapons in China, based on the CWC. The Ministry of Defense (MOD)/Self-Defense Forces (SDF) has seconded GSDF and other personnel to the Cabinet Office to be in charge of this project and since 2000, GSDF personnel with expertise in chemicals and ammunitions have been dispatched to conduct excavation and recovery projects on a total of 20 times (As of September

[11410] Personnel dispatched to the OPCW (at the time of the inspection

[11411] In addition, MOD officials are dispatched to major meetings such as the Wassenaar Arrangement, the Australia Group (AG) and the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR), which are international export control regimes and have made proposals to contribute to non-proliferation of key technologies from security perspectives

[11412] Moreover, Japan has been cooperating to enhance the effectiveness of regulations and decisions, such as by dispatching SDF personnel to training conducted by the Preparatory Commission for the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty Organization (CTBTO

[11413] Japan has concluded various conventions on the regulation of conventional weapons such as the Convention on Prohibitions or Restrictions on the Use of Certain Conventional Weapons Which May Be Deemed to Be Excessively Injurious or to Have Indiscriminate Effects (CCW), based on humanitarian perspectives and security needs

[11451] Reinforcing Defense Production and Technology Bases as a Virtually Integral Part of Defense Capability itself

[11452] Rapid advances in science and technology in recent years have brought about fundamental changes in the nature of national security

[11453] Countries are accelerating research and development to ensure their technological superiority, especially through the acquisition of cutting-edge technologies that could become so-called “game changers” which dramatically alter the future character of warfare

[11454] New technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), quantum technology, and technology for utilizing new forms of energy are being applied to equipment, expanding the character of warfare not only in the conventional domains such as ground, maritime, and air but also into space, cyber and electromagnetic domains, including the cognitive dimension

[11455] In addition, the rapid advancements of information-related technologies and information infrastructure, such as AI and SNS (Social Networking Services), has dramatically increased the risk of hybrid warfare, in which military and non-military means are combined, and the expansion of information warfare through the spread of disinformation or by other means

[11456] Even in Japan, there is now an urgent need to quickly acquire superior equipment that will support new ways of warfare, which can only be achieved through long-term, constant efforts to accumulate technological knowledge in Japan, develop highly skilled human resources, and maintain manufacturing equipment and facilities that meet our country’s particular needs

[11457] Therefore, the MOD has generally regarded Japan’s defense production and technology bases are essential infrastructures for securing superior equipment and makes efforts to maintain and reinforce these bases

[11458] However, in recent years, Japan’s defense production and technology bases have been exposed to challenging conditions, such as increased costs due to technological advances and the emergence of supply chain risks due to the complex and unstable international situation

[11459] These conditions, combined with particular characteristics of defense equipment, such as limited demand and unique specifications, led to low profitability and a negative outlook for business continuity and growth, mainly in the defense industry

[11460] Recently, companies deciding to withdraw from defense businesses are appearing intermittently, and even if they are not withdrawing, companies have been reluctant to make new investments, causing concerns that this could affect the operational availability of defense equipment and interfere with the operation of the SDF

[11461] Currently, the SDF can fully demonstrate its capabilities and accomplish its mission of defending Japan only by using equipment that incorporates advanced technologies

[11462] In the National Security Strategy formulated in December 2022 and other documents, the Government of Japan clearly stated its policy of tackling the current severe situation surrounding defense production and technology bases, which are essential infrastructures for securing superior defense equipment in Japan, making these bases virtually an integral part of defense capability itself, and making efforts to reinforce these bases fundamentally

[11463] Game changers

[11464] This refers to cutting-edge technologies that could drastically alter the future way of warfare, such as artificial intelligence (AI), hypersonic and high-power energy technologies, quantum technology

[11465] Countries are focusing on developing such technologies as some advanced technologies in the civilian sector have been converted to military technologies

[11466] Section 1 Reinforcing Defense Production Base

[11467] Japan’s defense production base has several unique characteristics

[11468] As a premise, Japan, which does not have arsenals (state-run factories for defense equipment), heavily relies on private companies to play an important role in producing defense equipment

[11469] Therefore, amid the demand for fundamental reinforcement of defense capabilities, the role of the defense industry is becoming increasingly important in securing equipment for the SDF to carry out its missions

[11470] Especially when manufacturing defense equipment, it is necessary to meet the high level of performance requirements and security measures

[11471] From the perspective of economic rationality, indicating a certain degree of predictability is required for companies to step into investments in this sector

[11472] In addition, opportunities for companies to recover investments are limited since their customers are basically limited to the MOD / SDF

[11473] defense production base has been weakening

[11474] Under such circumstances, companies deciding to withdraw from defense businesses or downsize their operations are appearing intermittently

[11475] Consequently, this not only interferes with the stable procurement of defense equipment essential for SDF operations, but also causes the loss of a proper competitive environment and innovation in the long term, resulting in Japan losing its technological superiority in security

[11476] In addition, the risk of information theft due to cyber attacks, as well as the risk of disruption to the supply of raw materials due to the imposition of export restrictions by other countries have become apparent in recent years

[11477] In light of this environment surrounding our bases, the MOD will take various measures to maintain and reinforce them

[11478] Act on Enhancing Defense Production and Technology Bases and its Basic Policy

[11479] Japan’s defense industry is responsible for each stage of the life cycle of defense equipment (research, development, production, sustainment and maintenance, supply, decommissioning, etc

[11480] In this context, defense equipment and the defense industry are inseparable

[11481] The Act on Enhancing Defense Production and Technology Bases was enacted in June 2023 and enforced in October of the same year in order to take necessary measures to maintain and enhance the ability of the defense industry to produce advanced equipment and ensure high operational rates

[11482] Under this Act, the Minister of Defense is supposed to establish a basic policy, which was announced in October

[11483] This basic policy prescribes the matters necessary to ensure adequate implementation of the measures stipulated in the Act

[11484] Also, it indicates the new direction on how to maintain and reinforce the bases in the future, replacing the “Strategy on Defense Production and Technological Bases” that was formulated in

[11485] Main Direction for Maintaining and Enhancing Bases (1) Significance of Maintaining and Enhancing Bases

[11486] The significance of maintaining and enhancing domestic bases has been pointed out in the past from the perspectives of ensuring Japan’s independence in the security environment, enhancing its deterrence, and contributing economically and technologically to domestic industries

[11487] That domestic bases play an important role in acquiring advanced defense equipment at an early stage and in maintaining and securing sufficient war sustainability of the SDF, but also because the defense industry is composed of a wide range of suppliers, ranging from prime contractors which have direct contracts with the MOD to subcontractors like small and medium-sized enterprises

[11488] In addition, in recent years, countries have been increasingly hoarding technology from the economic security perspective, and supply chains have been disrupted due to the spread of COVID

[11489] Under these circumstances, the need to maintain and reinforce bases in Japan has become even greater from the perspective of ensuring stable manufacturing of defense equipment directly concerning the defense of Japan, as well as securing technological superiority

[11490] Approach to Procurement of Defense Equipment

[11491] On the premise of acquiring defense equipment which meets required performance for the defense of Japan, it is necessary to decide how to acquire defense equipment according to the necessity to ensure continuous acquisition, sustainment and maintenance of the defense equipment in terms of expenses, and from the viewpoints of nurturing sectors in which Japan has a comparative advantage and complementing sectors in which Japan is falling behind or lacking, in addition to the growing need to maintain and reinforce bases in Japan

[11492] Specifically, when acquiring new defense equipment, domestically produced equipment will be pursued, focusing on the following areas: (a) Defense equipment that can meet various conditions, such as operational concepts, performance, acquisition cost, life cycle cost, schedule, etc., with domestic technologies (b) Defense equipment that is essential in maintaining war sustainability in the event of a contingency as well as in ensuring for the ability to improve operations and maintenance in peacetime (e.g., ammunition and ships) (c) Items that should not be dependent on foreign countries from the perspective of confidentiality (e.g., communications, cryptography) (d) Defense equipment that is indispensable for realizing operational concepts that consider Japan’s geographical and policy peculiarities (e) The latest technologies from foreign countries that are hard to obtain (f) Potential target of external threats through economic means (3) Approach to International Cooperation

[11493] As countries these days compete fiercely in R&D in the military field and make remarkable technological progress, it is difficult for each country to maintain necessary bases without cooperating with other countries

[11494] Promoting international cooperation in defense equipment and technology is essential, keeping in mind the basic principle that bases related to defense equipment, which should not be dependent on other countries, should be maintained and enhanced domestically

[11495] Therefore, it is necessary to promote international joint research and development in addition to active international cooperation and licensed production, contributing to incorporating the excellent technologies of various countries into Japan’s defense equipment

[11496] The transfer of defense equipment and technology is a key policy instrument to ensure peace and stability, especially in the Indo-Pacific region, to deter unilateral changes to the status quo by force, create a desirable security environment for Japan, and provide assistance to countries that are subject to aggression in violation of international law, use of force, or threat by force

[11497] Accordingly, the government and private sector will make joint efforts to promote the smooth transfer of defense equipment and technology of high-security significance and international joint development in various fields

[11498] Ideal State of the Defense Industry

[11499] It is of utmost importance that the defense industry maintain the capacity to manufacture the necessary defense equipment and support high operational rates

[11500] In addition, to make the Japanese defense industry internationally competitive like the defense industries of foreign countries including European countries and the U. S., it is important to review the industrial structure and build a defense industry led by companies with a high degree of defense demand dependence (the ratio of defense-related sales

[11501] Roles of the Government and Defense Equipment Manufacturers in Ensuring Stable Manufacturing of Defense Equipment

[11502] While the government emphasizes creating an environment in which the defense equipment manufacturers can work on defense projects and determine to continue such projects further, defense equipment manufacturers are expected to proactively act on the government’s initiatives to maintain and enhance the bases, newly recognizing that they are essential entities responsible for national defense

[11503] Business operators engaged in the manufacture of defense equipment 2 Measures Based on the Act on Enhancing Defense Production and Technology Bases (1) Specific Initiatives (reinforcing supply chain resilience, improving manufacturing process efficiency, enhancing cybersecurity, supporting business succession, etc

[11504] Various risks are assumed to impede the stable manufacturing of defense equipment, such as the risk of difficulty in importing raw materials because of export restrictions imposed by a foreign government, the risk of delay in delivery or failure to meet the performance requirements because of sluggish productivity and technological standards caused by aging facilities that have not been renewed, the risk of major concerns for any parts infected with malware or spyware in the manufacturing process, the risk of leakage of information on performance due to cyber attacks, and the risk of withdrawing from defense projects because it has become challenging to continue the business

[11505] The following specific initiatives need to be taken by defense equipment manufacturers to respond to such risks effectively and ensure the supply chain consisting of prime contractors and suppliers functions more effectively and efficiently, thereby contributing to stable manufacturing of designated defense equipment

[11506] a) Reinforcing supply chain resilience

[11507] Domestic production and stockpiling of raw materials Research and development of alternate materials and products (b) Improving manufacturing process efficiency Introduce state-of-the-art equipment and technologies Automate inspection processes by introducing AI (c) Enhancing cybersecurity

[11508] Enhance information systems

[11509] Employee training (d) Support for business succession, etc

[11512] The MOD then enters into a contract directly with the defense equipment manufacturer for the specific initiatives after approval of the plans and pay compensation without delay following the contract’s provisions

[11513] In fiscal 2023, 36 projects with a total value of approximately ¥9.9 billion were approved

[11515] Facilitation of Equipment Transfer and the Designated Equipment Transfer Support Corporation

[11516] When transferring defense equipment and technology, the defense equipment manufacturer may be required to make appropriate adjustments to specifications and performance from the national security perspective

[11517] In particular, it is necessary to appropriately address concerns of losing Japan’s technological superiority over other countries in the defense sector by securing information on advanced technologies used in Japan’s defense equipment

[11518] The necessary grants are provided when the Minister of Defense requires a defense equipment manufacturer to adjust specifications and performance

[11519] On February 16, 2024, the Minister of Defense designated the Designated Equipment Transfer Support Corporation to provide the necessary grants from the fund and to ensure that equipment transfer conducted by defense equipment manufacturers is carried out smoothly and under appropriate management, in line with the policy objectives of the MOD

[11520] The MOD delivered 40 billion yen in FY2023 and 40 billion yen in FY2024 to the Designated Equipment Transfer Support Corporation to establish the fund

[11523] Protecting the Confidential of Defense Equipment

[11524] In manufacturing defense equipment, the MOD provides contractors with classified information on defense equipment, such as advanced technologies, for steady procurement of higher-quality defense equipment

[11525] On the other hand, in recent years, the threats of leakage of classified information in defense equipment including cyber attacks and corporate acquisition by countries of security concern, has become higher

[11526] With this in mind, the classified information provided by the government to contractors has been re-designated as “Confidential of Defense Equipment,” explicitly indicating to contractors and their employees that handling such classified information requires strict management

[11527] In addition, the same penalties currently imposed on SDF personnel will be applied to persons who intentionally leak these confidential, which will prevent leakage more effectively

[11528] Government Ownership of Designated Defense Equipment Manufacturing Facilities by the Minister of Defense, etc

[11529] If it is determined that stable procurement of designated defense equipment by the MOD is not possible through the various efforts described in (1) and (2) above, the MOD may acquire the designated equipment manufacturing facilities or equipment that manufacture such designated defense equipment

[11530] The acquired defense equipment manufacturing facilities will be managed by contractors commissioned by the MOD for the manufacture of designated defense equipment

[11531] Therefore, being private companies, the business entities are expected to operate efficiently, no different from their regular business activities, even when this system is applied

[11683] Section 2 Reinforcing Defense Technology Base I. Necessity of Reinforcing Defense Technology Base

[11684] In order to acquire defense equipment required for the new ways of warfare, the use of our domestic technologies is extremely important

[11685] The development of scientific technologies and innovations based on the country’s advanced technological capabilities is at the source of Japan’s economic and social development and constitutes a key element of its comprehensive national power integral to its national security

[11686] In addition, the active utilization of Japan’s advanced technological capabilities developed by both its public and private sectors over the years in the area of national security without being held back by existing approaches is an essential activity for strengthening Japan’s architecture for national defense

[11687] As competition among major countries intensifies in terms of conducting research on cutting-edge technologies and leveraging its results for applications in national security, each country has focused on reinforcing its technology base for the purpose of national security by investing heavily in R&D aimed at the early operationalization of technologies that could become so-called “game changers” which dramatically alter the future character of warfare

[11688] Although Japan’s research and development expenditures for the MOD have trailed those of the

[11689] United States and other countries, they have increased significantly in recent years due to their importance

[11690] On the other hand, while the distinction between technologies developed for civilian use and for security purposes has become increasingly blurred in practice, it is important to work strategically to ensure technological superiority as a nation by actively leveraging the results of research and development in science and technology in Japan’s public and private sectors for the research and development of equipment

[11691] Therefore, it is necessary to further promote research and development domestically and develop and strengthen the technology base for the technology areas on which Japan should focus

[11692] In the cases of defense equipment and technology cooperation, such as equipment procurement and international joint development, it is important to maintain the leading role by owning important cutting-edge and other technologies

[11706] Direction for Reinforcing Defense Technology Base shown in Defense Technology Guideline

[11707] The National Security Strategy of Japan, National Defense Strategy, and Defense Buildup Program all state the necessity of reinforcing the defense technology base and call for the active utilization of Japan’s advanced technology research results by both its public and private sectors for the research and development of equipment and to strengthen the framework for the research and development of new equipment

[11708] In June 2023, the MOD formulated the Defense Technology Guideline 2023 to embody the policy of reinforcing the defense technology base and serve as a guideline for the MOD to promote various initiatives in an integrated and powerful manner

[11709] The MOD publishes this Guideline to improve the predictability of our partners, foster a common understanding of reinforcing the defense technology base, and establish a foundation to promote technological cooperation actively

[11710] A summary of the Guideline is given below

[11711] Current Status and Challenges of Defense Technology Base

[11712] Rapid advances in science and technology have added to Japan’s economic and social development

[11713] These changes are also significantly impacting the national security environment and changing the face of warfare

[11714] As a result, we may fail to protect Japan’s peace and independence and maintain national security by simply continuing to improve the capabilities of our equipment systems

[11715] To respond to this tense security environment, it is necessary to spin-on Japan’s Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) capabilities, maximize their use for security and defense purposes, and spin off the outcomes of the MOD’s R&D back to society

[11716] To achieve the defense of our nation at all times, R&D at the MOD now necessitates taking new approaches and implementing methods different from those used in the past

[11717] Vision for the Future through Reinforcement of Defense Technology Base

[11718] The Ministry of Defense and the Japan Self-Defense Forces (SDF) need sufficient defense capabilities to defend Japan

[11719] The purpose of reinforcing the defense technology base is to provide the necessary technological support

[11720] Therefore, the future vision in Defense Technology Guideline 2023 is always to defend our nation through technology

[11721] Approaches to Realize This Vision

[11722] Pillar: Accelerating delivery of functions and equipment necessary for the defense of Japan

[11723] The MOD will develop the functions and equipment necessary to defend Japan, which are directly linked to the future ways of warfare, and deliver them in 5 years or within approximately the next 10 years

[11724] nd

[11725] Pillar

[11726] Ensuring technological superiority and creating advanced capabilities

[11727] Over the next 10 years and beyond, various technologies will be put into practical and operational use as new functions and equipment under nationwide collaborations that gather Japan’s STI capabilities from the public and private sectors

[11728] These efforts will create new value as functions and capabilities to defend Japan in the future, realizing defense innovation that will transform our country’s defense, securing technological superiority, and achieving advanced capabilities ahead of other countries through defense innovation

[11729] Means to Realize This Vision

[11730] To achieve the 1st and 2nd pillars, it is necessary to “create” the functions and equipment that the MOD/SDF require, “nurture” technologies strategically, and “understand” various aspects of science and technology

[11731] These efforts will be carried within the MOD and with relevant ministries and agencies, research institutes, industry and academia to build an ecosystem that will allow us to continue to grow together, collaborating in a sustainable, autonomous and comfortable manner while creating synergies and ensuring technology preservation

[11732] Create

[11733] The MOD will take every possible measure to rapidly strengthen our defense capability, including speeding up the time required for R&D of functions and equipment

[11734] The ministry will quickly implement the necessary functions and equipment, demonstrate them in operational fields, and reflect the results and feedback acquired in further improvements

[11735] They will also provide functions and equipment quickly and flexibly while actively introducing R&D methods for early deployment

[11736] This includes introducing new methods such as manufacturing prototypes of an operational quality that troops can use, trial fielding the prototypes, and demonstrating them in the operational field as soon as possible, leading to improved deterrence

[11737] Open innovation that actively utilizes R&D resources and ideas outside the ministry for solving any issues will be promoted

[11738] The ministry’s policy, operational, and technical divisions will work together to create the concept of future warfare, the direction for future R&D, and the acquisition of functions and equipment

[11739] In addition to predicting technologies and warfare in the future, the MOD will also engage experts from outside the ministry with extensive knowledge of science and technology in the civilian field to examine how technology can be utilized against new threats

[11740] Technical knowledge, human resources, facilities and test equipment are the essential foundation of R&D

[11741] The MOD will share its goals with ATLA’s research institutes and test centers, which have the R&D infrastructure, as well as with partners that have supported R&D projects, to improve the predictability of industries and implement projects in alignment with our direction for reinforcing the defense technology base

[11742] Investments for the continued maintenance and reinforcement of the technology base essential to advancing R&D will be made

[11743] The MOD will communicate and collaborate with companies, including start-ups unfamiliar with defense-related R&D, to establish a system that allows various industries to participate in our projects

[11744] A technology base that will enable defense-related companies to integrate the technologies of start-ups and other companies into functions and equipment will be built

[11745] The Innovative Science and Technology Initiative for Security (ISTIS), which solicits and outsources goal-oriented basic research with the expectation that it will contribute to future R&D in the defense sector, focuses on developing technologies in niche areas that find it difficult to gain investments from the civilian sector and on identifying and developing the basic research that will expand the boundaries of the S&T field

[11746] This program will continue to be utilized to create the new technology base

[11747] To assign personnel who can fulfill diverse roles to the appropriate positions flexibly and quickly, new initiatives for human resource utilization and promotion, such as further strengthening human resource development and expanding the recruitment of experienced personnel, will be actively pursued

[11748] Nurture

[11749] The MOD will not limit itself to past R&D experience and will also explore technologies that should be nurtured, actively taking brand-new approaches that differ from conventional R&D methods

[11750] The ministry will also encourage challenging research and create an R&D system that can accept unpredictable technological risks

[11751] Given the MOD’s limited resources and the fact that the ministry’s R&D investments are just a small part of the S&T investments by the government of Japan, various science and technology activities outside the ministry will be actively utilized for defense purposes

[11752] To effectively utilize the results of R&D with different objectives for the defense sector, efforts will be made to concretely communicate the needs of the ministry and the direction of our efforts, create an environment that encourages members of the S&T community to participate in MOD projects, seek new partners, and build and expand networks among researchers

[11753] An ecosystem that rewards the efforts of industries and allows businesses to grow naturally will also be developed

[11754] The MOD will create new chemical reactions by fusing the defense sector with the non-defense sector to nurture technological solutions based on new ideas

[11755] Great efforts will be made to maximize domestic and international STI capabilities to nurture technologies

[11756] The outcomes of the MOD’s R&D have also contributed to raising Japan’s capabilities in STI

[11757] Various R&D activities at the MOD will be promoted to nurture Japan’s capabilities in STI, with an eye on addressing global issues

[11758] Through STI, the MOD will expand the human resources that conduct goal-oriented basic research, secure diverse researchers, pioneer new research areas, and establish and strengthen human connections in emerging research areas to expand STI capabilities

[11759] Understand

[11760] The MOD will determine what it should do in the future based on an accurate understanding of the current S&T environment, such as the technological trends in the private sector in Japan and overseas, the current status of R&D in industries including startups in Japan, advanced and innovative technologies held by research institutes and academia, and the results of R&D projects

[11761] As various science and technologies are beginning to be used in the actual battlefield nowadays, the MOD will accurately and quickly understand how S&T is being used currently, how new technologies may be used in future warfare, and how this will change the national security environment and our nation’s defense, including MOD and SDF activities

[11762] Appropriate measures will be implemented for such S&T changes

[11763] The MOD will actively communicate outside the ministry about what it is doing regarding technology, its purpose, and how its efforts affect the national security environment and defense activities

[11764] Plans and future R&D projects will be shared with outside the Ministry as far as possible to improve the predictability of stakeholders

[11788] Development of the Next-Generation Fighter Aircraft

[11789] For the defense of Japan and to ensure air superiority well into the future, it is vital that Japan continues to employ superior, state-of-the-art fighters

[11790] Therefore, with regard to the next-generation fighter aircraft that would succeed the F-2 fighters scheduled to be decommissioned starting around 2035, it is imperative to realize Japan-led development which ensures freedom of modification for timely and appropriate upgrades in the future and domestic production and technology bases for high readiness, etc., on the premise that the aircraft maintains the capability to effectively counter numerically superior opponents

[11791] To achieve this, the MOD concluded a FY2020 project contract with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd., in October 2020 as a prime company to be in charge of the holistic integration of the fighter, and the development began

[11792] Japan, the United Kingdom, and Italy then conducted a joint analysis on the extent of commonality of the aircraft, and on the basis of the results, the three nations agreed to develop a common platform

[11793] This was officially announced by the leaders of the three nations as the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) in December

[11794] The program enables the three nations to bring together technological advantages and share costs and risks for the joint development of an advanced fighter aircraft which will ensure future air superiority

[11795] This cooperation will not only encourage further cooperation among the industries of each country but also maintain and reinforce Japan’s defense industrial and technology bases by increasing the number of mass-produced next-generation fighter aircraft, nurturing the next generation of engineers with international experience, and introducing advanced development and manufacturing methods such as digital engineering

[11796] In December 2023, Defense Minister Kihara met with the UK Secretary of State for Defence Shapps and Italian Defence Minister Crossetto in Tokyo to sign the Convention on the Establishment of the GCAP International Government Organization,” an international organization essential to establishing an efficient tri-nation cooperation

[11797] Furthermore, this cooperation between the three countries, which share fundamental values and are allies of the United States, will serve as the foundation for a broader cooperation with the United Kingdom and Italy for generations to come and contribute significantly to peace and stability in both the Indo-Pacific region and Europe

[11798] In December 2022, the United States have announced to support Japan’s security and defense cooperation with likeminded allies and partners, including with the United Kingdom and Italy on the trilateral joint development of the next generation fighter aircraft

[11799] Japan and the United States have also agreed to launch a concrete collaboration by the end of 2023 on autonomous systems such as UAVs that could complement Japan’s next fighter program among other platforms

[11800] In December 2023, the Japan MOD and the U.S. Department of Defense signed a project arrangement for joint research on Overwhelming Response through Collaborative Autonomy which is expected to be applied to UAVs that will be used in collaboration with the next-generation fighter aircraft

[11858] Based on the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology and the Implementation Guidelines formulated in April

[11859] Japan promotes defense equipment and technology cooperation with other countries in order to contribute to the maintenance and strengthening of defense technology and industrial bases, as well as to the promotion of our national security, peace and international cooperation

[11860] The transfer of defense equipment and technology as outlined in the National Security Strategy describes that such transfer is a key instrument to ensure peace and stability, especially in the Indo-Pacific region, to deter unilateral changes to the status quo by force, to create a desirable security environment for Japan, and to provide assistance to countries that are subject to aggression in violation of international law, use of force, or threat of force

[11861] From this perspective, the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology, its Implementation Guidelines, and other systems will be considered for revisions

[11862] The Liberal Democratic Party and the Komeito Party have held 23 discussions of the ruling party’s Working Team

[11863] since April 2023, including the history of defense equipment transfers and hearings from experts

[11864] In response, in December 2023, the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology and its Implementation Guidelines were revised based on the recommendations of the ruling party WT

[11865] Furthermore, a Cabinet resolution was passed in March 2024 after inter-party discussions between the ruling parties

[11866] The Implementation Guidelines were partially revised to establish a stringent mechanism

[11867] It is now possible to transfer finished products regarding the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP), a joint development project among Japan, the United Kingdom and Italy, from Japan to countries other than partner countries

[11868] In addition, to smoothly promote such transfers, Japan will carry forward with the transfer of defense equipment and technology through joint public and private efforts by establishing a fund and providing corporate support as needed, etc

[11869] Systems Regarding Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology New Three Principles (1) Clarification of Cases Where Transfers Are Prohibited (the First Principle

[11870] The cases where overseas transfers of defense equipment are prohibited are clarified as follows: (1) in the case of violating the obligations under treaties and other international agreements that Japan has concluded; (2) in the case of violating the obligations based on the Resolution of the United Nations Security Council; or (3) in the case of transferring to countries in conflict

[11871] Limitation to Cases Where Transfers May Be Permitted

[11872] As Well As Strict Examination and Information Disclosure (the Second Principle

[11873] The cases where transfers may be permitted are limited to (1) cases that contribute to the active promotion of peace contribution and international cooperation, (2) cases that contribute to the security of Japan, or other cases

[11874] In addition, it has been decided that important cases would be deliberated at the National Security Council and along with this, information concerning the cases that were deliberated would be disclosed

[11875] Ensuring Appropriate Control regarding Extra-Purpose Use or Transfer to Third-Party Countries (the Third Principle

[11876] Overseas transfers of defense equipment and technology will be permitted only in cases where appropriate control is ensured, and the Government will in principle oblige the government of the recipient country to gain its prior consent regarding extra-purpose use and transfer to third parties

[11877] However, in cases where it is judged appropriate for the active promotion of peace contribution and international cooperation, cases involving participation in the international systems for sharing parts, and cases where parts are delivered to a licenser, appropriate control may be ensured with the confirmation of the control system at the destination

[11878] Reference 65 (Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology); Reference 66 (Implementation Guidelines for the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology

[11879] Partial Revision of the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology

[11880] The National Security Strategy states that the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology and the Implementation Guidelines will be revised to promote smooth transfer of defense equipment and technology of high security significance and international joint development in a broad array of fields

[11881] In doing so, the necessity, requirements, and transparency of the related procedures for transfer of defense equipment and technology will be under adequate consideration, while maintaining the three principles themselves

[11882] Based on this, the ruling party’s WT was held 23 times after April 2023, discussed the revision of cases where overseas transfers may be permitted, as well as how to ensure appropriate management after the transfer, including strict examination when determining whether a transfer is allowed and prior consent for transfers to third countries, while also taking into account of examples from other countries

[11883] In December 2023, the ruling party’s WT consolidated the recommendations for the government

[11884] Based on the recommendations, the government partially revised the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology and the Implementation Guidelines in the same month

[11885] This is the first revision since the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology was formulated in April

[11886] In addition, this revision of the Implementation Guidelines made it possible to transfer defense equipment and technology in a broad array of fields

[11887] The first project after the revision is the transfer of patriot missiles, which Japan is manufacturing under license, from Japan to the U. S. After deliberation at the National Security Council, it was confirmed that the project falls under the category of a case that can be approved for overseas transfers

[11888] The Ministry of Defense (MOD) intends to create a desirable safety and security environment for Japan based on the revised system

[11889] In order to achieve this environment, the MOD will further promote the transfer of defense equipment and technology through collaboration with relevant ministries and agencies and by joint public and private efforts

[11890] This revision makes it possible to transfer defense equipment in a broad array of fields and at the same time, requires the more strict examination for the transfer

[11891] The government will maintain its basic philosophy as a peace-loving nation that conforms to the Charter of the United Nations and the course it has taken as a peace-loving nation, and promote transfer of defense equipment and technology strictly and carefully in the same manner

[11892] A summary of the December 2023 revisions to the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology and the Implementation Guidelines is as follows

[11893] Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology

[11894] The current three principles will be maintained, and the significance of transfer of defense equipment and technology and the recognition of the security environment was added and updated in the preamble in accordance with the National Security Strategy

[11895] It is also stated that Implementation Guidelines will be amended in a timely manner in response to changes in the security environment and security needs

[11896] International Joint Development and Production

[11897] This revision makes it possible to transfer parts and technology from Japan directly to countries other than its international joint development and production partner countries

[11898] Transfer of Defense Equipment Related to Licensed Products

[11899] Defense equipment (including finished products) for licensed products, including those not of U.S. origin, can now be supplied to the license provider country

[11900] However, when providing defense equipment that corresponds to licensed products considered as weapons under the SDF Law to countries other than the license provider country, it excludes the case of the provision to countries where combat is currently deemed to be taking place as part of an armed conflict unless there are special circumstances in consideration of the need in terms of Japan’s security

[11901] Provision of Repairs and Other Services to Countries Cooperating with Japan in Security Area

[11902] This revision makes it possible to provide repairs and other services to countries cooperating with Japan in security area including the U. S. **Footnotes

[11904] Meeting of all Ministers of State under the leadership of the Chief Cabinet Secretary for the checking, sorting, cross-sectoral and substantial coordination, and promotion of items that are included in the Integrated Innovation Strategy 2019 (Cabinet Decision on June 21, 2019) and which require coordination between the control towers related to innovation

[11905] The term “defense equipment” is deemed appropriate for the title of "Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology,” since possible articles of overseas transfers play a role in contributing to peace and international cooperation, as was seen in the example of the provision of bulldozers and other items belonging to the SDF to disaster-stricken countries

[11906] Similarly, due to the fact that technology is also provided in addition to goods, the term “transfer” was adopted rather than “export.”

[11909] The National Security Council discusses all first-time transfers of arms under the Self-Defense Forces Law (direct transfer or transfer to a third country), and similar transfers of arms for the second and subsequent times are also discussed by the National Security Council if they require particularly careful consideration

[11910] Transfer of Parts

[11911] This revision makes it possible to transfer parts to countries cooperating with Japan in security area, after clarifying the definition of parts.[4] Refers to items incorporated as part of a finished product

[11912] However, this excludes items that can function as equipment by themselves

[11915] Assistance to the country that is subject to aggression with equipment (excluding arms

[11916] This revision enables to transfer equipment and technology that does not fall under the category of arms under the Self-Defense Forces Law to a country that is subject to aggression in violation of international law, regardless of cooperation with Japan in security area

[11917] Strict Examination

[11918] The perspective of strict examination was expanded in light of the diversification of types of transfers, such as transfers of arms under the Self-Defense Forces Law and transfers from license provider country to a third country

[11919] Procedures for Deliberations

[11920] Direct transfers of arms under the Self-Defense Forces Law and transfers of such arms to third parties are basically deliberated and announced by the National Security Council

[11921] Before revision, it was stipulated as “The overseas transfer of defense equipment, which is part of the equipment transferred by the Minister of Defense according to the provisions of Article 116-3 of the Self-Defense Forces Law to Ukraine, which has been invaded in violation of international law.” 3 Direct Transfer of GCAP Finished Products to Third Countries

[11922] In the proposal consolidated by the ruling party's WT in December 2023, it was considered that the direct transfer from Japan to third countries other than the partner countries pertaining international joint development and production requires ongoing deliberations

[11923] Under these circumstances, in particular the finished GCAP products, to realize aircraft that has the capabilities required to protect our country, it is considered necessary to hold a mechanism that allows direct transfer from Japan to third countries other than the partner countries

[11924] In this context, the government has coordinated with the ruling party and provided explanations to the Diet

[11925] Based on this, in March 2024, the Cabinet decided that the transfer of finished products regarding the GCAP from Japan to third countries can be permitted

[11926] In the future, when Japan transfers the finished GCAP products directly to third countries, a Cabinet decision will be made on each case, which is so called a “double Cabinet decision”

[11927] Furthermore, the Implementation Guidelines were partially revised to include “three restrictions”: (1) At present, direct transfer from Japan to countries other than partner countries is restricted to finished products regarding GCAP; (2) transfers will be restricted to countries that have concluded an international agreement obligating the use of defense equipment transferred from Japan in a manner consistent with the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations; and (3) it excludes the case of the transfer to a country where combat is currently deemed to be taking place as part of an armed conflict

[11928] These strict decision-making process shows clearly that Japan will maintain its basic philosophy as a peace-loving nation that conforms to the Charter of the United Nations

[11929] The Ministry of Defense, in light of the current revision, will firmly proceed with discussions with the United Kingdom and Italy, to realize a fighter aircraft suitable for Japan’s security environment to ensure the peace and stability of our country in the future

[11930] Commentary

[11931] Promoting Defense Equipment and Technology Cooperation and Transfer of Defense Equipment Section 3 “Transfer of Next-Generation Fighter Aircraft to Third Countries (Main Points Discussed During the Parliamentary Debate)”

[11932] Why is it necessary for Japan to acquire the next-generation fighter aircraft

[11933] Our country, Japan, is an island nation surrounded by sea on all sides, and any invasion will occur via air or sea

[11934] Therefore, to secure the safety of Japan, which adheres to nonaggressive defense, attacks from the air by aircraft or cruise missiles and from the sea by naval vessels have to be prevented as early as possible while it is still distant

[11935] Fighter aircraft have been developed and operated as core equipment to carry out these defense missions

[11936] While neighboring countries promote the development and deployment of next-generation fighter aircraft, it is indispensable for Japan too to develop cutting-edge fighter aircraft that are more advanced than those of the neighboring countries to maintain Japan’s peace and stability in the future

[11937] Why is it necessary for Japan to conduct international joint development with the United Kingdom and Italy

[11938] As equipment becomes increasingly sophisticated and expensive, countries worldwide are adopting an approach of joint development through cooperation with partner countries by mutually contributing funds and technology to acquire superior equipment

[11939] Under such circumstances, Japan thoroughly examined such possibilities as independent development and joint development with the United States to advance the development of the next-generation fighter aircraft

[11940] As a result, international joint development with the United Kingdom and Italy was determined as the most appropriate option from various perspectives, including the feasibility of realizing the required performance and schedule

[11941] Therefore, it was decided to develop an advanced next-generation fighter aircraft by bringing together the technologies of the three countries, while sharing the risk and cost

[11942] Q Why was the transfer of next-generation fighter aircraft to third countries allowed

[11943] The process of international joint development involves construction of a common airframe through discussing requirements which reflect each country’s security environment

[11944] Under the assumption that all countries will contribute equally, each nation advocates their respective preferred performance

[11945] While the United Kingdom and Italy consider promoting the transfer of finished products to third countries an important contribution, they also expect a similar response from Japan

[11946] If Japan lacks a mechanism for direct transfer to third countries and does not work towards cost reduction, it is likely that the United Kingdom and Italy will not compromise on the performance they seek to achieve

[11947] This situation could make it challenging to realize the fighter aircraft Japan wishes to acquire

[11948] Therefore, it is considered that having a mechanism for direct transfer to third countries and ensuring a position where Japan contributes equally with the United Kingdom and Italy is in the national interest of Japan

[11949] Isn't it necessary to go through strict procedures when transferring next-generation fighter aircraft to third countries

[11950] Regarding the transfer of next-generation fighter aircraft to third countries, in addition to the cabinet decision on the recent revision of the current Implementation Guidelines, a new cabinet decision will be taken individually each time a fighter aircraft is transferred to a third country in the future

[11951] This process, known as the “Double Cabinet decision”, ensures a more rigorous approach

[11952] Furthermore, a partial amendment to the Implementation Guidelines poses three restrictions: (1) Direct transfer from Japan to countries other than partner countries is restricted to finished products regarding GCAP, (2) Transfers will be restricted to countries that have concluded an international agreement obligating the use of defense equipment transferred from Japan in a manner consistent with the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations, (3) It excludes the case of the transfer to a country where combat is currently deemed to be taking place as part of an armed conflict

[11953] In this way, Japan can clearly show that it is steadfast in observing the UN Charter and its basic principle of being a peace-loving country by establishing more stringent processes and conditions

[11954] Japanese government's policy regarding the overseas transfer of defense equipment remains steadfast

[11955] Japan continues to uphold our basic principles as a peace-loving nation abiding by the UN Charter and the path followed thus far

[11956] Prime Minister Kishida answering questions related to the transfer of next-generation fighter aircraft to third countries (March

[11960] Commentary

[11961] Responses from Foreign Countries, Companies, and Others Regarding the Revision of the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment

[11962] After the partial revision of the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology and its accompanying Implementation Guidelines, the Ministry of Defense, in collaboration with relevant ministries and agencies, has seized various opportunities to elucidate the revised content to representatives from foreign countries and companies

[11963] These opportunities have included briefing sessions for company representatives and military attachés from various nations, reciprocal visits by high-level officials from different countries, and international exhibitions where the Acquisition, Technology & Logistics Agency (ATLA) has established booths

[11964] Representatives from various countries have expressed appreciation for Japan's efforts to promote the transfer of defense equipment and technology to create a desirable security environment, among other objectives

[11965] They have also expressed expectations that the revision will broaden the possibilities for new defense equipment and technology cooperation between Japan and their respective countries

[11966] Additionally, following consultations with the ruling coalition parties, the revision expands the scope of defense equipment transfers across various sectors

[11967] Moreover, it mandates that the potential impact on international peace and security must be carefully evaluated under the Self-Defense Forces Law when transferring weapons abroad

[11968] This includes assessing whether the recipient country or region is engaged in armed conflict

[11969] This amendment signifies a more rigorous review process for such transfers

[11970] The Ministry of Defense has clarified to each country that Japan will remain committed to its foundational principles as a peace-loving nation, adhering to the UN Charter

[11971] It will also highlight its historical commitment to peace to foster a wide-ranging understanding of Japan’s initiatives

[11972] Furthermore, company representatives have expressed their approval of the recent revision, which permits the transfer of defense equipment across various sectors

[11973] This change not only facilitates the seamless exchange of such equipment but also promises to bolster the growth potential of the defense industry

[11974] Acknowledging the pivotal role that defense equipment transfer plays as a policy tool for deterring unilateral force-based attempts to alter the status quo and for shaping a favorable security landscape for Japan—especially given the most challenging and complex security environment since the post-war period—the Ministry of Defense will persist in advancing defense equipment transfers

[11975] This will be achieved through rigorous collaboration with public and private sectors to sustain peace and stability across the Indo-Pacific region

[12157] Provision of Defense Equipment to Developing Countries

[12158] Surrounded by an increasingly severe security environment, it has become even more important for Japan that the nations which have a cooperative and friendly relationship with Japan in terms of security and defense have appropriate capabilities

[12159] It is also critical to develop a foundation that will serve as the basis for the international community to cooperate towards improving the security environment

[12160] Among these friendly nations, some have difficulties in acquiring an adequate level of defense equipment on their own because of the scale of their economy and fiscal situation

[12161] Some of these states have been requesting to use SDF equipment that is no longer in use

[12162] Under these circumstances, to respond to the needs of such friendly nations, the MOD established a special provision under Article 9, paragraph (1) of the Public Finance Act in the SDF Law, which came into force in June

[12163] The provision enables the MOD to grant or transfer SDF equipment that is no longer in use to the governments of developing states at a lower price than the current price

[12164] Even in the case of granting or transferring equipment at a lower price than the current price as per this provision, whether or not to transfer such equipment, and to which government such equipment is to be transferred, will be determined case-by-case in light of the Three Principles on Transfer of Defense Equipment and Technology and other regulations

[12165] In addition, the Government of Japan and partner countries must conclude an international agreement to prevent extra-purpose use and transfer to third-parties without the prior consent of Japan. [12215] Project Management throughout Equipment Life Cycle

[12216] Acquisition of Defense Equipment through

[12217] Focused Project Management

[12218] As defense equipment is becoming more sophisticated and complex, its entire life cycle (concept study, research and development, mass production, deployment, operation and maintenance) cost has a tendency to increase in recent years

[12219] It has become extremely important to streamline acquisition throughout the life cycle of equipment and to establish a systematic management to realize the streamlining in order to efficiently acquire equipment of assured quality at appropriate cost in a required timeline as planned

[12220] Therefore, since the establishment of ATLA in October 2015, ATLA undertakes project management throughout the life cycle of equipment upon selecting important equipment, and promotes efforts to realize the optimized equipment acquisition

[12221] Specifically, the MOD has selected 33 designated items for major programs designated for project management and 12 items for semi-major programs for project management as of the end of March

[12222] Fig

[12223] REFERENCE : Project management

[12224] New destroyers that combine improved multi-mission capabilities with compact hulls

[12225] For major programs designated for project management, the MOD designates a Project Manager (PM) dedicated to each specific major program, following which project management for that program is conducted by an Integrated Project Team (IPT), which is composed of officials from relevant divisions within the MOD

[12226] For each of the 45 major and semi-major programs designated for project management as of the end of March 2024, the MOD has formulated an Acquisition Strategy and an Acquisition Plan (Designated Item Plans), which specify the basic matters necessary to systematically implement project management until the present, such as the purpose of the acquisition program, acquisition policy, and life cycle cost

[12227] Furthermore, in principle, ATLA annually reviews the implementation status of the Designated Item Plans and endeavors to promote appropriate project management that reflects the latest status by conducting analysis and evaluation, on the basis of which the Designated Item Plans are reviewed as necessary

[12228] In August 2023, analysis and evaluation of the acquisition program were implemented for the 34 major and semi-major programs which had been designated for project management

[12231] Initiatives to Promote and Strengthen

[12232] Project Management

[12233] The following initiatives have been implemented to promote and strengthen project management

[12234] a. Cost and Schedule Management Using WBS (Work Breakdown Structure

[12235] For certain kinds of equipment, etc., produced in Japan, the MOD promotes the introduction of a management method to visualize the progress of work and cost generated by component (WBS

[12236] Since April 2020, efforts have been made for the public and private sectors to jointly manage costs and schedules through the use of an incentivized risk-sharing management contract system, which allows for the early detection of cost increases and schedule delays and for action to be taken promptly

[12237] b. Method for More Accurate Cost Estimate

[12238] Life cycle cost has been estimated based on actual cost data of similar equipment developed or introduced in the past

[12239] However, as a larger amount of cost data is needed for a more accurate estimate, the MOD promotes the establishment of a cost database by collecting cost data and accumulating them into a database

[12240] c. Accumulation and Development of Expertise

[12241] For further improving the management skills of PMs and enhancing human resources among those who engage in project management, the MOD provides opportunities to study project management methods from overseas and the private sector on a regular basis

[12242] Future Initiatives

[12243] In order to further promote effective and efficient equipment acquisition, the MOD needs to enhance the effectiveness and flexibility of project management throughout equipment life cycles

[12244] Therefore, the DBP stipulates that further efforts for effective and efficient acquisition of equipment will include cost reduction through planned and stable acquisition of equipment by expanding the application of long-term contracts, improving the predictability of companies and promoting efficient production, procurement in consideration of the supply-demand situation of equipment including that of other countries, and narrowing down the SDF’s own unique specifications that cause costs to rise

[12245] Improving the Contract System and Other Related Matters

[12246] In order to promptly respond to changes in the surroundings, the MOD has been reviewing acquisition systems through meetings of the Comprehensive Acquisition Reform Committee since 2007 and the Contract Systems Study Group comprising experts since

[12247] Since FY2016, a special research officer system has been adopted to properly implement the review results in practice

[12248] The production of defense equipment requires a significant amount of time

[12249] Therefore, if a certain amount is to be procured in bulk, a contract for more than five years is needed in many cases

[12250] With regard to defense equipment and services, economies of scale tend not to work mainly due to the following reasons: (1) the MOD is the only customer; and (2) companies that provide such defense equipment, etc., are limited

[12251] In addition, it is difficult for companies to systematically move forward with their businesses with a high degree of predictability, a trait that is peculiar to the defense industry

[12252] For these reasons, although the period of expenditure for acts that incur national debt is limited to five years in principle under the Public Finance Act, this period has been extended to a maximum of ten years for specific equipment through the enactment of the Long-term Contract Act

[12253] The introduction of this change regarding long-term contracts will make stable procurement possible, leading to the realization of the systematic improvement of defense capability

[12254] At the same time, for companies, given that the procurement amount will be assured, the systematic use of personnel and equipment, as well as cost reductions due to bulk orders, will be made possible

[12255] In addition, by implementing longer-term, multiple-year contracts utilizing the Private Finance Initiative (PFI) Act, the planned acquisition and execution of budgets is achieved through the equalization of national expenditure

[12256] At the same time, certain benefits, such as lower equipment procurement costs by reducing risks for the parties taking orders and by promoting the entry of new suppliers, can be obtained

[12257] In addition, regarding the procurement of certain equipment for which little competitiveness can be expected due to its characteristics, and for companies that work on cost reduction by utilizing the MOD’s programs, the MOD ensures transparency and fairness and promotes the appropriate use of limited tendering contracts after clarifying and categorizing the targets, with a view to implementing prompt and efficient procurement and enhancing predictability for companies

[12258] Incentivize Companies to Reduce Cost

[12259] With regard to the procurement of defense equipment, the cost is tending to increase because a large variety of equipment has no market price

[12260] Based on those characteristics, it is necessary to achieve both the reduction of procurement cost and improvement of companies’ incentives to reduce cost simultaneously

[12261] In order to achieve this, ATLA has applied the incentivized risk-sharing management contract system to the next-generation fighter aircraft project and the stand-off electronic warfare aircraft project since April 2020, under which the public and private sectors jointly manage the performance and progress of the contract and the cost, with a certain percentage of any cost reduction achieved awarded to the contractor

[12262] In addition, a system to provide incentives for cost reductions has also been implemented from the same month in order to evaluate the companies’ own cost reduction efforts

[12263] The expansion of its scope of application and other approaches to encouraging such efforts are constantly being considered
