[12275] Acquisition of Defense Equipment

[12276] In procuring equipment, by properly combining the introduction of new, high performance equipment, along with life extension and improvement of existing equipment, the MOD/SDF will efficiently secure necessary and sufficient quality and quantity of defense capability

[12277] In this regard, the MOD/SDF will strengthen its project management throughout its equipment life-cycle, including during its research and development activities, and reduce the life-cycle costs to improve cost-effectiveness

[12278] In addition, by incorporating advanced civilian technologies, the MOD/SDF will steadily realize acceleration of defense equipment deployment for areas that could directly affect the SDF’s current and future ways of warfare and are particularly urgent and significant from a policy perspective

[12279] Part II, Chapter 3, Section 2-4 (Optimization Efforts); Section 2-4-4 (New Measures for Early Deployment) 3 Efforts to Increase Fairness and

[12280] Transparency

[12281] The MOD implements measures for making contracts more appropriate and strengthening checking functions to promote the enhancement of fairness and transparency in relation to the acquisition of equipment and materials

[12282] As part of its efforts to achieve more appropriate public procurement across the whole government, the MOD continues to carry out the introduction and expansion of a comprehensive evaluation bidding system and make bidding procedures more efficient

[12283] In addition to these, based on the lessons learned from past incidents such as overcharging and falsification of the results of equipment testing by defense-related companies, measures such as strengthening system investigation, reviewing penalties, and ensuring the effectiveness of supervision and inspection have been steadily implemented to prevent the recurrence of such incidents

[12284] Through these measures, the MOD strives to prevent the recurrence of misconduct, enhance fairness and transparency, and ensure proper contracting

[12285] In addition, ATLA carries out multilayered checks on the contracts it administers through both internal and external checking systems and checks and balances within the organization

[12286] Specifically, ATLA will further enhance internal inspections by the Inspection and Audit Department as well as defense inspections conducted by the Inspector General’s Office of Legal Compliance and deliberations by the Defense Procurement Council, which is composed of external experts

[12287] Moreover, ATLA has also improved its education department and strives to enhance compliance awareness by providing thorough education pertaining to compliance for ATLA personnel

[12288] Advancing Initiatives Aimed at Effectiveness of Foreign Military Sales (FMS) Procurement FMS (Foreign Military Sales) is a form of U. S. security assistance authorized by the Arms Export Control Act (AECA), etc., that enables U. S. allies and partners to purchase defense equipment and services from the U. S. government

[12289] The characteristics of FMS include: (1) prices are estimates, (2) payments are made in advance in principle and balanced out after fulfillment, and (3) delivery dates are estimates

[12290] FMS is critical to reinforcing the defense capabilities of Japan

[12291] Meanwhile, there are FMS-related various issues, such as late delivery and late case closure

[12292] As the FMS procurement amount is hovering at a high level in recent years, the governments of Japan and the U. S. have been actively working together to make improvements in these issues

[12293] Specifically, ATLA and Defense Security Cooperation Agency (DSCA) have held the Security Cooperation Consultative Meeting (SCCM) to discuss the issues over FMS procurement eight times since

[12294] At the 8th SCCM held in January 2024, Japan and the United States agreed to continue strengthening case management between them in terms of late delivery and late case closures in view of the increase of FMS procurement going forward, and to advance efforts aimed at reducing the number of late deliveries and late case closures while improving the transparency in pricing

[12295] In addition, in April 2023, ATLA and the U. S. Department of Defense concluded a framework to confirm reciprocal and free-of-charge quality assurance services for equipment, etc

[12296] This framework exempts quality assurance fee for FMS procurement, which reduces FMS procurement costs and strengthens collaborative relations within Japan–the U. S. Alliance in procurement, thereby advancing the effectiveness of FMS procurement

[12316] The National Security Strategy states that economic security is to ensure Japan’s national interests, such as peace, security, and economic prosperity, by carrying out economic measures

[12317] In the face of various threats imposed through economic means, Japan needs to comprehensively, effectively, and intensively execute necessary economic measures to enhance

[12318] Japan’s autonomy and to secure the superiority and indispensability concerning our technologies and others

[12319] Developments within the Japanese Government

[12320] To date, Japan has promoted initiatives that contribute to strengthening economic security within its existing legal framework

[12321] In May 2022, the Economic Security Promotion Act was established to comprehensively and effectively promote economic measures related to ensuring national security

[12322] The act developed frameworks for strengthening the resiliency of supply chains, ensuring the safety and reliability of critical infrastructure, public-private collaboration on important cutting-edge technologies, and non-disclosure of selected patent applications

[12323] In May 2024, systems for the non-disclosure of patent applications and core infrastructure became operational, and all systems stipulated by the law were put into operation

[12324] Various measures related to economic security are constantly being reviewed and revised

[12325] For example, in December 2022, 11 resources including semiconductors and batteries were designated as specific important resources to strengthen the resiliency of supply chains, and efforts are underway to secure their stable supply

[12326] In February 2024, new initiatives were also implemented, such as the designation of advanced electronic components (capacitors, high-frequency filters) as important resources (bringing the total to 12) and adding uranium as a target mineral to the list of designated important minerals

[12327] The Key and Advanced Technology R&D through

[12328] The Cross Community Collaboration Program is led by the relevant ministries and agencies

[12329] The

[12330] K Program implements research and development projects on advanced technologies, including Artificial

[12331] Intelligence (AI), quantum technology, and others, to meet the country’s needs

[12332] The results of the research are intended not only for civilian use but also for public use, including for national security

[12333] The key technologies to be supported by the K Program are defined in the

[12334] R&D vision

[12335] In 2023, the Research and Development

[12336] Vision (Second Round) was decided to reinforce and complement the Research and Development Vision (First Round) by particularly strengthening efforts in the cyberspace and other areas, and research and development began in sequence

[12337] In addition, regarding the security clearance system in the economic security field, a bill on the protection and utilization of critical economic security information was approved by the

[12338] Cabinet and submitted to the Diet in February 2024, which was enacted as a law in May of the same year

[12339] Furthermore, interest in economic intimidation has increased in recent years, and various discussions have been held on this topic

[12340] At the G7 Hiroshima Summit held in May 2023, it was confirmed that a “Coordination

[12341] Platform against Economic Coercion” would be established for responding to economic intimidation, and cooperation with allied and like-minded countries would be promoted

[12342] Initiatives of the MOD

[12343] As inter-state competition intensifies in domains that cross the border between security and the economy, it is extremely important to enhance Japan’s autonomy and safeguard Japan’s superiority and indispensability through economic security measures, such as preserving and fostering advanced technologies as well as maintaining and reinforcing Japan’s defense production and technology bases as a virtually integral part of defense capability in accordance with the NDS

[12344] The MOD, as the government agency in charge of security, actively participates in government-wide initiatives by sharing its knowledge and needs related to maintaining and reinforcing Japan’s defense production and technology bases, which has been amassed over the years

[12345] Specifically, in addition to dispatching personnel to the Office of the Director-General for Economic

[12346] Security in the Cabinet Office, the MOD contributes to resolve economic security challenges by fundamentally strengthening its internal systems, including the expansion of its staff, to proactively offer its knowledge and needs related to security to government-wide initiatives

[12347] Chapter 2 Reinforcing Foundation for SDF Personnel, the Core Element of Defense Capability, to Demonstrate their Abilities Reinforcing Human Resource Base

[12348] The core element of defense capability is SDF personnel

[12349] To demonstrate defense capability, the MOD/SDF will secure the necessary personnel and reinforce the human resource base to create an environment that enables all

[12350] SDF personnel to demonstrate their own abilities while maintaining high morale and pride

[12351] In light of severe recruitment environment of SDF personnel and the changes taking place across the entire society, such as trends in the private-sector labor market and changing attitudes toward working styles, need to be taken into consideration when considering measures to reinforcing the human resource base of the SDF

[12352] Given these circumstances, an “Expert Panel on Reinforcing the Human Resource Base of the MOD/SDF” consisting of experts from outside the MOD was established in

[12353] February 2023 under the purview of the Minister of

[12354] Defense, to increase the effectiveness of measures for reinforcing the human resource base

[12355] After discussions at six review meetings, a report was compiled in July of the same year which recommended that to ensure the sustainability of Japan’s defense capabilities even in a society with a declining birthrate and a declining population, measures like securing diverse human resources, including those from outside SDF, and effective measures throughout the entire life cycle of

[12356] SDF personnel has to be taken more broadly and in more detail than ever before

[12357] Based on these recommendations, at the 7th review meeting in January 2024, the MOD made a report on the progress of various measures aimed at securing diverse human resources, including those from outside the SDF, and promoting active participation throughout the life cycle of SDF personnel

[12358] Experts have expressed their opinions on future issues, and based on these opinions, measures to strengthen the human resources base will be proceeded with

[12359] Enhancing Recruitment Efforts

[12360] In order for the MOD/SDF to execute their various missions properly, it is vital to stably secure excellent human resources, even in the recruiting environment with a decreasing number of people eligible for recruitment due to a declining birth rate

[12361] There is an increasingly fierce competition to secure human

[12362] resources, and the number of recruitments in FY2023, especially for the so-called “shi”(E1-E3) candidates for uniformed SDF personnel and general candidates for enlistment (Upper), decreased by approximately 1,900 compared to FY2022, which is cause for great concern

[12363] For this reason, it is necessary to recruit those with a strong desire to join the SDF by sufficiently explaining to potential applicants the missions, roles, and duties of REFERENCE

[12366] In addition, the Provincial Cooperation Offices based in 50 locations throughout Japan, have been enhancing their recruitment system by increasing the number of part-time staff in FY2023, recruiting and employing uniformed SDF personnel, etc., attempting and perseveringly with the cooperation of obtaining local governments, schools, recruitment counselors, and others

[12367] Moreover, local governments carry out some of the administrative activities regarding the recruitment of uniformed SDF personnel and candidates for uniformed

[12368] SDF personnel, including announcing the recruitment period and promoting the SDF as a workplace, with the MOD bearing the requisite cost

[12369] At the same time, the MOD is strengthening collaboration with local governments to ensure necessary cooperation, including information provision on recruitment targets, which is indispensable for smooth administrative activities regarding recruitment

[12440] Utilization of SDF Reserve Personnel and others

[12441] It is essential to secure the required number of uniformed

[12442] SDF personnel promptly depending on situational changes in the event of a crisis

[12443] To secure the required number promptly and systematically, the MOD maintains the following three systems: the SDF Reserve Personnel system, the SDF Ready Reserve Personnel system, and the Candidates for SDF Reserve Personnel system

[12444] SDF Reserve Personnel become uniformed SDF personnel upon issuing a defense call-up order or other orders and carry out logistical support and base guard duties

[12445] SDF Ready Reserve Personnel become uniformed SDF personnel and are assigned to carry out their mission together with active-duty uniformed SDF personnel as part of frontline units following the issuance of a defense call-up order or other orders

[12446] Candidates for

[12447] SDF Reserve Personnel, some of whom are recruited among those with no prior experience as uniformed SDF personnel, are appointed as SDF Reserve Personnel after completing the necessary education and training

[12448] Until now, SDF Reserve Personnel and Ready

[12449] Reserve Personnel have been summoned during large-scale disasters such as earthquakes or typhoons, and the. COVID-19 pandemic

[12450] During the 2024 Noto Peninsula

[12451] Earthquake Disaster Relief Operations, SDF Reserve

[12452] Personnel and Ready Reserve Personnel qualified as doctors or nurses were dispatched to provide medical support (mobile medical visits) and daily life support (transportation of goods) in the affected areas

[12453] Since SDF Reserve Personnel and others are engaged in their respective jobs under normal circumstances, the understanding and cooperation of the companies, etc., that employ these personnel are essential for them to attend regular training, etc

[12454] For this purpose, the MOD provides a special subsidy to the companies that employ SDF Ready Reserve

[12455] Personnel and take necessary measures to allow such employees to attend training sessions for 30 days a year, by taking into consideration the burden on such companies

[12456] The SDF Reserve Personnel in action during the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake Disaster

[12457] Relief Operations

[12458] Moreover, in order to secure their understanding and cooperation regarding the duties of SDF Reserve

[12459] Personnel and SDF Ready Reserve Personnel, companies, etc., that employ these personnel are provided with a subsidy in the event that (1) SDF Reserve Personnel or SDF Ready Reserve Personnel respond to a defense operation call-up order, civil protection dispatch call-up order, or disaster relief call-up order, etc., or if (2) they have no choice but to leave their regular occupations due to injuries during their duties, etc

[12460] In addition, a special subsidy for companies that cooperate with the training of SDF Ready Reserve

[12461] Personnel is paid to companies, etc., that employ individuals who, after being Candidates for SDF Reserve Personnel with no prior experience as uniformed

[12462] SDF personnel, are appointed as SDF Ready Reserve Personnel after completing the necessary education and training as SDF Reserve Personnel, and which take the necessary measures to ensure that such employees can attend training sessions with peace of mind

[12463] Many other countries also have reserve personnel systems

[12552] In 2022, the MOD developed “The Basic Policy on

[12553] Mental Health in the Ministry of Defense” and adopted various measures with a view to preventing suicide among its personnel

[12554] Specifically, the MOD has engaged in improving the work environments by raising awareness of mental health checks for all employees and by educating them to make use of counseling services, as well as by promoting measures related to work-life balance

[12555] The MOD is also strengthening its support system by securing qualified counselors, collaborating with supervisors, counselors, and medical institutions, and diversifying consultation channels

[12557] MOD improving Living and Work Environments. 1 Initiatives to Improve Living and Work Environments

[12558] The NDS calls for the continued improvement of the living and work environments to enable all SDF personnel to demonstrate their own abilities while maintaining high morale and pride

[12559] Specifically, to ensure readiness, the SDF is developing the necessary housing and is promoting measures against aging and earthquake proofing of barracks, government office buildings and housing

[12560] Additionally, it will work to gradually improve the living environment to ensure the privacy of SDF personnel, for example, by turning barracks into private rooms, and steadily renew worn-out living- and work-related equipment and secure the requisite amount of daily consumables

[12561] In addition, in order to improve the education, living, and work environments for female SDF personnel, women’s quarters will be set up in buildings and on vessels and submarines, while women’s restrooms and bathrooms will be built or renovated at training areas and other locations

[12562] Initiatives to Support Families

[12563] In addition to exchanges between units and personnel's families, as well as between the families, the MOD in cooperation with relevant external groups and organizations is also actively working to develop a family support system to be implemented in the event of large-scale natural disasters and other events, which will include receiving cooperation in confirming the safety of the family members of SDF personnel and providing them with assistance in their livelihoods

[12564] In addition, the MOD is promoting various types of support measures for the families of SDF personnel

[12565] For units dispatched overseas or to vessels for operations expected to continue for an extended period of time, the MOD has been creating a communication environment that allows the personnel and their families to get in direct contact

[12566] Moreover, the MOD has been implementing a range of support measures for the families of the personnel, including supporting additional shipments of comfort items sent from families to SDF personnel deployed overseas, holding briefing sessions and establishing consultation desks (family support centers) for families, and creating a website for the families of SDF personnel

[12567] MOD Human Resources Development

[12568] Enhancing the ability of the individual uniformed SDF personnel who comprise SDF units is essential for the execution of the units’ duties

[12569] For this purpose, the respective SDF training units and schools provide opportunities for phased and systematic education according to ranks and duties to nurture necessary qualities and instill knowledge and skills

[12570] Based on the DBP, the GSDF High Technical School will be jointly operated by the Ground, Maritime and Air SDF as well as transformed into a coeducational school

[12571] The MOD/SDF will strengthen the joint education in each SDF service as well as education and research including those of the cyber domain in each SDF service and at the National Defense Academy

[12572] At the same time, the MOD/SDF will promote standardization of the educational curriculum and utilization of state-of-the-art technologies

[12573] In order to strengthen the content and structure of education and research, including in the cyber domain, the National Defense Academy is providing cyber literacy education and education on cross-domain operations for all grades to acquire cyberspace-related knowledge

[12574] Additionally, from FY2024, the Department of Information Engineering will be reorganized as the Department of Cyber and Information Engineering, to carry out more specialized education and research focused on the cyber domain

[12575] Furthermore, education requires considerable human, time, and economic commitment, including securing instructors with special skills as well as improving equipment and educational facilities

[12576] In the event that personnel need to further improve their professional knowledge and skills, or that it is difficult for them to acquire such knowledge and skills within the SDF, the MOD/SDF commissions education to external institutions, including those abroad, as well as domestic companies and research institutes. (HRB Part II, chapter 1, Section 4-5-2(3) (Education and Research

[12577] Because SDF personnel execute their missions in a challenging environment, efforts have been made to improve their treatment based on the special nature of their missions and work environments

[12578] In FY2024, a number of improvements will be implemented, including raising the allowances paid to crew members of destroyers and submarines as well as those serving in the JSDF Cyber Defense Command and the Amphibious Task Force, and providing new allowances to personnel working at radar sites, snipers, and personnel undergoing ranger training

[12579] From FY2023, in accordance with the DBP, surveys are being conducted on overtime work performed by uniformed SDF personnel and the salary systems of military personnel in other countries

[12580] In the future, the treatment of SDF personnel will be improved in light of not only the special nature of their missions and work environment but also the increase in the number of new missions, taking into account the results of these surveys

[12581] At the same time, to ensure that SDF personnel can execute their missions with high morale and pride, measures related to honors and privileges, including expanding the scope of conferment of decorations and the appropriate commendation of achievements, will be promoted

[12582] Commemorating Personnel who Perished in the Line of Duty

[12583] Since the establishment of the National Police Reserve in 1950, SDF personnel have endeavored to complete their noble missions to protect the peace and independence of Japan with a strong sense of responsibility, regardless of danger

[12584] During this time period, however, more than 2,000 personnel have lost their lives in the line of duty

[12585] In the MOD/SDF, funeral ceremonies are carried out by the respective units to which SDF personnel who perished in the line of duty belonged in order to express condolences

[12586] Moreover, in order to eternally recognize the achievements of the personnel who perished in the line of duty and to express the deepest respect and condolences, memorial ceremonies are carried out in various forms, such as the Memorial Service for members of SDF personnel who lost their lives in the line of duty conducted with the participation of the Prime Minister

[12587] Achievements of 26 SDF members (20 GSDF, 5 MSDF, and 1 ASDF members) who lost their lives in the line of duty were recognized in a Memorial Service in FY

[12588] Dealing with Retirement and Re-employment of SDF Personnel and Related Matters

[12589] In order to maintain the SDF’s strength, most uniformed SDF personnel retire after their mid-50s, while fixed-term uniformed SDF personnel retire in their 20s or mid-30s

[12590] For many uniformed SDF personnel, re-employment is essential to safeguard their livelihood

[12591] Therefore, it is of paramount importance to provide re-employment support for active uniformed SDF personnel in order to relieve their anxiety about the future and allow them to devote themselves to their duties

[12592] The DBP also states that it is the responsibility of the Government to secure the livelihood of uniformed SDF personnel after their retirement

[12593] It also calls for the MOD/SDF to further improve and strengthen re-employment support such as by enhancing the career guidance system and job training opportunities for SDF personnel scheduled to retire, and by strengthening cooperation with local governments, relevant organizations and private companies

[12594] Retired uniformed SDF personnel have excellent abilities in planning, leadership, capacity, cooperativeness, and responsibility gained through their work performance, education and training

[12595] Furthermore, they have various qualifications and licenses acquired through their duties and vocational training

[12596] Therefore, they are making positive contributions in a broad range of sectors, including manufacturing and service industries, as well as finance, insurance, real estate, and construction industries, in addition to the disaster prevention and crisis management departments of local governments

[12597] Specifically, as of the end of March 2024, a total of 665 retired SDF personnel work as crisis management officers and others at the disaster prevention and crisis management departments of local governments: 46 prefectural bureaus have 109 of them in total, and 467 municipal bureaus have 556 all over Japan

[12598] Since strengthening cooperation between the MOD/SDF and local governments will help to reinforce the crisis management capabilities of local governments, efforts are also being made to strengthen re-employment support in this regard

[12599] Furthermore, the MOD offers disaster prevention and crisis management education for retiring uniformed SDF personnel seeking employment in the disaster prevention and crisis management departments of local governments

[12600] An individual who completes the course is certified as a regional disaster prevention manager by the Cabinet Office upon request

[12601] The requirement for this certification is a rank of at least Ichii or a rank of Nii (First Lieutenant (GSDF, ASDF)/Lieutenant Junior Grade (MSDF

[12602] with the effective work experience of an Ichii (Captain (GSDF, ASDF)/Lieutenant (MSDF

[12603] In addition, exchange of opinions regarding re-employment support for SDF personnel scheduled to retire with the security industry, where many SDF personnel are reemployed, will be continued, and in December 2023, the All Japan Security Service Association and the Ministry of Defense agreed to collaborate on initiatives related to securing human resources in the security industry and provide smooth reemployment support for SDF personnel scheduled to retire

[12604] Additionally, in order to increase the number of SDF Reserve Personnel and SDF Ready Reserve Personnel, in addition to maintaining and increasing the number of uniformed SDF personnel under the fixed-term system, it is decided that a scholarship would be provided to support the education of individuals who enter a university in Japan after completing their tenure as fixed-term uniformed SDF personnel and who are appointed SDF Reserve Personnel while at university

[12605] Meanwhile, with regard to the re-employment of SDF personnel, the following three regulations, as are the cases in other national government employees, have been put in place to ensure public trust regarding the fairness of official duties: (1) regulation on requesting re-employment of other personnel and retired personnel and on requesting information; (2) regulation on seeking employment opportunities at companies in which the retired personnel had a stake whilst in office; and (3) regulation on requests (lobbying) by re-employed personnel. Compliance with these regulations is monitored by bodies comprised of academic experts with no history of serving as SDF personnel

[12606] Any violation of these regulations will be strictly dealt with through the imposition of penalties

[12607] Additionally, for the purpose of the appropriate implementation of centralized management and disclosure of re-employment information by the Cabinet, it has been decided that information on the re-employment status of retired SDF personnel who were in managerial positions (equivalent to the position of Senior Coordinator in the MOD or higher) is to be published every fiscal year by the Cabinet

[12608] The Monument for SDF Personnel who Perished in the Line of Duty was constructed in 1962 in Ichigaya

[12609] In 1998, the Memorial Zone in its current form was completed by combining this monument with other monuments located in the same area

[12610] The MOD holds an annual memorial ceremony for SDF personnel who perished in the line of Duty, led by the Minister of Defense and with the attendance of surviving family members and the Prime Minister

[12611] At the Monument for SDF Personnel who Perished in the Line of Duty in the Memorial Zone, there is an iron plate containing the names and other information of personnel who perished in the line of Duty

[12612] When foreign dignitaries such as Defense Ministers visit the MOD, they make offerings of flowers, expressing their respect and condolences to personnel who perished in the line of Duty

[12613] Memorial ceremonies are also held at individual SDF posts and bases

[12663] Creating an Organizational Environment of Zero Tolerance for Harassment of Any Kind

[12664] The Japanese people have high expectations of the MOD/ SDF, and it is indispensable for us to gain their support and trust all the time to fully exercise our ability to complete our duties

[12665] In order to meet their expectations to this end, the SDF personnel are required to be an invariably disciplined existence more than ever

[12666] The MOD/SDF has taken various measures such as thorough instructions on service discipline in order to foster well-disciplined personnel

[12667] However, disciplinary action has been taken in recent years for a number of cases of harassment

[12668] In order to exert organizational strength and respond decisively to a wide range of situations, the MOD/SDF must create a working environment that enables SDF personnel, who are the core of Japan’s defense capability, to perform their tasks confidently with high morale and peace of mind

[12669] Harassment, in particular, must not be tolerated, as it destroys mutual trust among the personnel of MOD/SDF, which are fundamentally based on unit actions and shakes the very foundation of the organization

[12670] Given this understanding, the MOD/SDF is committed to addressing harassment cases and fundamentally reviewing harassment prevention measures with a sense of urgency to create an environment where harassment is absolutely not tolerated

[12671] Response to Harassment Incidents

[12672] The MOD/SDF have established a hotline for consultation from SDF personnel

[12673] The annual number of consultations was 109 when the hotline was permanently established in

[12674] FY2016 and has since increased to 857 in FY

[12675] Power harassment, in particular, which accounts for about 80% of the total number of such consultations, is a major problem; such harassment could lead to a violation of the dignity and human rights of MOD/SDF personnel, suicide incidents, and adversely affect the work environment

[12676] Power harassment is caused by inadequate knowledge of it and the communication gap between superiors and their subordinates

[12677] In order to resolve and prevent these issues, the MOD/SDF has provided classroom training and remote learning to enhance understanding and raise awareness of power harassment among MOD/SDF personnel; conducted education to promote understanding and enhance leadership capabilities among MOD/SDF personnel (particularly those in managerial positions); and taken measures to improve and strengthen the consultation system

[12678] In order to eradicate disciplinary violations, such as assault and battery, power harassment, and so on, the standards of disciplinary actions were tightened in

[12679] The number of cases of harassment for which disciplinary actions were taken was 549 in FY

[12680] Of these, 30 personnel were subject to the heaviest disciplinary action of discharge (3 power harassment cases and 27 sexual harassment cases

[12681] Furthermore, as some personnel are reluctant to seek advice at the SDF consultation desk, a consultation desk staffed by counselors and other professionals outside of the SDF on weekends, holidays, and after-hours has been established in addition to the existing consultation desk staffed by lawyers

[12682] However, despite the various harassment prevention measures that have been adopted so far, there have been cases where harassment has occurred and the response was inadequate

[12683] For example, there was a case of a former GSDF personnel who had lodged a complaint that they were subject to sexual harassment during training and on a daily basis at their unit, but the information was not reported to the commanding officer, and the facts of the case were not properly investigated

[12684] Following the complaint by the individual, an investigation conducted by a higher-level unit, it was determined in September 2022 that sexual harassment, including sexual violence, had indeed occurred, and disciplinary actions for those involved were taken in the same year

[12685] Such incidents suggest that the effects of the MOD’s existing harassment prevention measures are inadequate in terms of effectiveness, and is extremely serious and deeply regrettable

[12686] Types of disciplinary action include dismissal, demotion, suspension, reduction in pay, and reprimand

[12687] The disciplinary actions taken are determined based on a comprehensive evaluation of the causes, motives, and circumstances of the disciplinary violation, the position and rank of the offender, as well as the impact of the disciplinary violation both inside and outside the unit

[12700] Directive, etc., of the Minister of Defense on Measures to Eradicate Harassment

[12701] On September of 2022, then Defense Minister Hamada issued a directive on measures to eradicate harassment, in which (1) all personnel once again be informed of harassment consultation helpdesk’s and counselor’s availability and encourage them to seek consultation and report any harassment accordingly, (2) urgent review of the current status of harassment-related consultations and the appropriate follow-up in all cases, (3) special defense inspection of the entire MOD/SDF, and (4) establishment of an advisory panel to conduct a fundamental review of harassment prevention measures

[12702] Furthermore, in August 2023, following the recommendations of “The Ministry of Defense Committee of Experts on Harassment Prevention Measures” described below, the then Minister of Defense Hamada issued a message to all personnel, emphasizing that each member is responsible for creating an environment in which harassment is not tolerated and that it is urgent to review and create fundamental measures promptly

[12703] Minister of Defense Kihara instructed to eradicate harassment, etc

[12704] In October of the same year, in response to harassment incidents that occurred in the Maritime Self

[12705] Defense Force, Minister of Defense Kihara issued “The

[12706] Minister of Defense Instructions on Strict Measures for Harassment Response.”

[12707] He directed the immediate investigation of cases reported through special defense inspections, urgent review of individual cases, and swift reporting of unreported cases to ensure strict handling of all harassment incidents

[12708] Additionally, Minister of

[12709] Defense Kihara issued a message to all personnel and commanders/management personnel, urging each member to be aware of their role, actively work on harassment prevention, consult without hesitation if they experience harassment, and support victims promptly if they witness or receive reports of harassment, taking appropriate action without delay

[12710] The Ministry of Defense Committee of Experts on Harassment Prevention Measures

[12711] Based on the directive of the Minister of Defense in September 2022, “The Ministry of Defense Committee of Experts on Harassment Prevention Measures” was established in November

[12712] This panel conducted a fundamental review of harassment prevention measures, which included eight discussions in total, on-site inspections at each Self-Defense Force unit, and interactions with personnel

[12713] The panel also exchanged views with a former member of the Ground Self-Defense Force who was a victim of sexual harassment and considered the results of special defense inspections on harassment prevention status, which will be described later

[12714] In August 2023, after reviewing these issues, the panel submitted recommendations to the MOD regarding “The Fundamental Review of Harassment Prevention Measures”

[12715] The panel pointed out in the recommendations that the MOD/SDF is still in the process of fostering an organizational culture that does not tolerate harassment and that efforts in this regard are inadequate

[12716] It also highlighted that the responsibility of the supervisor (commanders) are unclear regarding harassment prevention measures and that they lack awareness of their duties and outlined strategies that the MOD should undertake in the areas of (1) preventive measures, (2) response to incidents, and (3) post-incident measures

[12717] Specifically, the panel proposed reforms to organizational culture through measures such as regular issuance of messages from the top management, reviewing of training, improving the qualifications of counselors, accelerating the resolution of problems (disciplinary actions), and disseminating information on disciplinary measures

[12718] The Special Defense Inspection on Harassment Prevention Status

[12719] Based on the directive of the Minister of Defense in September 2022, the Defense Inspection General’s Office of legal compliance conducted a special defense inspection on the status of harassment prevention status and accepted harassment reports and/or complaints from MOD/SDF personnel regarding harassment consultation and response

[12720] The Defense Inspection General’s Office of legal compliance interviewed the complainants to determine the basic facts of the harassment incidents, and eventually reviewed regarding the final 1,325 cases that were reported by the end of November 2022 deadline

[12721] Taking into account the complainants’ preferences, they notified the relevant agencies where the incidents occurred and proceeded with detailed investigations

[12722] “Results of Special Defense Inspection” were publicly announced in August

[12723] The results of the special defense inspection revealed that the counselors and consultation desk were not being adequately utilized

[12724] More than 60% of the complaints alleging inadequate handling of harassment incidents revealed that the complainants had not even sought advice from counselors or consultation desk

[12725] There are concerns about the adequate response by counselors and consultation desk, and the situation arising after consultations, casting doubts about whether the harassment consultation system was effectively fulfilling its intended role

[12726] Moreover, numerous complaints were voiced about dissatisfaction with the responses received despite seeking consultation

[12727] Dissatisfaction with responses to complaints was confirmed to potentially contribute to the ineffectiveness of the harassment consultation system

[12728] Therefore, this Special Defense Inspection indicated a need to improve and thoroughly implement harassment prevention measures, including the consultation system, as a corrective measure

[12729] Japanese Only

[12730] In December 2022, a Maritime Self-Defense Force member reported to their superior that they had been subjected to sexual harassment while on duty

[12731] Despite the individual's wishes, the individual was compelled to meet with the perpetrator, another member of the unit, and receive an apology

[12732] The perpetrator and the superior received suspensions in November 2023, with the former receiving a 10-month suspension and the latter a 3-month suspension

[12733] The Fundamental Review of Harassment Prevention Measures

[12734] As part of its future actions, the MOD, based on the results of the expert committee and the Special Defense Inspection, formed a Harassment Prevention Measures Review Team in August 2023 to examine effective measures, including a review of consultation systems and education

[12735] Specifically, the aim is to reform organizational culture that may contribute to harassment, with plans for regular messages from the top management including the Minister of Defense, as well as utilizing educational opportunities to reform personnel awareness

[12736] Additionally, there are plans to review harassment prevention education, provide training to improve the qualifications of managers (commanders) and counselors, standardize and clarify disciplinary action criteria, expand the harassment consultation system, and increase awareness of consultation services

[12737] In November 2023, Minister of Defense Kihara convened “The Meeting on Harassment Prevention.”

[12738] He instructed ministry officials to raise the awareness of each member, especially supervisors and commanders of the organization, to take leadership in preventing harassment, to prioritize support for the victim members first, and to respond promptly to harassment

[12739] He stated that team members who had been victimized should not hesitate to report it to their supervisors or the reporting desk and that any member who witnessed the victimization should report it on behalf of the victimized members of the team

[12740] Furthermore, during “The Defense Ministry Employee Harassment Prevention Month” in FY2023, efforts were made to intensively raise awareness of harassment prevention measures through various educational activities and discussions, including those conducted by external experts

[12741] Conference on Harassment Prevention convened by the MOD (November

[12742] We will continue to ensure that all SDF personnel are thoroughly educated on harassment

[12743] We will also continuously review and update our measures to keep up with the times, incorporating insights from external experts

[12744] Our goal is to create an environment in which harassment is not tolerated at all. REFERENCE

[12745] Promotion of harassment prevention measures and consultation desk (Japanese Only

[12746] Section 3 Further Promotion of Work-Life Balance and Women’s Participation

[12747] Japan is facing the most severe and complex security environment since the end of World War II, and the situations that require a response by the MOD/SDF are increasing in number and becoming longer in duration

[12748] On the other hand, Japan faces rapidly declining birth rate, making it more difficult than ever to secure SDF personnel who are the core of defense capabilities

[12749] Under these circumstances, it is expected that an increasing number of MOD/SDF personnel, both male and female, who are responsible for various duties, will face time and commuting constraints for childcare, and nursing care and other reason due to major changes in the social structure

[12750] Amid such challenging circumstances, ensuring preparedness to consistently respond to various situations requires creating an environment that enables staff to be sound both mentally and physically, maintain high morale and pride, and fully demonstrate their abilities

[12751] To this end, the MOD/SDF will promote better work-life balance and the active participation of female personnel based on the NDS, etc

[12752] Specifically, the MOD/SDF established the Action Plan in 2015 in order to promote work-life balance of female personnel and conducted various initiatives

[12753] In 2021, the MOD/SDF established a new action plan based around the pillars of (1) reform of promoting work-life balance, and (2) promoting women’s active participation

[12754] In March 2023, the MOD/SDF is further advancing initiatives through revising the Action Plan focused on the following five items, (1) promotion of work from home, (2) transition to paperless work environment, (3) rigorous management of working hours, (4) promotion of paternity leave, and (5) establishment of a workplace environment in which all personnel can work comfortably

[12755] Working Style Reform to Promote Work-Life Balance

[12756] Value and Mentality Reform

[12757] In order to promote working style reform, focus needs to be placed especially on reforming the values and mentality of staff in managerial positions regarding working style

[12758] The MOD/SDF has been issuing top management messages and conducting seminars and lectures aimed at raising awareness of working style reforms and the concept of work-life balance

[12759] With the increase of personnel facing time/commuting constraints for child/family care, the MOD/SDF is also promoting correction of long working hours, encouraging taking leave, and telework to ensure proper work-life balance so that all personnel can exert his/her full potential

[12760] In addition, the MOD/SDF is conducting initiatives for “management reform” aimed at enhancing the management ability of administrative staff

[12761] Working Style Reform in the Workplace

[12762] Efforts aimed at the promotion of work-life balance will lead to effective initiatives and the creation of a culture in which personnel consider specific measures for improving their workplace environment based on the actual conditions of their workplace

[12763] Based on this perspective, the MOD has been holding the “Competition for Initiatives to Promote Working Style Reform at the Ministry of Defense” with awards presented to particularly outstanding initiatives, which are then introduced within the MOD to help other personnel reform their working styles

[12764] Flexible Working Hours and Location

[12765] In light of workload fluctuations and the time constraints faced by individuals such as childcare, nursing care, etc., the MOD/SDF has introduced an early/late shifts and a flex-time system to allow for the flexible selection of working hours

[12766] In April 2023, further flexibility is being pursued, including a reduction in core hours under the flextime system

[12767] In the MOD/SDF, considering the uniqueness of certain jobs, work from home has now been made possible at all institutions, except for those jobs where work from home is not feasible

[12768] The MOD/SDF will continue to promote digitalization, including the computerization of documents as well as the installation of more terminals, in order to establish business processes in which tasks can be completed with work from home

[12769] Rigorous Management of Working Hours

[12770] Through the systemization of working hour management, surveys conducted on overtime work, etc., efforts are being made to rectify the long working hours that may be detrimental to the physical and mental health and welfare of personnel

[12771] Development of an Environment that Enables Personnel to Play an Active Role while Engaging in Childcare and Nursing Care

[12772] The MOD/SDF has developed various schemes that enable its personnel to balance work with their childcare/nursing care commitments, such as hiring fixed-term staff who take over those on childcare or other leave

[12773] In particular, the MOD/SDF is working to enable all male personnel with a newborn child to take paternity leave or time off work

[12774] As part of the efforts, the MOD/SDF is encouraging all male personnel with a newborn child to take paternity leave or time off work for approximately one month or more

[12775] The MOD/SDF is also developing an environment that enables its personnel to balance work life with their family life through various initiatives, such as by providing explanations on systems related to childcare and nursing care, introducing role models, and creating “childcare forms” to help managers and the human resources department better understand the details of the situation surrounding their personnel’s childcare

[12776] A system has also been established to allow SDF personnel who retired mid-career due to childcare or nursing care commitments to be re-employed

[12777] Ensuring Childcare Services

[12778] Developing an environment in which MOD/SDF personnel are able to devote themselves to their duties without worrying about childcare or other concerns is important in maintaining a permanent state of readiness

[12779] The MOD/SDF has set up workplace nurseries at camps and bases in eight locations across Japan

[12780] In addition, in the event of situations where a quick response is required such as disaster relief, the MOD promotes support measures to provide temporary childcare in SDF camps and bases for children of SDF personnel

[12782] For the further expansion of the recruitment and promotion of female personnel, the MOD/SDF has been making various efforts to promote the activities of motivated and qualified female personnel by setting up specific goals under the Action Plan

[12783] Moreover, as part of its efforts related to Women, Peace and Security (WPS), Japan is promoting the participation of women in disaster prevention and disaster response efforts and decision-making for security policy

[12784] The MOD/SDF, which is the main entities in these efforts, is working on promoting women’s participation and conducting various activities related to the WPS field both in Japan and overseas

[12785] As the importance of activities considering the needs of women and girls who are placed in particularly vulnerable situations during conflicts and disasters grows both in Japan and overseas, the MOD/SDF recognizes that all personnel are the main contributors to WPS and aims to further contribute to the promotion of WPS through the promotion of women’s participation, etc

[12786] A concept that encapsulates the idea that peace is more sustainable when women take the lead and actively participate in all levels of conflict prevention, response and reconstruction, and peacebuilding, as well as disaster prevention, while recognizing the importance of protection and relief for women and girls, and those in need, as they are more vulnerable during conflicts and disasters

[12788] Expansion of the Recruitment and Promotion of Female Personnel

[12805] Significance of Promoting Active Engagement of Female SDF Personnel and Personnel Management Policy

[12806] With SDF duties becoming increasingly diverse and complex, SDF personnel are required more than ever to have multifaceted capabilities, including higher levels of knowledge, decision-making ability, and skills

[12807] In addition, under a severe recruitment environment due to the declining birth rate and continuing trend of higher education, it is anticipated that the number of SDF personnel with time and location restraints, including those involved in childcare, nursing care, and other responsibilities, will significantly increase

[12808] In light of these changes, the SDF is required to evolve from a conventional organization with an emphasis on homogeneity among the members, into an organization that is capable of incorporating diverse human resources in a flexible manner

[12809] At present, the largest human resource that the SDF has not been able to fully utilize is women, who account for half of the population targeted for recruitment

[12810] Promoting the active engagement of female SDF personnel has the following significance: (1) securing useful human resources; (2) utilizing diverse perspectives; and (3) reflecting values of the nation

[12811] For this reason, the MOD/SDF has decided to open up a path for female personnel with motivation, ability, and aptitude to have opportunities to demonstrate their abilities in various fields, with the aim of doubling the ratio of female SDF personnel

[12812] In terms of employing and promoting female SDF personnel, the MOD/SDF sets out a personnel management policy to ensure equal opportunity between men and women and assign the right person to the right place based on the person’s motivation and ability/aptitude

[12813] Removal of the Assignment Restriction of Female SDF Personnel

[12814] The MOD/SDF has completely removed the assignment restriction of female SDF personnel with the exception of units to which female personnel cannot be assigned for reasons of maternity protection (namely, part of the GSDF Nuclear Biological Chemical (NBC) Weapon Defense Unit [chemical] as well as Tunnel Company Units

[12815] As a result, the assignment of female personnel to vocations, such as fighter pilots, paratroopers, and submarine crew members, is currently underway

[12842] Section 4 Transformation of Medical Functions

[12843] The NDS stipulates that, from the perspective of sustainability and resiliency, the SDF medical force, which has been placing importance on sustaining the health of SDF personnel, will transform into an organization that saves the lives of SDF personnel who carry out their missions in a contingency in spite of danger

[12844] Under circumstances where the SDF’s missions are becoming more diverse and internationalized, it is important to accurately address the needs of various medical activities, such as providing medical support in disaster relief operations and international peace cooperation activities, as well as capacity building on military medicine

[12845] The MOD/SDF, therefore, is enhancing the medical functions: (i

[12846] Strengthening seamless medical care and evacuation posture from the frontlines to the destination hospital, (i) Reinforcement of integrated medical operational posture, and (ii) Fundamental management reform of the National Defense Medical College as the three pillars to improve the combat trauma care capabilities

[12847] In addition, the MOD/SDF is further enhancing and strengthening its medical capabilities so that they can appropriately respond to various emergency events and carry out its multiple missions in Japan and abroad

[12909] Initiative to Enhance Combat Casualty Care Capabilities

[12910] The Blood Transfusion Strategy of the Ministry of Defense for Treatment of Combat Injuries

[12911] Most deaths in war are due to exsanguination from bomb wounds, gunshot wounds, and other similar causes

[12912] Securing and using blood products for transfusion to prevent such deaths is extremely important

[12913] However, it is necessary to gather the opinions of external experts on measures concerning blood products and medical treatment using blood products from the perspective of medical efficacy, safety, and ethics

[12914] Thus, the Study Meeting on

[12915] Blood Transfusion in Combat Casualty Care by the MOD/SDF was established under the Parliamentary Vice-Minister of Defense

[12916] Matsumoto

[12917] Based on the common understanding that simple, safe, and speedy use and management of blood transfusion is required in combat casualty care, which is subject to geographical, human, and material constraints, the panel of experts determined that, given the unique environment surrounding combat casualty care, it would be appropriate for the MOD/SDF to prepare a blood transfusion protocol manual that takes every possible measure to improve the survival rate of soldiers, in addition to transfusion procedures based on domestic guidelines prescribed by the

[12918] Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare

[12919] The panel of experts also identified various issues to be addressed when preparing the protocol, such as human resource development, establishment of a system within the ministry, and preparation of safety management and utilization procedures, and gave recommendations for solving these issues

[12920] Based on the recommendations, the MOD/SDF will formulate a blood transfusion strategy that can be used appropriately and ensures safety so that the lives of as many members as possible can be saved

[12921] as well as promoting the necessary research in defense medicine to advance the quality of the SDF’s medical services in areas such as the treatment of trauma, burns, and physical injuries, infectious disease control, and mental health

[12922] In particular, research on artificial platelet could be beneficial in treating combat injuries if it can be successfully put to practical use

[12923] In addition, in FY 2024, a “Center for Trauma, Burn and Tactical Medicine” will be newly established at the

[12924] NDMC to train medical and nursing officers capable of providing medical care for combat trauma care

[12925] In addition, an operational posture will be established to provide highly advanced medical care at the NDMC

[12947] Section 5 Reinforcing Policy-Making Function

[12948] The NDS stipulates that, for the SDF to fully exert its capabilities and respond to the severe, complex, and fast- paced strategic environment, strategic and agile defense policy planning and making are required, including in domains such as space, cyber, and electromagnetic spectrum

[12949] To fundamentally strengthen these functions, the NDS calls for closely cooperating with relevant ministries and agencies, private research institutions, and private companies, particularly those in the defense industry, as well as reviewing and reinforcing the research system of the MOD/SDF led by the National

[12950] Institute for Defense Studies (NIDS) and reinforcing its function as an intellectual base

[12951] Efforts for Reinforcing Policy-Making Function

[12952] It was clearly stated in the NDS that the need to fundamentally reinforce strategic and agile defense policy planning functions, a consultation framework will be established to obtain policy advice from experts

[12953] Based on this policy, the first meeting of the “Advisory Panel on the Fundamental Strengthening of Defense Capabilities” was held in February 2024, bringing together experts and specialists from various fields

[12954] Capabilities” was held in February 2024, bringing together experts and specialists from various fields

[12955] During this meeting, candid discussions were held on the fundamental reinforcement of defense capabilities and the relationship between security and economic growth

[12956] In addition, the National Defense Strategy states that the MOD/SDF will strengthen its posture to comprehensively advance, from a strategic perspective, the SDF’s future ways of warfare and the utilization and nurturing of cutting-edge technologies and application of those technologies to defense equipment necessary for future SDF operations, while closely cooperating with relevant ministries and agencies, private research institutions, and private companies, particularly those with the defense industry as their core

[12957] The MOD’s research and educational institutions, including the National Institute for Defense Studies, are working to improve the quality of their research on a routine basis to produce results that contribute to

[12958] Japan’s policy-making and strengthen its function as an intellectual foundation

[12959] In addition, from the perspective of promoting public understanding of knowledge and information about Japan’s national security policies, including the results of such research: (1) review and strengthen the research system of the

[12960] MOD/SDF by building networking and strengthening institutional collaboration with research and educational institutions, universities, think-tanks, etc., in Japan and abroad; (2) provide policy-quality research results backed by advanced expertise and research capabilities; (3) disseminate highly trustworthy information based on the aforementioned research results, etc.; and (4) contribute to the promotion of security education by dispatching instructors to educational institutions, etc., holding public symposiums, etc., in order to reinforce its intellectual base through NIDS and various schools, among other initiatives

[12961] The National Institute for Defense Studies (NIDS) conducts policy-oriented research and studies primarily on security and military history and policy simulations to promote collaboration with policy-making departments by taking advantage of its unique position as a national academic research and educational institution focused on national security

[12962] In addition, as an educational institution equivalent to the National Defense University of other countries, it also functions as a university-level national defense educational institution for the training of senior MOD/SDF officials, and employees of other ministries and agencies

[12963] NIDS manages and publishes a large volume of data on military history as a facility possessing historical materials, etc. in accordance with the Public Records and Archives Management Act1, and serves as the largest research center on military history in Japan

[12964] In April 2023, the Cyber Security Division was established at NIDS in response to research needs in the increasingly important field of cybersecurity based on the Defense Buildup Program, which calls for a review of the research system to support the augmentation of the functions of strategic and agile defense policy planning and formulation, and reinforcement of its functions as an intellectual foundation

[12965] NIDS, an institution that plays a role in defense exchange and security dialogue also emphasizes international exchange and conducts research exchanges with defense universities, security research institutes, etc., in other countries with the main objective of improving the quality of its research and education and contributing to national security by strengthening relations of trust with said countries

[12966] Specifically, activities include mutual dispatch of researchers for lectures, holding study groups and participating in international conferences, receiving visits from foreign government and military officials, and inviting foreign researchers and experts

[12967] Through these exchanges, the NIDS is improving the quality of its research and studies and strengthening its intellectual network

[12968] In FY2023, the International Symposium on Security was held under the theme “New Horizons in the Nuclear Age,” the International Forum on War History Studies was held under the theme “Japan's Security and the Korean Peninsula during the Cold War.”

[12969] In addition, the International Conference on Policy Simulation “Connections Japan 2023/24” was held by the National Institute of Defense Studies (January 2024) under the theme “Development of Policy Simulation Techniques for the Security Environment in the Indo-Pacific Region.”

[12970] This international conference was held as an opportunity to introduce the latest knowledge and discussions held in Japan and abroad on various security issues, and it will continue focus on timely themes to help address policy-related issues and reinforce Japan’s intellectual base

[12971] In addition, NIDS proactively disseminates information by publishing major research results on its website and issuing various publications, such as the “NIDS China Security Report” and “Security & Strategy,” which have been published annually to date

[12972] Researchers at NIDS have also published many books, articles, and essays on their research findings, some of which have received awards for the outstanding research conducted

[12973] Part III, Chapter 1, Section 4-5 (Responses in the Cyber Domain) Actions by Other Institutions

[12974] The National Defense Academy of Japan (NDA) is responsible for training and educating individuals who are expected to become SDF officers, providing more advanced training and education for SDF personnel, etc., and conducting the research needed to perform these functions

[12975] In its role, the NDA conducts a large volume of fundamental research related to general academic and defense policy-related research, and upholds and improves a high standard of research

[12976] In addition, the results of the NDA’s research that is mainly centered on the themes handled by the Center for Global Security are widely disseminated outside the academy through presentations at seminars and colloquia held by the NDA as well as through online publications, such as the Global Security Seminar Series and the Global Security Study Series

[12977] SDF Command and Staff Colleges, etc., periodically hold various security-related seminars and symposiums that are attended by researchers, including overseas researchers and foreign military personnel, etc., from industry (companies), government (national and local), and academia (universities, etc.), which contributes to research and studies regarding Japan’s national security opinions and the exchange of opinions from a variety of different perspectives in the future through discussions

[12978] The colleges also strive to obtain knowledge and information necessary for research and studies to maintain and improve the quality of their education and research by hosting visiting researchers as well as participating in exchanges, etc., with educational and research institutions, etc., in Japan and overseas

[12979] The colleges proactively disseminate information by publishing major research results and initiatives on their websites, issuing various publications, and through other means

[12980] Commentary

[12981] National Defense Academy Graduation Ceremony

[12982] The National Defense Academy's graduation ceremony was held on March

[12983] Prime Minister Kishida attended the ceremony and addressed the graduates as the Supreme Commander of the Self-Defense Forces

[12984] In his address, Prime Minister Kishida quoted the ancient Roman maxim, “If you want peace, prepare for war”, emphasizing the necessity of deterrence to avert wars and safeguard peace

[12985] He affirmed that Japan must strive to enhance its diplomatic power and significantly strengthen its defense forces

[12986] Prime Minister Kishida motivated the graduates, emphasizing that the strengthening of the defense forces cannot be achieved merely by increasing and renewing the SDF's equipment, and said the graduates performing important duties to make the defense forces function in the future, themselves form the core of the defense forces, that their efforts are indispensable for the strengthening of the defense forces, and that the very existence of each graduate will act as a deterrent to war

[12987] Prime Minister Kishida at the graduation ceremony of the National Defense Academy (March

[12989] Measures Related to Training and Exercises

[12990] Chapter I. Training and Exercise Initiatives

[12991] In order for the MOD/SDF to fulfil its mission of defending our nation, it is essential for all personnel and every unit, which is the core of the defense force, to maintain a high level of training and improve upon their skills on a regular basis

[12992] It can be said that a high level of capabilities and skills is the foundation of our nation’s deterrence and response capabilities

[12993] The MOD/SDF actively conducts various high-level bilateral/multilateral training and exercises, and various exercises involving other ministries and local governments to further improve deterrence and response capabilities

[12994] It is essential to strengthen deterrence and response capabilities and stabilize the security environment surrounding Japan to maintain peace in Japan

[12995] To this end, the MOD/SDF is actively promoting bilateral/multilateral exercises with Japan’s ally, like-minded countries, and others in the wider Indo-Pacific region as part of its efforts to achieve the vision of a “Free and Open Indo-Pacific.”

[12996] In particular, MOD/SDF is strengthening its partnerships in the Indo-Pacific region, which is closely connected to Japan’s national security, and is working to create a security environment that does not tolerate unilateral changes to the status quo by force and such attempts, by maintaining and improving the capabilities and skills of each country through common efforts such as bilateral/multilateral exercises with allied, like-minded countries, and by strengthening deterrence and response capabilities through collaboration and cooperation, thereby creating a synergistic effect

[12997] In addition to these efforts, the MOD/SDF is also working to strengthen cooperation in responding to global security challenges and destabilizing factors to which it is difficult for any individual country to respond

[13004] Training that Contributes to Reinforcing Japan’s Capability to Respond to Various Contingencies

[13005] Joint Training of the SDF

[13006] It is of paramount importance that the SDF be prepared to seamlessly and fully demonstrate its deterrence and response capabilities through repeated training involving joint operations of the GSDF, MSDF, and ASDF on a routine basis

[13007] To this end, the SDF has been conducting SDF joint exercises since 1979 to rehearse joint operations by alternating between field training exercises and command post exercises almost every year

[13008] In addition, in order to respond to large-scale disasters and various other disasters in an expeditious and appropriate manner, the SDF organizes various disaster prevention drills while also actively participating in disaster prevention drills organized by the Japanese Government and local governments as part of its efforts to strengthen cooperation with various ministries and agencies, local governments, etc

[13009] Furthermore, the SDF has been conducting training regularly so that it can immediately rescue or transport Japanese nationals and others overseas, in emergency situations

[13010] SDF Joint Exercise (JX

[13011] In November 2023, the SDF conducted “Joint Exercise,” a nationwide joint exercise for FY 2023 as a field training exercise

[13012] This was the SDF’s largest-scale field training exercises, with approximately 30,000 participants from the GSDF, MSDF, and ASDF

[13013] The exercise was conducted in a comprehensive manner based on a series of hypothetical scenarios ranging from gray-zone situations to armed attack situations in order to respond to armed attacks in various domains, including in the space, cyberspace and electromagnetic domains

[13014] U.S. forces engaged in some exercises to maintain and strengthen Japan-U. S. coordination

[13015] In addition to ASDF fighter jets using civilian airports for the first time as joint training, the exercise also included maneuver deployment training of units using civilian vessels and ports, joint use of U. S. military bases, and disaster drills on remote islands

[13016] This realistic and advanced exercise maintained and improved the SDF’s joint operation capabilities

[13017] Joint Exercise for Rescue (JXR

[13018] In order to maintain and enhance its disaster response capabilities, the SDF conducts disaster drills revolving around its command and staff activities in the event of a large-scale earthquake, the coordination between major units, and its coordination with disaster prevention organizations as well as the U. S. Forces in Japan

[13019] During this exercise conducted in June 2023 based on the hypothetical scenario that a Nankai Trough earthquake had occurred, the SDF tested its response plan by conducting drills for emergency transportation of troops and equipment to isolated areas and transportation of supplies to isolated disaster areas along the coast, assuming a situation where isolated areas have occurred, thereby improving its ability to respond to disasters

[13020] Remote Island Disaster Relief Exercise (RIDEX) and Tomodachi Rescue Exercise (TREX), a Japan-U. S. Bilateral Integrated Disaster Response Exercise

[13021] The SDF conducts field training exercises on responding to sudden large-scale disasters on remote islands to maintain and enhance the SDF’s ability to respond to disasters on remote islands as well as strengthen collaboration with the U. S. Forces and relevant disaster prevention organizations

[13022] Comprehensive Disaster Prevention Drill “Disaster Prevention Day.”

[13023] The MOD/SDF conducted an operation drill at the Disaster Response Headquarters of the MOD on September 1, 2023, assuming the occurrence of an earthquake directly under the Tokyo metropolitan area, so that the SDF can be quickly and systematically dispatched when a disaster such as a large-scale earthquake occurs

[13024] In addition, the MOD/SDF participated in disaster drills conducted by local governments

[13025] Commentary: 2023 Self-Defense Forces Joint Exercise “05JX”

[13026] To help achieve a drastic reinforcement of defense capabilities amid the increasingly tense security environment surrounding Japan, the SDF conducted their largest-ever military exercise in November 2023, designated 05JX

[13027] The SDF was able to use this exercise to improve operational capability by including the space, cyberspace, and electromagnetic domains into ground, maritime, and air operations, such as integrated anti-ship attack and integrated air and missile defense, and through cross-domain training

[13028] In addition, where training for ground operations and amphibious operations had previously been conducted by function, these operations were now organically linked and carried out comprehensively, closely connecting command post activities at the operational command center with the movements of field units to achieve integrated operational and tactical levels

[13029] JX was thus more practical and sophisticated than ever

[13030] Thanks to the deep understanding of residents and the cooperation of the relevant local governments, the SDF was able to conduct fighter aircraft takeoff and landing training at the Okayama, Oita, Amami, and Tokunoshima airports during 05JX

[13031] The participation of the U. S. armed forces in part of this exercise, along with countries like Australia, Canada, France, New Zealand, Philippines, the ROK, the UK, Germany, and NATO attending as observers, also contributed to strengthening cooperation with allies and like-minded countries

[13032] With a strong determination to prevent any unilateral change in the status quo or attempts to do so by force, the MOD/SDF are committed to further strengthening the deterrence and response capabilities to protect the peace and security of Japan through these training exercises

[13043] Training of Each SDF Service. A high-level of training by each SDF is a fundamental prerequisite for being able to fully exert joint defense capabilities

[13044] As such, each SDF continuously conducts individual training for its troops and organizational training for its units, forming the foundation of a strong SDF

[13045] The GSDF conducts field training exercises at the regional army level to improve its response capabilities for various contingencies and other situations

[13046] Furthermore, GSDF units from across the country conduct Ground Self-Defense Force exercises

[13047] They strive to improve their operation execution capabilities and operational effectiveness by demonstrating various unit actions while contributing to enhancing deterrence and response capabilities

[13048] In addition, it conducts parachute drop training from U.S. Air Force and other aircraft in Japan and overseas, training for amphibious operations, and live-fire training for Medium range SAM/SSM (Surface-to-Air Missile / Surface-to-Ship Missile) units to enhance various tactical skills necessary for joint cross-domain operations

[13049] MSDF

[13050] The MSDF conducts training between naval units, and between naval vessels, aircraft (including the ASDF) and ground units (including the GSDF), as well as mine warfare training in Japan and deployment training that leverages superior U. S. training infrastructure with the cooperation of the U. S. Navy in order to improve various tactical capabilities

[13051] In addition, the MSDF conducts MSDF exercises (field training exercises) in which units all over Japan are mobilized, as part of efforts to enhance readiness

[13052] Section 1 Training and Exercise Initiatives. ANNUAL Exercise 2023 (November

[13053] The “ANNUAL Exercise 2023,” conducted in November 2023, rehearsed commanders’ tactical decisions and unit operational procedures, based on a series of hypothetical situations ranging from the gray zone to an armed attack

[13054] In this largest-ever exercise by the MSDF, in addition to the U. S., Australian, and Canadian navies and air forces, the Philippine Navy participated as an observer for the first time

[13055] Various tactical training exercises, including anti-submarine warfare and anti-surface warfare, were conducted to improve the MSDF’s operation execution capabilities and strengthen cooperation with the navies of participating countries

[13056] The MSDF has also strengthened cooperation with the Japan Coast Guard, and in June 2023, conducted field training exercise with the Japan Coast Guard for the first time after the Minister of Defense established the Control Procedures for the Japan Coast Guard

[13057] This exercise was conducted under the assumption that the Japan Coast Guard would be placed under the control of the Minister of Defense in an armed attack situation and would evacuate residents, provide information to vessels, and perform evacuation support

[13058] Through the exercise, the MSDF rehearsed and verified information communication procedures with the Japan Coast Guard

[13059] In addition, bilateral exercises with the Japan Coast Guard were conducted to enhance joint response capabilities, including training related to comprehensive response and strengthening of cooperation, and training to deal with suspicious vessels

[13062] It also conducts unit-specific training and training on inter-unit coordination procedures involving units, such as fighter units, air warning and control units, and surface-to-air guided missile units, as well as comprehensive training that includes air transport units and air rescue units

[13063] For example, the ASDF conducts the field training exercise Air Defense Command Comprehensive Training, in which all relevant units in Japan are mobilized, as well as PAC-3 maneuver and deployment training, overseas flight training, etc., to enhance maneuver and deployment capabilities and responsiveness
