[13068] Training that Contributes to Strengthening the Japan-U. S. Alliance

[13069] The Japan-U. S. Alliance is essential to Japan’s national security, and Japan-U. S. bilateral exercises play a significant role in enhancing Japan’s deterrence and response capabilities

[13070] The SDF has consistently conducted joint training involving different SDF services as well as Japan-U. S. bilateral joint exercises (field training exercises and command post exercises) to improve the SDF’s tactical skills and strengthen collaboration with the U. S. Forces, demonstrating Japan and the United States’ unified commitment to and capacity for achieving peace and stability in the region

[13071] Japan-U. S. Bilateral Joint Exercises

[13072] Since 1986, the SDF has been conducting the Japan-U. S. bilateral joint exercises “Keen Sword” (field training exercise) and “Keen Edge” (command post exercise) to rehearse SDF operational procedures and the Japan-U. S. Joint Response Plan for armed attack situations, etc., as well as to improve the readiness of the SDF and the interoperability of Japan and the United States

[13073] In FY 2023, the Japan-U. S. bilateral joint exercise, “Keen Edge 24” (command post exercise), was conducted to rehearse command and staff activities for Japan-U. S. joint response to a variety of contingencies and joint operations of the SDF

[13074] Australian defence forces participated in this exercise for the first time and rehearsed command and control to improve the effectiveness of Japan-U. S.-Australia defense cooperation

[13075] In addition, Japan-U. S. joint response drills against ballistic missiles were also conducted to maintain and enhance the SDF’s joint operation capabilities and Japan-U. S. joint response capabilities

[13165] Comments from a Crew Member who Participated in Japan-France Bilateral Exercise

[13166] Tomoko Kondo, Airman 1st Class, Vehicle and Equipment Maintenance Squadron, Maintenance Supply Group, 9th Wing, ASDF C'est une grande chance

[13167] A perfect opportunity

[13168] I participated as a French interpreter in a bilateral exercise between the ASDF and the French Air and Space Force in July

[13169] It was the first time I had been offered a position as an interpreter for this exercise, and I still remember my excitement upon receiving this offer

[13170] This was because my motive to join the military had at last been fulfilled

[13171] On one hand, I felt overwhelmed by the expectations of those around me, as I had to engage in highly specialized interpretation

[13172] However, I wanted to make the most of my friendly nature, the spirit of Japanese hospitality, and my love for the French language and do my best to promote defense cooperation and exchange

[13173] One month before the exercise, I was temporarily assigned to a unit at Nyutabaru Air Base to make various preparations

[13174] Since this was the first-ever bilateral exercise during which French Air and Space Force aircraft visited Japan, it was necessary to prepare everything from scratch

[13175] This involved various activities, including meetings for each event, preparing menus for luncheons, sharing images of French culture and national identity, arranging Japanese-French bilingual moderators, and preparing commentary manuscripts

[13233] Section 2 Establishing the Respective Training Environments and Safety Management

[13234] Training Environment

[13235] Given the increasingly severe security situation surrounding Japan, it is important to work to establish units and other organizations and enhance the quality of the training so that the SDF can exert its capabilities to the fullest

[13236] Because of this, SDF training has been planned and conducted under conditions that are as close as possible to actual combat situations, yet it is necessary to further enhance the training environment in order to maintain and enhance the readiness of the SDF

[13237] It is against this background that the MOD/SDF is promoting initiatives to enhance the training infrastructure in Japan and abroad to conduct efficient and effective training and exercises

[13238] As part of these efforts, the MOD/SDF is working to expand the establishment and utilization of domestic maneuver areas in Hokkaido and elsewhere

[13239] Furthermore, the SDF is also facilitating expanded joint/shared use of U. S. Forces facilities and areas located in Japan by the SDF while accounting for relations with local communities

[13240] Furthermore, the SDF will facilitate the use of places other than SDF facilities or U. S. Forces facilities and areas, and the utilization of excellent training environments overseas, such as the U. S. and Australia, and introduce simulators actively

[13241] Elsewhere, facilities are in the process of being established on Mageshima (Kagoshima Prefecture), where the Ground, Maritime, and Air Self-Defense Forces will be able to conduct training and other activities

[13242] Further, to maximize the capabilities of the SDF in any situation, it is necessary to conduct training using civilian airports regularly

[13243] Based on this belief, ASDF fighter aircraft trainings are conducted at civilian airports as part of the SDF Joint Exercise

[13244] Section I-1-1 (1) (SDF Joint Exercise “JX”) GSDF

[13245] Maneuver areas and ranges are unevenly located and do not have sufficient space

[13246] Thus, the GSDF is unable to conduct exercises with large units or artillery training with extended-range cannons for example

[13247] These constraints tend to grow as equipment is modernized

[13248] There are also constraints imposed by the urbanization of the areas surrounding maneuver areas and ranges

[13249] Rising Thunder, a maximum range firing exercise utilizing the extensive U.S. firing training range (November

[13250] Due to the circumstance, the GSDF conducts live-fire training of surface-to-air guided missile units and surface-to-ship guided missile units in the United States and elsewhere, as it cannot be conducted in Japan

[13251] In addition, the GSDF is improving its tactical skills through participation in field training by utilizing excellent training bases that are not available in Japan, such as multilateral exercises overseas

[13252] In addition, it conducts field training exercises at the division and regional army levels by maximizing the use of limited domestic maneuver areas, and also conducts more practical training outside of SDF facilities and areas while obtaining the understanding and cooperation of local communities

[13253] The timing and location for using sea areas for training around Japan are limited by such factors as weather, ocean conditions, marine traffic, and fisheries

[13254] Because of this, for example, training that must be conducted in relatively shallow sea areas, such as minesweeping training and submarine rescue training, is being conducted in places such as parts of Mutsu Bay and Sagami Bay

[13255] A new minesweeping exercise was conducted at the Sea of Sumounada in western Kyushu in March

[13256] In addition, the MSDF is improving its tactical skills through participation in bilateral/multilateral exercises overseas, such as sending a minesweeper unit to the U. S.-hosted International Maritime Exercise (CUTLASS EXPRESS (IMX-CE)) held in the Middle East

[13257] Furthermore, with the increase in the number of overseas missions, the MSDF also strives to conduct training systematically and efficiently so that a large number of units will be able to produce training results in a short amount of time

[13258] Through participation in multilateral exercises conducted overseas and entering the same training areas, and bilateral and multilateral exercises etc., when returning to base, we are working to improve efficient and effective tactical skills and strengthen cooperation and response capabilities with our ally and like-minded countries. 3 ASDF

[13259] Currently, since much of the training airspace surrounding Japan is not broad enough, the performance and features of aircraft cannot be fully demonstrated in some training

[13260] In addition, long trips to and from the training airspace are required in the case of some bases

[13261] Furthermore, in operating airports, it is necessary to take great care regarding aircraft noise in conducting early morning and nighttime flight training

[13262] Because of this, the ASDF strives to ensure that its training is systematic and efficient

[13263] In the Iwo-To training airspace, for example, aircraft are dispatched successively from the units to conduct training intensively, focusing on training that cannot be conducted sufficiently on the mainland and other exercises

[13264] In addition, it conducts bombing and gunnery training with live ammunition by such means as joint use of USFJ bombing and gunnery areas

[13265] Other efforts are being made to utilize the overseas training environment such as the live-fire training for Patriot missiles by anti-aircraft units in the United States

[13267] Initiatives for Safety Management, etc

[13268] The Ministry of Defense (MOD)/SDF constantly strive as one for safety management, such as by implementing the highest level of safety measures and precautions during routine training

[13269] In April 2023, a UH-60JA, a multipurpose helicopter (with 10 crew members) from the GSDF Vice-Camp Takayubaru (Kumamoto Prefecture) was involved in an accident in which it disappeared from radar when flying over the ocean north-northwest of Miyakojima Island, Okinawa, during an aerial reconnaissance and all 10 members died in the line of duty

[13270] In March 2024, the MOD announced the results of an investigation into an accident involving a two-engine aircraft in which a gradual loss of power in the second engine, followed by a loss of power in the first engine, occurred, which had never been reported before, making it difficult to maintain altitude and causing the aircraft to crash

[13271] As measures to prevent recurrence, we will conduct more detailed checks and inspections to identify the causes of the decrease in the output of both engines and thoroughly implement measures such as training on how to respond to similar incidents to prevent recurrence and ensure flight safety

[13272] Following the crash of the U.S. Air Force CV-22 (Osprey) off the coast of Yakushima in November 2023, the MOD has requested the U. S. side that the Ospreys deployed in Japan be flown after the safety of the flight has been confirmed, except the aircraft conducting the search and rescue operations

[13273] The MOD has also requested early provision of information regarding the circumstances and causes of the accident

[13274] Flights of GSDF V-22 (Osprey) have been suspended temporarily until the circumstances of the accident are clarified

[13275] Ospreys of the U. S. Air Force deployed in Japan have not flown since December

[13276] From December 7 of the same year, the U. S. military suspended operations of Ospreys by all military services using Ospreys

[13277] On March 8, 2024, the U. S. Forces announced that it would lift the grounding measures of Ospreys and the MOD has received extremely detailed information from the U. S. side regarding the circumstances, causes, and safety measures of the accident

[13278] Based on the professional perspectives of the MOD/SDF and from the standpoint of possessing and operating Ospreys, the MOD independently assessed that the U.S. Forces’ cause analysis and safety measures regarding the accident are reasonable, and has concluded that operations of Ospreys, including the GSDF Osprey, can be resumed safely

[13279] Japan and the United States confirmed that flights would resume in sequence

[13280] From the 14 of the same month, Japanese and U. S. Ospreys in Japan will resume flight operations, starting with flights deemed safe by taking necessary safety measures

[13281] Regarding the resumption of Osprey operations, Japan and the U. S. have confirmed at every level that ensuring flight safety is the top priority

[13282] Japan and the U. S. will continue cooperating to take all possible measures to ensure safety

[13285] Furthermore, in light of the collision between a Japan Airlines aircraft and a Japan Coast Guard aircraft at Tokyo International Airport in January 2024, MOD/SDF is advancing necessary measures to prevent similar accidents by working closely with the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism (MLIT

[13286] In April 2024, during a nighttime anti-submarine warfare training exercise, two MSDF SH-60K patrol helicopters crashed in the ocean east of Torishima Island in the Izu Islands

[13287] A search is underway for the crew on board and the aircraft, and an investigation is underway into the cause of the accident

[13288] In addition, in June 2023, an incident occurred at the Hino Basic Shooting Range (Gifu Prefecture), during a live-fire training for new personnel, in which one SDF cadet fired at three members, resulting in two members being killed in the line of duty

[13289] This incident should never occur in any organization handling weapons, and the MOD/SDF will continue to make every effort to prevent recurrence and thoroughly implement safety management, which includes training the personnel and reviewing the firing procedures

[13290] In this way, any accident and incidents that may cause injury to Japanese nationals, damage their property, or lead to the loss of life of SDF personnel, must be prevented at all costs

[13291] After thoroughly investigating the causes of these accidents and incidents, the MOD/SDF will ensure that each and every member of SDF personnel is reminded of the latest safety management guidelines

[13292] At the same time, the MOD/SDF as a whole will make every effort to ensure safety in the operation of vessels, aircraft, vehicles, etc., through conducting safety education for SDF personnel and the steady maintenance of equipment, etc., so as to ensure that public confidence is not undermined

[13297] Chapter 4 Initiatives to Live in Harmony with Regional Societies and the Environment

[13298] Various activities of the Ministry of Defense and Self-Defense Forces are hard to implement without the understanding and cooperation of each and every person and local governments

[13299] Therefore it is necessary to further deepen the trust between regional society and people, and the SDF

[13300] Section 1 Measures to Harmonize with Local Communities and the Environment

[13301] The National Defense Strategy of Japan provides that in order to enable the SDF and the U.S. Forces in Japan to seamlessly and effectively conduct activities on a daily basis, the MOD will strive to gain understanding and cooperation of local governments and residents in the areas around the SDF and the U.S. Forces facilities

[13302] To this end, the NDS provides that the MOD/SDF will actively engage in public relations activities on a regular basis regarding the policies and activities of the MOD/SDF, and also the roles of the U. S. Forces in Japan on a regular basis, and coordinate to accommodate the requests and situations of local communities, while fulfilling accountability

[13303] At the same time, the MOD/SDF will continue to promote measures to improve the living environment of areas around defense facilities including those against noise to further strengthen the cooperation for the defense of Japan

[13304] Key supporting Civilian Life

[13305] The MOD/SDF conducts activities to support the lives of citizens in a range of fields, in response to requests from local governments and relevant organizations

[13306] Such activities contribute to further deepening the trust in the SDF, and provide SDF personnel with pride and confidence

[13307] The GSDF handles the disposal of unexploded ordnance and other dangerous explosives found throughout Japan

[13308] In FY2023, there were 2,348 cases (approximately 37.5 tons

[13309] In particular, cases handled in Okinawa Prefecture accounted for approximately 19% of the total number of cases

[13310] The MSDF clears and disposes of underwater mines and other dangerous explosives; in FY2023, there were 197 pieces (approximately 4.1 tons) handled

[13311] Furthermore, in some communities, the existence of SDF units themselves are a major contribution to the communities’ maintenance and vitalization, and in other communities, the SDF’s emergency patient transportation support the community healthcare

[13312] In conducting unit reorganization, establishing as well as administering camps and bases, the MOD/SDF will give due consideration to regional characteristics so as to gain understanding of local governments and residents

[13317] In addition, it supports regional medical treatment efforts by providing general medical care at some SDF hospitals1 and National Defense Medical College as well as conducting urgent transport for emergency patients from isolated islands

[13344] Measures to Promote Harmony between Defense Facilities and Surrounding Areas

[13345] Defense facilities are diverse in their use, and often require large volumes of land

[13346] In addition to this, as of January 1, 2024, approximately 29% of the land area and 30 of the 76 facilities and areas (for exclusive use) of the USFJ are jointly used by the SDF in accordance with the Japan–U.S. Status of Forces Agreement, with the purpose of enhancing the diversity and efficiency of Japan–U.S. bilateral training and exercises

[13347] Meanwhile, problems related to restricted establishment and operations of defense facilities have emerged due to the urbanization of areas around many of the defense facilities

[13348] Also, another problem is that frequent aircraft operations such as takeoffs and landings cause noise and other issues, impacting the living environment of local residential communities

[13349] With that being said, defense facilities, as the foundation that supports the defense capabilities of Japan and the Japan-U. S. Security Arrangements, are indispensable for Japan’s national security

[13350] Therefore, in order for the facilities to exert their full function, it is necessary to maintain the conditions for their constant and stable utilization by ensuring harmony between the defense facilities and the surrounding areas and by obtaining the understanding and cooperation of local residents

[13351] For that purpose, the MOD has taken measures to prevent, reduce or mitigate aircraft noise and other impacts caused by activities of the SDF or the USFJ, or by the existence/operations of airfields and other defense facilities in the surrounding areas since 1974 based on the Living Environment Improvement Act, etc

[13352] In addition, in order to relieve the impact caused by the existence and operation of defense facilities, subsidies are provided for the development of facilities for stabilizing the everyday lives of residents while Specified Defense Facilities Environment Improvement Adjustment Grants are given to municipalities around defense facilities that have particularly significant impact on the living environment

[13353] Specified Defense Facilities Environment Improvement Adjustment Grants are utilized not only for the development of facilities but also for so-called “soft projects” such as aid for medical expenses

[13354] In 2023, in order to respond with greater precision to the operational modes of specified defense facilities and their impact on surrounding areas, the criteria for the calculation of Specified Defense Facilities Environment Improvement Adjustment Grants was reviewed and Training Grants for training of the SDF, the U. S. Forces, etc., at defense facilities other than specified defense facilities was established in view of the diversification of training, etc

[13355] In addition, the subsidiary framework has been revised to take into account the actual circumstances of the operation of the SDF, impact on the local area, requests from local communities, etc., by further extending the subsidized projects for the development of facilities for stabilizing the everyday lives of residents based on the requests of local governments, etc

[13356] In response to the requests by the relevant local governments, the MOD continues to study how the measures to harmonize defense facilities and surrounding areas should be in an attempt to make them more suitable, effective and efficient, in consideration of the severe fiscal situation

[13427] Efforts to Develop Understanding and Cooperation Concerning the Stationing of the USFJ

[13428] Amid the increasingly severe security environment surrounding Japan, maintaining the presence of the USF and its readiness is vitally important for ensuring the security of Japan

[13464] Response to Laser Irradiation and Kite Flying towards SDF and U. S. Forces Aircraft

[13465] There have been cases of SDF and U. S. Forces aircraft being interfered by laser irradiation and kite flying during flight operations

[13466] These extremely dangerous and malicious acts could disrupt a pilot’s ability to operate the aircraft, which could result in a catastrophe, such as plane crash

[13467] Therefore, the MOD works closely with relevant local governments to disseminate information to local residents regarding the risks involved in these acts by putting up posters and requesting to report to the police

[13468] Additionally, the Ordinance for Enforcement of the Civil Aeronautics Act was revised in December 2016, making these interference acts subject to regulation as well as fines and other penalties

[13469] Response to Flight Activities over Defense Facilities and Surrounding Airspace, including Small Unmanned Aerial Systems

[13470] In recent years there have been terrorist small drones, including commercial drones, some of which are targeted at military facilities

[13471] Given such circumstances, there is a possibility of drone terror attacks in Japan on SDF/USFJ facilities and areas, which if attacked, would seriously affect the function of the national security defense foundation

[13472] To address such concern, “The Drone Act” came into effect on June 13, 2019, to prohibit small drones from flying over and around SDF/USFJ facilities and areas designated by the Minister of Defense

[13473] As of the end of May 2024, 304 SDF facilities, including areas of SDF Headquarters and 63 USFJ facilities and areas have been designated as No Drone Zone

[13474] Response to the Act on Review and Regulation of Real Estate Usage

[13475] In line with the previous iteration of the National Security Strategy formulated in December 2013, which called for Japan to review issues related to the use of land in areas such as the areas surrounding defense facilities from the standpoint of national security, the MOD has been conducting research since FY2013 to ensure a systematic understanding of the situation of land ownership in areas surrounding defense facilities

[13476] Under the Act on the Review and Regulation of the Use of Real Estate Surrounding Important Facilities and on Remote Territorial Islands, the Cabinet Office designates areas around facilities that are important for national security (“important facilities”) and areas within remote territorial islands as “monitored areas” or “special monitored areas,” and reviews the use of real estate and buildings in these areas

[13477] If the Cabinet Office identifies any acts that impede the functions of important facilities and remote territorial islands (adverse acts), it recommends or orders the real estate user to stop the adverse acts

[13478] So far, zones have been designated four times under the same act

[13479] Regarding defense-related facilities, 13 locations were designated with the initial announcement in December 2022, 48 locations in the second announcement in July 2023, 176 locations in the third announcement in December of the same year, and 157 locations in the fourth announcement in April

[13480] This Act has major significance from the perspective of ensuring that defense-related facilities, which constitute the foundation of Japan’s national defense, are able to function properly

[13481] The MOD will adopt the appropriate measures in this regard in cooperation with the Cabinet Office

[13501] Responding to Climate Change and Environmental Issues A sense of crisis regarding the sustainability of the global environment has been mounting internationally

[13502] Countries around the world have been making efforts on this front following the adoption of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) at the UN and the Paris Agreement, an international framework on climate change, in

[13503] Japan has also formulated the Fifth Basic Environment Plan, which was approved by the Cabinet in 2018, and has been working to realize a sustainable society while expressing its intention to further accelerate initiatives in Japan and abroad

[13504] In addition, the Plan for Global Warming Countermeasures and the Climate Change Adaptation Plan were approved by the Cabinet in October 2021, and specific climate change measures aimed at achieving carbon neutrality by 2050 as well as the targets for FY2030 are underway

[13505] In response to the acceleration of domestic and overseas efforts, the MOD/SDF, as a member of the Government, also needs to respond to various climate change and environmental issues and contribute to their resolution while implementing measures with a greater focus on the coexistence of SDF/USFJ facilities/areas with the surrounding areas

[13506] In addition, it is inevitable that the issue of climate change will have an even greater impact on future MOD/SDF operations, including various plans, facilities, and equipment, as well as on the security environment surrounding Japan, including responses to future energy shifts, all of which must be addressed in an appropriate manner

[13635] The Air Review

[13636] On November 11, 2023, the MOD/SDF held The Air Review 2023, under the review of Prime Minister Kishida, at the ASDF's

[13637] Iruma Air Base (Saitama Prefecture

[13638] The purpose of this Air Review was to raise awareness of the mission and morale of the personnel

[13639] The ceremony was conducted without spectators, with Prime Minister Kishida, the Supreme Commander of the Self-Defense Forces, delivering a speech and inspecting the troops

[13640] In his speech, the Prime Minister greatly boosted the morale of personnel by referring to concrete achievements concerning the transportation of Japanese nationals and others in Israel, such as “The sincere manner in which the personnel performed their duties on board the aircraft and at the transit points, and their meticulous attention to the evacuees, significantly eased the anxiety of the evacuees”

[13649] Democracy, which is the most important system of the country, is founded on the principle that the public has access to accurate information, thereby making appropriate judgment and exercise of sovereignty

[13650] Administrative documents held by the government are of the utmost importance for the public’s access to accurate information

[13651] For this reason it is an important responsibility for the government, including the MOD/SDF, to manage information in an appropriate manner and appropriately respond to the public’s disclosure requests for administrative documents

[13652] Promotion of Proper Management of Public

[13653] Records and Archives and Proper Operation of the Disclosure System of Administrative

[13654] Documents

[13655] The MOD/SDF takes it seriously that the issues over daily reports in South Sudan and Iraq brought about the public’s distrust in the MOD/SDF

[13656] The MOD/SDF is making every effort to prevent recurrence based on measures necessary for the proper management of public records and archives by the entire government

[13657] The MOD/SDF is also working on ensuring proper management and responding to disclosure requests for administrative documents by reforming the awareness of personnel and the organizational culture, enhancing the supervisory framework, etc

[13658] We will promote systematic and efficient management by managing administrative documents electronically, from their creation to storage, disposal, and transfer, facilitating tracking administrative documents, history management, and search

[13659] At the same time, we also promote improvement in the efficiency of document management operations by reducing the use of paper-based administrative documents, contributing to improved work environment and work style reforms such as telework

[13660] “Measures for Ensuring Appropriate Management of Public Records” (adopted by the Ministerial Council on the Management of Administrative Documents and Related Matters on July

[13664] Initiatives for Policy Evaluation, etc. Engagement in Policy Evaluation

[13665] The MOD has been conducting the evaluation of various policies based on its policy evaluation system

[13666] In FY2023, the MOD conducted policy evaluations of research and development (R&D) programs and projects concerning Special Taxation Measures

[13667] Promotion of Evidence-Based Policy Making (EBPM

[13668] The MOD, under the supervision of Director-General for

[13669] Evidence-based Policymaking, practices EBPM through the Administrative Project Review and promotes its initiatives such as in decision-making process

[13670] Initiatives for the Personal Data Protection

[13671] System

[13672] In light of respecting individual rights and interests in line with the Act on the Protection of Personal Information, the MOD/SDF has adopted measures to manage the security of personal information under its control and responds appropriately to requests for the disclosure of such information

[13673] Appropriate Operation of the Whistleblower

[13674] Protection System

[13675] The MOD/SDF sets up a system to handle whistleblowing made by its officials, employees and outside workers, establishing internal and external contact desks to deal with whistleblowing and to protect whistleblowers
